author: copilot
body:
SWR alerts were only timing out when a later transmit path re-entered the monitor logic, and short good-SWR retransmissions could miss the clear path. This change makes alert expiry truly wall-clock based and ensures low-SWR recovery clears the warning reliably.

- **Decouple timeout clearing from transmit activity**
  - Added a dedicated timeout poll in `src/swr_monitor.c` that clears `vswr_tripped` and resets trip time when the configured alert lifetime expires.
  - Exposed the poll helper so it can run from the existing GTK periodic tick, not only from transmit-time SWR measurement paths.

- **Make low-SWR recovery deterministic**
  - Moved SWR handling during TX onto a short periodic interval in `ui_tick()`, instead of relying only on the slower display update cadence.
  - This allows a brief follow-up transmission with recovered SWR to clear the alert consistently.

- **Unify SWR trip reset behavior**
  - Added a shared reset path for `vswr_tripped` and `vswr_trip_time`.
  - Reused it for:
    - timeout expiry
    - under-threshold recovery
    - initialization
    - band-change clearing

- **Refresh overlay when trip state changes**
  - Triggered immediate spectrum/waterfall redraw when `vswr_tripped` changes so the `HIGH VSWR` overlay clears as soon as the state flips.

Example of the new timeout polling path:

```c
poll_vswr_alert_timeout();
if (in_tx && (ticks % vswr_check_tick_interval) == 0)
	check_and_handle_vswr(vswr);

if (last_vswr_tripped != vswr_tripped) {
	update_field(get_field("spectrum"));
	update_field(get_field("waterfall"));
	last_vswr_tripped = vswr_tripped;
}
```

author: atabor89
body:
## What (docs correction)

Fixes a wrong finding from #184. The user clarified:
- **"rogue bonus" meant rogue/unexplained**, not the Rogue class.
- **Only the Adventurer class gives a campaign bonus** — Rogue and the other classes do not, and pets' innate per-campaign bonuses are already in the chamber logic. So the chamber's mystery ×2 is **not** a class bonus.

My #184 wrongly tied it to a "per-class campaign multiplier" in `CIEAPBPBCLL.KEPCFJNJDPJ`/`NOAKCBPMNDD`. Re-reading the method: it's a **dungeon** calc — it switches on the pet's *element* and combines elemental stats, and the Rogue branch is its **dungeon-loot** bonus (matching the Rogue tooltip). Not a campaign reward. That lead is disregarded.

The chamber sim's ×2 is back to genuinely unidentified — most likely a **global** campaign-XP multiplier (a 2nd upgrade / research / god / Patreon perk, or the wiki `250` base being outdated). The clean way to resolve it: back-solve from the in-game per-cycle Adventurer class-XP at a known growth + hours.

## Scope
`decode_roadmap.md` only. Self-correcting the record so the false assumption doesn't propagate — which is the whole point of this exercise.

author: bsletten
body:
The golden thread, end to end in the CLI — file reads now cache and invalidate on write.

- **ikigai-core `0.1.7 → 0.1.9`** (`depends_on` + the `Sink` auto-cut).
- **ikigai-fs** path dep (→ `0.1.2` once published): the local file space mounts in `FileEndpoint::cacheable()` mode.
- **ikigai-resolve**: cache status now comes from a pre-issue `is_cached` probe, not a cache-length delta — the delta misreports once golden-thread eviction (evict + reinsert nets zero) is in play. Engine cache-status tests unchanged (63 pass).

**Live in the REPL:**
```
source urn:file:notes.txt   [computed]
source urn:file:notes.txt   [cached]      ← file reads cache now (were always uncacheable)
sink   urn:file:notes.txt …  (auto-cuts the thread)
source urn:file:notes.txt   [computed]    ← the write invalidated it; returns the new value
source urn:file:notes.txt   [cached]
```

**⚠️ Draft until `ikigai-fs 0.1.2` is published** — it's a path dep here, which CI can't resolve. After publish: switch to `ikigai-fs = "0.1.2"`, un-draft. (Caveat: cacheable workspace files don't see out-of-band editor edits until the file watcher lands — that's the next step.)

author: anneoneone
body:
## What

Adds a step to the `deploy-hetzner` job that ships `docs/stream-rework/prod/moafunk.liq` to the box and restarts Liquidsoap **only when the file changed**.

## Why

Verified after #227 merged: the public mount **stayed at 128 kb/s** even though the 256k change deployed. Root cause — `moafunk.liq` is **bind-mounted** into the host's `liquidsoap` container (`/etc/moafunk/moafunk.liq`, see `liquidsoap.service`); it's not in the backend image and was in **no** pipeline. `sync-scripts` only pushes `backend/scripts/*` to Lightsail. So repo edits to the encoder silently never reached production:

```
$ ffprobe https://admin.live.moafunk.de/live.mp3
  Audio: mp3, 44100 Hz, stereo, 128 kb/s        # ← still old, post-#227
```

## How

New step (icecast mode only — i.e. every push to main):
- `scp` the repo's `moafunk.liq` → `/tmp/moafunk.liq.new` on the box.
- `cmp` against `/etc/moafunk/moafunk.liq`; **unchanged → skip** (no restart, no stream gap).
- changed → `install` + `systemctl restart liquidsoap`, then assert the service is active (fail the job with `systemctl status` on error).

Safety: the deploy step already restarts `unheard-api` and drops any in-progress broadcast WS, so a same-deploy Liquidsoap restart adds **no new** live-show hazard. The change-gating means routine backend pushes (config unchanged) never touch Liquidsoap.

## Effect of merging

Merging this is itself a push to main → `deploy-hetzner` runs → syncs the already-256k `moafunk.liq` and restarts Liquidsoap → **the public mount becomes 256k with no manual step.**

## Validation

- `backend.yml` parses (`yaml.safe_load`); heredoc de-indents correctly (closing delimiter at col 0 after YAML strips block indent).
- Post-merge check: re-probe `https://admin.live.moafunk.de/live.mp3` → expect `256 kb/s`.

author: eilandert
body:
Second static deobfuscation layer beside the base64/hex/reverse decoders (PR-11 of the maldoc-deepening plan). Evaluates fully-literal VBA/VBScript string-building expressions so a keyword/URL/IOC split across constants surfaces to the maldoc rules.

## Folds (single-layer, FP-safe — every operand a literal present in source; no interpreter, no control flow, no dataflow, depth cap 1)
- Concatenation chains: `"po" & Chr(119) & "ershell"` (Chr/ChrW/ChrB, decimal or &H)
- Literal `Replace("expr","find","with")`
- `Array(n,n,...)` byte lists, plus a single-byte-XOR variant per literal `Xor` key present (trivial in-loop decoder pattern, applied once)

## Bounds
1 MiB input gate, per-kind match cap (256), output bounded by the existing global emit caps. Wired into `fromEncoded` after `emitReversed`; `extract.Version` bumped (`+vbafold`) to invalidate cached verdicts.

## Tests
Each transform, an XOR-keyed array, hex Chr arg, a benign no-op, an expired deadline. `gofmt`/`go vet`/`go test ./internal/extract` clean in golang:1.25.

author: emilioheredia-source
body:
### Problem

An FTP/SFTP tab left open for a long time stops working and never
reconnects. The user has to close the tab, open a new one, reconnect, and
navigate back to where they were.

Three issues combine to cause this:

1. **SSH connections got no TCP keep-alive at all.** `TScpSend.Connect`
   overrides `Connect` and never runs `TFTPSendEx.Connect`, which was the only
   place `SO_KEEPALIVE` was applied. So SSH/SFTP sockets had zero keep-alive and
   idle links were silently dropped by NAT/firewall timeouts.
2. **`TScpSend.NetworkError` almost never fired.** It required
   `CanRead(0)` **and** `last_errno <> 0`. When a server closes an idle session
   the socket becomes readable but libssh2's `last_errno` is still `0`, so the
   link was reported healthy and the next operation just failed with no
   reconnect attempt.
3. On a detected error the code only re-logged-in on the dead session object.

### Changes

- Factor keep-alive into `TFTPSendEx.ApplyKeepAlive` and apply it to **both**
  the FTP control socket and the SSH socket. On Unix it additionally tunes
  `TCP_KEEPIDLE`/`TCP_KEEPINTVL`/`TCP_KEEPCNT` (30/10/3) so idle connections are
  probed within ~1 minute instead of the OS default (~2 h): this keeps NAT
  mappings open and detects dead peers quickly. Gated by the existing
  `[General] TcpKeepAlive` option (default on), same as before.
- `TScpSend.NetworkError` now treats **either** condition (libssh2 error set, or
  an unexpectedly readable idle socket) as a dead link.
- On a dead link `FtpConnect` discards the stale connection and reconnects
  fresh, reusing the cached password when available or prompting again when not.
  A plain refresh of the view then reconnects and re-lists the folder currently
  shown in the tab. Quick connections (no stored entry) report
  "unable to reconnect" as before.

### Notes

- The aggressive per-socket idle tuning is `{$IFDEF UNIX}`; on Windows the plain
  `SO_KEEPALIVE` is still applied (system-default idle time). The reconnect
  logic is fully platform-independent.
- Built and tested on Linux (native + glibc-2.10 compat).

author: bowlesb
body:
Completes Ben's sector ask (the sector half): "whether different sectors are up/down, and how closely a given ticker aligns with its sector." Unblocked by the live `sector_map` (#181, 4980 rows / 11 GICS sectors).

## What

Two new universe-wide GATHER feature groups (+14 features, 694 → **708**):

**`sector_return` (8 feats)** — is the sector up/down + within-sector excess:
- `sector_return_{5,15,30,60}m` — equal-weight mean trailing-W return of THIS ticker's GICS sector (each name gets ITS sector's aggregate)
- `sector_excess_{5,15,30,60}m` — own trailing-W return minus its sector aggregate (within-sector excess)

**`sector_beta` (6 feats)** — how closely the ticker tracks its sector (the sector analogue of `market_beta`, regressor = the ticker's OWN sector aggregate, not SPY):
- `sector_beta_{15,30,60}m` — rolling OLS slope of own 1m return on its sector's 1m aggregate return
- `sector_corr_{15,30,60}m` — rolling correlation of the two

## Design (mirrors the templates)

- **Both are REDUCE_GROUPS** — a per-(minute, sector) universe gather broadcast back by sector, run once in the reader's gather phase (the `breadth` mechanism). Parity-true by construction; `single == sharded` proven by the new `test_sector_aggregates_via_reduce_identical`.
- **Unknown-sector (~27% unmapped) → NULL** — no peer group to aggregate, not a synthetic "unknown sector" mean.
- **The OLS `sector_beta` is a PLAIN `FeatureGroup`** (rolling power sums via `rolling_sum_by`), deliberately NOT a `ReductionGroup`/`StatefulRegressor` — it **never rides the incremental fast-path** (the #180 correlation-family lesson). Verified: neither group is a ReductionGroup or declares stateful_regressors.
- **Namespaced output** (`sector_return_`/`sector_excess_`/`sector_beta_`/`sector_corr_`); 708 globally-unique feature names, **no collision**. (No #161-class reduce-key collision: these aren't ReductionGroups, so there's no shared paired-column namespace — each `compute()` keeps its internal cols private and drops them before output.)

## Tests / verification

- Unit: sector-aggregate math, sole-member `beta==1`/`corr==1`, fixed-multiple beta recovery, **unknown-sector NULL**, `compute_latest == compute` parity, `single == sharded` reduce parity.
- Full fp suite green: `test_fp_sector_return`, `test_fp_sector_beta`, `test_fp_sharding`, `test_fp_latest`, `test_fp_platform`, `test_fp_new_families`, `test_fp_latency` (104+ passed).
- **RT-cost GREEN**: `sector_return` 2.2k us/feat (17.6ms), `sector_beta` 14.1k us/feat (84.6ms) — under the 60k us/feat ceiling; `sector_beta` is cheaper than its sibling `market_beta` (17.7k).
- `docs/FEATURES.md` regenerated from the registry (708 features).

## ⚠️ fingerprint-affecting → STAGE only

- Feature count 694 → **708**; bus fingerprint `0xae849d400c909972` → `0x13e7a10b1ee18d18`.
- **Combine with #168 + #177 + #179 in the next coordinated deploy; the Lead recomputes the MERGED fingerprint.**
- **NOT deployed / relaunched / fingerprint-flipped.**

author: attacktive
body:
The auto-update toggle could turn itself off. Its on/off state lived only in the in-memory `ServiceState.isRunning` singleton, so an OS process kill reset it to `false` and resuming relied entirely on `START_STICKY`'s restart — which One UI does not reliably honor. The service stayed dead and the toggle showed off until the user tapped Start again.

This persists the intent to DataStore (`auto_update_enabled`): `true` when the timer loop starts, `false` on an explicit Stop. On Home `ViewModel` creation it reconciles the in-memory flag from the persisted intent and revives the service when it should be running — the screen is foregrounded then, so the foreground-service start is allowed.

**Trade-off / known limitation:** reconciliation runs on `ViewModel` creation (a fresh open), not on a warm resume where the `ViewModel` already exists. On an existing install the flag isn't persisted until the loop runs once after updating. In both cases the worst case is simply the previous behavior, not a regression.

author: ljesparis
body:
## Resumen

Migra el template estático "Leonardo Esparis" (export de Claude Design) a **Astro limpio y componentizado**, manteniendo el **diseño visual exacto**: portfolio dark estilo terminal (fondo `#04070a`, acento verde `#3fe08f`, scanlines, glow animado, cursor parpadeante, fuentes Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono).

## Decisiones (acordadas)
- **Bilingüe EN/ES** mantenido (badge conectado al selector real, prosa traducida, hreflang).
- **Proyectos + Writing**: componentes construidos pero **comentados** en `HomeContent` hasta que haya contenido real (datos listos en los diccionarios).
- **Bio**: la del diseño ("últimos 4 años…").

## Arquitectura
- **Componentes**: `BaseLayout` (shell + efectos scanline/glow), `SiteNav`, `Hero`, `About`, `Projects`, `Writing`, `Footer`; contenido compuesto en `HomeContent` por idioma. Eliminados componentes huérfanos (`Header`, `Link`, `FormattedDate`).
- **CSS moderno**: tokens como **CSS custom properties** (colores/espaciado/tipografía/radios), **`clamp()`** para el nombre fluido, **flexbox**; **scoped styles** por componente y `global.css` solo con reset + tokens + keyframes.
- **Fuentes self-host** con `@fontsource` (sin requests externas → mejor Lighthouse); solo se sirve el woff2 que usa la página.
- **Rendimiento**: 0 frameworks JS (solo el prefetch de Astro, ~2 KB); assets `_astro` ≈ 160 KB (incluye woff2). No hay imágenes raster, así que `<Image>` de `astro:assets` no aplica (todo son SVG inline + efectos CSS).
- **Accesibilidad**: landmarks/headings semánticos, `aria-label` en iconos y nav, `:focus-visible`, guard `prefers-reduced-motion`, `color-scheme`/`theme-color` dark.
- Nueva **imagen OG** acorde al tema oscuro.

## Anti-patrones del template corregidos (y por qué)
- **`style-hover="…"`** → no es un atributo válido, los hover **nunca funcionaban**; reemplazado por `:hover` real.
- **Estilos inline por todas partes** → clases + tokens (mantenible, reutilizable).
- **`href="#"` muertos** → enlaces reales (LinkedIn/GitHub y selector de idioma).
- **Google Fonts por `<link>`** (request externa, bloquea render) → self-host con `@fontsource`.
- **Colores/fuentes repetidos** literalmente → variables CSS.
- `min-height:100vh` → `100svh` para móvil.

## Verificación
- `npm run build` limpio; 2 páginas (`/`, `/es/`).
- Output: efectos scanline/glow, nav `root@ljesparis:~$`, hero `Leonardo/Esparis`, about (EN/ES), footer con año dinámico + corazón; badge de idioma `EN`→`/es/` y `ES`→`/`; `html lang` correcto; fuentes woff2 self-host; `color-scheme: dark`.
- Proyectos/Writing no se renderizan (comentados) ✓.

## Nota honesta (accesibilidad vs. fidelidad)
Mantuve los colores **exactos** del diseño. Algunos textos meta muy tenues (mono `#4f7d63`, footer `#3c6650` sobre `#04070a`) quedan por debajo de AA de contraste. Prioricé "diseño visual exacto"; si quieres, subo ligeramente esos dos tonos para cumplir AA sin alterar la estética.

⚠️ No pude renderizar/capturar en el entorno (sin navegador headless); recomiendo una revisión visual con `npm run dev`.

author: choijunhuk
body:
## Summary
- Adds a workflow-level `concurrency` block (`group: deploy-${{ github.workflow }}`, `cancel-in-progress: false`) after the `on:` block and before `jobs:`
- Prevents concurrent Gradle test/build runs on the shared self-hosted runner that caused `NoSuchFileException .../in-progress-results.bin` failures on rapid successive merges
- `cancel-in-progress: false` ensures queued deploys run sequentially and Flyway migrations are never interrupted mid-flight

## Cross-repo runner limitation note
GitHub `concurrency` groups are scoped **per-repository**. These 5 repos share one self-hosted runner, but GitHub has no mechanism to serialize across repos via `concurrency`. This change serializes runs *within* each repo. If two different repos push simultaneously, their workflows can still run concurrently on the shared runner. The practical impact is reduced because most rapid pushes happen within one repo; cross-repo parallelism is less common and the runner's own queue will throttle naturally.

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify YAML parses cleanly (`python3 -c "import yaml;yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/deploy.yml'))"` → no error)
- [ ] Merge two quick commits to main and confirm the second workflow run shows "Waiting for concurrency group" in Actions UI

author: mgomezdev
body:
## Summary

- Gridfinity bins are generated with `position=\"center\"` (the OpenSCAD library default), so each STL mesh is **centred at its local XY origin** — a 42mm bin occupies `-21..+21`, not `0..42`.
- `autoarrange_plates` returns left/front **edge** coordinates, so without correction every bin was shifted half its width/depth to the left and front, placing items partially or fully outside the plate boundary.
- Fix: add `width_mm / 2` and `depth_mm / 2` to the 3MF `<item>` transform so the mesh centre lands at the correct plate position.
- Same correction applied to the thumbnail vertex offset so the 3D perspective render matches actual placement.
- `_make_box_mesh` in tests updated to use centred vertices, mirroring real STL behaviour.

author: kylephillipsau
body:
Five coherent commits, all verified on the staging dev image.

## Bug fixes
- **CSRF on admin email calls** — `EmailSettingsView` used bare `axios`, so the test-send/config calls carried no `X-CSRF-Token` and were rejected. Route them through the shared `apiClient`.
- **Email-auth DNS resolver** — the DKIM verifier + DNS panel hardcoded `8.8.8.8` over UDP, unreachable on Fly ("no connections available"), which also broke the periodic re-verify job. Use the host's system resolver, and DRY the two duplicated builders into one shared `email_auth_resolver()`.
- **Self-host fallback** — the queue's `resolve_batch` never fell back to the env identity (correct on hosted, anti-phishing), but on self-host it stranded the operator's notification mail. Inject deployment mode and gate the fallback: self-host falls back to its own env identity, hosted still defers. New test covers it.

## Hosted-awareness
- **Redact platform SMTP** — `get_email_config` returned `smtp_username` (the SES IAM key on hosted). Drop it entirely; on hosted return only the managed status + From. Expose `deployment_mode` on `GET /api/config`. The email view shows an "outbound delivered by Nosdesk" managed note on hosted, the operator's relay (no username) on self-host.

## Admin consolidation
- Replace the five scattered email surfaces (across Integrations + Appearance) with a single **Communication** group: **Channels** (inbound) and **Email delivery** (outbound). author: rankaiyx
body:
## Description

When a user interrupts agent generation (stop button), AgentScope `ReActAgent._reasoning` writes an empty message (`content=[]`) to memory via its `finally` block. On the next turn, the predictor (blacklist logic) assumed empty messages **survive** the base formatter, but AgentScope's `OpenAIChatFormatter` actually **drops** them — causing an assistant message count mismatch and skipping `reasoning_content` injection for the entire turn.

**Result:** ALL historical thinking content is lost → KV cache miss → latency spike.

### Root Cause

The predictor and base formatter use opposite approaches to decide which assistant messages survive formatting:

| Approach | Predictor (before) | Base Formatter (AgentScope) |
|---|---|---|
| Logic | Blacklist: known-dropped `{thinking, file}` | Whitelist: known-surviving `{text, tool_use, image}` |
| Empty `[]` | **Survives** (falsy short-circuit) | **Dropped** |
| `audio` (assistant) | **Survives** | **Dropped** |
| Unknown types | **Survives** | **Dropped** |

The blacklist approach is fragile — every new block type added by AgentScope that isn't in the blacklist causes silent misalignment, leading to reasoning content being injected into the wrong messages.

**Prior fix (#1557 for #1532):** Added `is_thinking_only` prediction to skip thinking-only messages, but the blacklist (`_FORMATTER_SKIPPED_TYPES`) still misses empty content (`[]` — falsy short-circuit), `audio` on assistant, and non-standard block types like `reasoning` (#5208). This PR completes the fix by inverting to a whitelist approach.

### Fix

Invert the predictor from blacklist to whitelist:

- `_FORMATTER_SKIPPED_TYPES` → `_FORMATTER_SURVIVING_TYPES`
- `all(b in SKIPPED)` → `all(b not in SURVIVING)`
- Empty content is now correctly predicted as dropped (`all([])` = `True`)

This is **fail-safe**: if AgentScope adds support for a new block type, the whitelist triggers a mismatch warning and skips reasoning injection safely, while the blacklist would silently misalign (wrong reasoning injected into subsequent messages).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit run --files src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py` passes
- [x] black: Passed
- [x] flake8: Passed
- [x] mypy: Passed
- [x] pylint: Passed
- [ ] Documentation updated (N/A — internal logic change)

## Local Verification

Re-entered a session containing `content: []` messages (from interrupted generation):

- **Before fix:** formatted messages missing all `reasoning_content`; log shows `Assistant message count mismatch` warning
- **After fix:** `reasoning_content` injected correctly, no mismatch warning

The verification operation is performed and confirmed by  human (rankaiyx). 

## Note on Reproducibility

Naturally triggering the creation of a session containing `content: []` empty messages requires interrupting agent generation before the first streaming token arrives — the timing window is extremely narrow and depends on model latency, making it difficult to reproduce reliably.

author: love-lena
body:
Two pure consolidation/encapsulation seams from the deep-modules assessment, in one PR per the fold-in-over-extra-PR norm. **Zero observable behaviour change** — the proof is that the existing mcp/violet/attest resume tests pass against the shared module (AC#3).

> **Review flag (house style — new exported surface):** this introduces two new exported types/APIs that need a sign-off look: the **`seqcursor.Store`** module surface (app-internal, under `clients/go/apps/internal/`) and the SDK's **`sextant.PublishResult`** value type. Both are deliberate; details below.

## Part A — one shared cursor-store module

**New module:** `clients/go/apps/internal/seqcursor` (stdlib-only — `encoding/json`, `os`, `path/filepath`, `strings`; pulls in no SDK/bus/NATS/wireapi, so it widens no existing importcheck closure). It owns the genuinely-shared primitive the three sites triplicated: a durable, monotonic, per-subject `map[string]uint64` cursor, JSON-enveloped as `{"next":{...}}`, written atomically (temp + `os.Rename`, 0600, mkdir-on-first-use), degrading silently to empty on a missing/corrupt file or empty path.

**Interface (caller-owns-locking — the Store carries no mutex of its own):**
```go
func Open(path string) (*Store, error)                  // missing/corrupt → empty; "" → in-memory (Save no-ops)
func (s *Store) Since(subject string) uint64            // 0 if untracked
func (s *Store) Advance(subject string, next uint64) (changed bool)  // monotonic; reports change
func (s *Store) Retain(keep ...string) (changed bool)   // load-time security filter (drop foreign subjects)
func (s *Store) Save() error                            // atomic temp+rename; no-op when path==""
func Sanitize(key string) string                        // filename-safe token (replaces 2 verbatim copies)
func Path(dataDir, subdir, key string) string           // canonical session-keyed path; "" → in-memory
```
Surface kept minimal: I dropped the spec's proposed `Set`/`Track`/`Forget`/`Subjects`/`Tracked` because their only candidate caller (substate) keeps its own richer map (see below) and would not use them — "abstract only against a second implementation."

**How each site delegates (keeping its site-specific shell):**
- **attest `Cursor`** (`mcp/attest/cursor.go`) — fully delegates: now a thin shell holding a `*seqcursor.Store`; `LoadCursor`/`Since`/`Advance`/`Save` route straight through, keying via `seqcursor.Path(dataDir,"attest-cursor",sid)`. `attest/identity.go`'s duplicated `sanitize` now calls `seqcursor.Sanitize` too (its `filepath.Join` keying is untouched, so the identity-file path is byte-identical).
- **violet `ackStore`** (`violet/internal/violet/ack.go`) — fully delegates: embeds `*seqcursor.Store`, keeps its `mu` + locked-in `subject` + per-frame synchronous save. `readFrom`→`Since`, `advance`→`Advance`+`Save`, `alreadyAnswered`→`Since`, the load-time foreign-subject filter (criterion 1)→`Retain` at construction.
- **MCP `substate`** (`mcp/substate.go`) — shares the **keying only** (`seqcursor.Path`, dropping the duplicated `sanitizeSession`). Its on-disk doc is a superset (`{context, subjects:{seq,deliver}}`) and its `subjectCursor{Seq,Deliver}` shape + first-prime write-through are test-visible, so it keeps its own combined-doc writer (spec Q1 realization (a) — the one that keeps `substate_test.go`/`restore_test.go` green unchanged). It still imports `seqcursor`, so the delegation rule (C.1) bites.

**Resume tests pass unchanged**, except two white-box constructions that reached a field now inside the Store — rewritten to drive the *same behaviour* through the constructor (behaviour-preserving, not a behaviour change):
- `attest/cursor_test.go` `TestCursorNeverRewinds`: `&Cursor{path:,Next:}` → `LoadCursor(t.TempDir(), sessionA)` (the test never saves; in-memory monotonic behaviour is identical).
- `violet/.../ac8_test.go` `TestAC8AckStoreSubjectScoping`: the old test hand-built `&ackStore{next:{own,foreign}}`; the foreign subject is now dropped at *load* via `Retain`, so the test seeds an on-disk file with both subjects, loads via `newAckStore`, and asserts the foreign one is dropped and never persists — a stronger, production-faithful test of the same criterion-1 guarantee.

New core tests: `seqcursor_test.go` (round-trip, monotonic no-op, Retain drop, missing/corrupt degrade, in-memory, Sanitize table, Path empties, atomic-write whole-file).

## Part B — the SDK `wireapi` public-boundary leak

`PublishMsg` returned `protocol/wireapi.PublishOutput` across the public boundary. Replaced with an SDK-owned exported value type:
```go
type PublishResult struct { ID string; Seq uint64 }
func (c *Client) PublishMsg(...) (PublishResult, error)  // maps wireapi.PublishOutput → PublishResult inside the SDK
```
This is the established SDK pattern (`wireapi.ArtifactGetOutput → Artifact`, `wireapi.ClientEntry → ClientInfo`). `wireapi` stays imported *inside* the SDK (its sanctioned home); it just stops appearing in an exported signature.

**Callers updated** — all read `.ID` (or discard the result), unchanged off `PublishResult`: `mcp/handlers.go`, `workflow/main.go`, `violet/.../adapter.go` (maps to violet's own `publishResult` adapter type — left intact, it's a fake-able interface boundary), `violet/.../replies.go` (discards). The `conv/goals` `goalsOps` adapter (landed by #173) uses the void-returning `Publish`, **not** `PublishMsg`, so it needed no change.

**Dash e2e caveat (spec B.3):** `dash/e2e_test.go` was the one non-SDK `wireapi` importer in `clients/` (a `_test.go` building a wedged-bus harness — invisible to importcheck's prod-closure `Closure()`, but caught by the grep). Inlined `wireapi.CallSubject(id, OpClientsHello)` to the literal `"sx.api."+id+".clients.hello"` (a deliberately-malformed harness should not depend on the production wire binding) and dropped the import. After this, `grep -rn 'protocol/wireapi' clients/go/apps clients/go/conventions` returns nothing (prod **and** test).

## Part C — importcheck rules + bite-witnesses

Two rules in `internal/importcheck/importcheck.go`, each with a self-test that pins the predicate to real code (so it can't go vacuously green):
- `AssertUsesSeqCursor` + `TestCursorSitesDelegate` (the three sites must reach `seqcursor`).
- `AssertNoWireAtom` + `TestAppsNoWireAtom` (no clients/ package outside the SDK imports the wire atom; the bus is out of subject by construction) + `TestWireAtomRuleBites` vacuity guard (mirrors `TestNewEdgesBite`: proves the SDK's closure really holds the `wireAtom` edge, so the rule has a real shape to catch).

**Bite-verification (inject → fail → revert), both confirmed on the live tree:**

1. **Rule 1 (`AssertUsesSeqCursor`):** reverted attest to a private in-memory cursor (and inlined `sanitize` in identity.go so the package dropped all seqcursor edges). `TestCursorSitesDelegate/.../attest` **FAILED** —
   `…/clients/go/apps/mcp/attest: production closure does not reach …/seqcursor; the durable per-subject cursor is the shared module's, not a re-declaration`
   — while the mcp + violet sub-tests stayed green. Reverted → green.

2. **Rule 2 (`AssertNoWireAtom`):** injected `_ "…/protocol/wireapi"` into `mcp/handlers.go`. `TestAppsNoWireAtom/.../mcp` **FAILED** —
   `…/clients/go/apps/mcp: …/clients/go/apps/mcp imports …/protocol/wireapi directly; the wire atom is the SDK's alone`
   — while the other five app packages stayed green. Reverted → green.

> Honest note on Rule 1's reach: for attest the seqcursor edge also exists via `identity.go`'s `Sanitize` use, so "closure reaches seqcursor" is a *necessary proxy* for "delegates the cursor" rather than airtight for that one package (importcheck is an import-closure tool — it can't assert "this specific symbol is used"). For mcp and violet the edge is the cursor itself. The bite above removed *all* seqcursor edges from attest to demonstrate the mechanism fires.

## AC checklist
- **#1** ✅ `seqcursor.Store` owns the monotonic/atomic/idempot

author: send
body:
## Summary

Implements HTML §4.10.5.1.14 **Color state** value sanitization ("update a color well control color" → "serialize a color well control color"), default **Limited-sRGB-opaque** path. Closes the `#11-input-color-well-sanitize` defer slot (`Color` was the no-op `=> None` arm in the `sanitize_value` chokepoint).

A fresh `<input type=color>` now correctly settles to `#000000` (spec: *"there is always a CSS color picked … no way to set the value to the empty string"*) instead of leaking an empty/invalid value via the `value` IDL getter and form submission. Any CSS `<color>` form is accepted (`red` / `#f00` / `rgb()` / `hsl()` / `transparent`) and canonicalized to opaque `#rrggbb` lowercase.

## Two commits

1. **`refactor(css)`** — relocate the CSS color parser (148 named colors + hex/rgb/hsl/transparent) from `elidex-css::color` into **`elidex-plugin`**, co-located with the `CssColor` type it produces. `elidex-css` re-exports `parse_color` so all existing `elidex_css::parse_color` callers stay unchanged. Adds `CssColor::parse_str(&str) -> Option<CssColor>` (whole-string parse + exhaustion check). Gives engine-independent `elidex-form` (which deps `elidex-plugin`, not `elidex-css`) a shared color-parse home — one home for CSS + form, no `form→CSS-engine` dependency, no duplicate parser. Pure refactor, behavior-neutral.
2. **`feat(form)`** — the `<input type=color>` `Color` sanitization arm: parse → opaque black on failure → force opaque → `#rrggbb` lowercase via `CssColor`'s opaque `Display` branch.

## Design notes

- **Dirty-value-flag source (B2, interop-faithful)**: spec step 2.1 sources the `value` *content attribute* when the dirty flag is set, but combined with the value-mode IDL setter (which sets dirty *before* sanitizing, §4.10.5.4) the literal text would make `input.value = "#ff0000"` serialize to `#000000`, breaking the universal `value` round-trip every browser preserves (no engine ships the content-attr branch — it's a 2024 color-well artifact). This engine sanitizes the **live value** at every establishment site; keeps the single pure chokepoint (no content-attr seam, no new reconciler arm). Documented in-code with a re-evaluation trigger.
- **Deferred** to new slot `#11-color-well-alpha-colorspace`: `alpha` (alpha channel + `color()` form), `colorspace=display-p3`, and exact toward-+∞ component rounding — all need the (absent) CSS Color 4 float pipeline. Default path is exact for integer/hex/named inputs; fractional sRGB rounds to nearest (≤1-LSB), folded into that carve.

## Testing

- `mise run ci` green (check + clippy + fmt + 11,941 tests + doc-tests + deny).
- New: `CssColor::parse_str` exhaustion tests; `elidex-form` color sanitize tests (canonicalization, invalid→`#000000`, force-opaque, `input.value="#ff0000"` round-trip).
- Pre-impl `/elidex-plan-review` (5-agent) + post-impl design review (code-review + 5 elidex axes): 0 actionable findings.

body:
## Resumen

Cierra **HU-04.6 (IUDCYGI-30)**. El agente puede tomar notas durante/después de la llamada en el detalle del cliente; el editor guarda automáticamente cada 5 segundos sin parpadeos, con indicador visible "Guardando…" / "Guardado HH:MM" / "Error al guardar".

## Cambios

### Backend
- `note/` paquete completo: `Note` entity → `notes` table, `NoteRepository`, `NoteRequest` (alta), `NoteUpdateRequest` (PUT), `NoteResponse`, `NoteService`, `NoteController`.
- Endpoints:
  - `GET /api/v1/notes?clientId=...` → lista ordenada por `updated_at DESC`.
  - `POST /api/v1/notes` → 201, autor resuelto desde el JWT subject (username → user_id).
  - `PUT /api/v1/notes/{id}` → 200 / 404.
- `NoteEndpointIT`: 3 specs — roundtrip create→list→update, 401 sin Bearer, 404 al actualizar id inexistente.

### Frontend
- `src/hooks/useAutosave.ts` — hook genérico con baseline en primer render, debounce, status `idle | saving | saved | error`, `lastSavedAt`, soporta `disabled` para no disparar saves mientras se carga la nota inicial.
- `src/api/notes.ts` — fetchers tipados.
- `src/components/notes/NotesPanel.tsx`:
  - Carga la nota más reciente del cliente al montar.
  - Textarea con `aria-label`.
  - Status badge con iconos contextuales (`Loader2`, `CheckCircle2`, `TriangleAlert`, `CircleDashed`).
  - Convierte alta de nota nueva (POST) y edición (PUT) según haya nota previa.
- `ClientDetailPage` reemplaza el placeholder por `<NotesPanel clientId={...} />`.

### Tests Vitest
- `useAutosave.test.ts` (5 nuevos): baseline en primer render no guarda, dispara onSave tras delay, debounce con cambios encadenados, estado error cuando onSave rechaza, respeta `disabled`.

## Commits

```
cab6731 feat(crm): NotesPanel con autosave 5s + hook useAutosave [IUDCYGI-30] · Joaquín
30c728a feat(api): notas CRUD por cliente (POST/PUT/GET /api/v1/notes) [IUDCYGI-30] · Joaquín
```

## Test plan

- [x] `mvn test-compile` OK.
- [x] `npm run lint` clean.
- [x] `npm test` → **31/31 verde** (5 nuevos en useAutosave).
- [x] `npm run build` OK.
- [ ] CI verde.

## Decisiones

- **Una sola nota "activa" por cliente** en este PR — el agente edita la última nota o crea una nueva si no hay ninguna. El modelo permite múltiples notas por cliente (cdr_id puede usarse para asociar a una llamada concreta en S4/S5), pero la UI simple cubre el DoD.
- **Autor resuelto en backend** desde el JWT, no en frontend — evita que el cliente mienta sobre la autoría.
- **Trim antes de guardar** + skip notas vacías — no contamina la BD con notas en blanco mientras el agente piensa.
- **`disabled` en useAutosave** mientras `loaded === false` — evita un save fantasma con el body cargado.

## Pendiente / Conocido

- Capturas del autosave para `docs/evidencias/HU-04.6/` — en el demo intermedio.
- Asociación nota↔CDR (`cdrId`) ya está modelada pero no expuesta en UI; la usaremos cuando el panel CDR ofrezca "agregar nota a esta llamada" (HU futura, fuera del scope S3).

body:
Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/64014

`stream/iter`'s `pipeTo()` already checks the abort signal after receiving
source batches, but the no-transform path did not observe aborts while waiting
for the next source chunk.

This updates that path to use the existing abort-aware iterator wrapper so
`pipeTo()` rejects promptly when the signal aborts, even if the source
`next()` call is still pending.

## Cross-repo runner limitation note
GitHub `concurrency` groups are scoped **per-repository**. These 5 repos share one self-hosted runner, but GitHub has no mechanism to serialize across repos via `concurrency`. This change serializes runs *within* each repo. Cross-repo parallelism remains possible but is less common in practice.

author: kayrozen
body:
## Problem

Phase D station rotation finally fires, but the first MP3→AAC switch (30 s in) aborts the HTTPS stream. This surfaced as the "AAC overflow" in logs 41/42, but it was never a heap overflow — it was a two-stage TLS failure.

**Stage 1 (already fixed on `main`):** ESP-IDF v5.3.1 added a strict guard in `esp_mbedtls_set_client_config()` that rejects any TLS connection with no cert-verification option set. ADF v2.8's `http_stream.c` predates this and never sets `crt_bundle_attach`, so every `https://` URL failed immediately with `0x8017`. Cleared by `CONFIG_ESP_TLS_SKIP_SERVER_CERT_VERIFY`.

**Stage 2 (this PR):** With verification skipped, TLS advanced one step further and failed in `mbedtls_ssl_setup()`:

```
E esp-tls-mbedtls: mbedtls_ssl_setup returned -0x7F00
I esp-tls-mbedtls: SSL - Memory allocation failed
```

`-0x7F00` = `MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_ALLOC_FAILED`. `ssl_setup()` allocates the TLS record I/O buffers (default 16 KB in + 16 KB out = **32 KB**) from **internal DRAM**, where our streaming-phase min-ever is ~7 KB. The allocation fails and the stream aborts on open (`Empty aac file`, then the BT underflow flood).

## Fix

`CONFIG_MBEDTLS_EXTERNAL_MEM_ALLOC=y` routes all mbedTLS allocations to **PSRAM** (~3.7 MB free) instead of internal DRAM. The 32 KB of TLS buffers are not DMA buffers, so PSRAM is a valid home for them. This is the IDF-recommended configuration for TLS on PSRAM-equipped boards with tight internal DRAM. Requires `CONFIG_SPIRAM_USE_MALLOC=y`, already set.

## Scope

One config line (plus rationale comment) in `sdkconfig.defaults`. Plaintext-HTTP MP3 is unaffected.

## Verification

Flash the resulting build and watch the MP3→AAC switch at the 30 s mark: the TLS handshake should now complete and report `Stream info — codec:2` (AAC) instead of `Empty aac file`. Keep an eye on PSRAM min-ever margin during the brief dual-decoder hot-swap window.

author: monkopedia-coder
body:
## Summary
Closes the **no-PR-CI gap**: hauler's only workflow was `publish.yaml` (release-triggered), so PRs got no remote checks and build/style debt accumulated silently (the ktlint debt just cleared in #8; the broken `:benchmark` module). This adds `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` running on every `pull_request` and `push` to `main`:

```
./gradlew :hauler:assemble :hauler:check ktlintCheck -x klibApiCheck
```

That gate compiles all host-buildable targets (JVM / JS / WASM / Linux / MinGW), runs the tests, the **JVM `apiCheck`** (BCV public-API gate), the license-header check, and **`ktlintCheck`** across the whole repo. Mirrors `publish.yaml`'s JDK-21 / temurin / `setup-gradle` setup; adds a `concurrency` group so superseded runs cancel.

This PR self-validates: the workflow runs on its own PR, against the now-ktlint-clean `main`.

## Verified locally (JDK 21)
`./gradlew :hauler:assemble :hauler:check ktlintCheck -x klibApiCheck` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**.

## Deliberate scope (documented inline in the workflow) + follow-ups
- **ubuntu-latest** — Apple (macOS/iOS) targets skip on a non-mac host; they stay covered at release by `publish.yaml`. Kept out here so the gate is reliably green. **Follow-up:** a dedicated `macos-latest` Apple-compile job (low risk, but needs a macOS run to confirm green before enabling).
- **`-x klibApiCheck`** — BCV's native-klib ABI check needs all targets (incl. Apple) plus a committed klib baseline, neither available on Linux; the JVM `apiCheck` still gates the API. **Follow-up:** generate + commit a macOS klib baseline to turn on `klibApiCheck`.
- **`:hauler` only** — the `:benchmark` module is pre-existingly broken against the 0.4.x Flow API (stale `dumpDeliveries`/`deliveries(scope,rates)` usage). Not gated here; `ktlintCheck` still covers its style. **Follow-up:** port `:benchmark` to the 0.4.x API or retire it.

These three follow-ups are filed-worthy as separate health items; flagging here for visibility.

author: xingguangweiwo
body:
### Motivation

- Introduce a strict runtime protocol to handle heterogeneous focal-plane metadata so stacks with different coordinate types/units can be processed uniformly.
- Support multiple verification protocols (`rank`, `coordinate`, `calibrated`) so physical checks can respect available metadata and calibration confidence.
- Enable protocol-aware, parameter-free joint refinement of all-in-focus latents and canonical depth maps to reduce physical inconsistency while preserving offline model parameters.
- Expose focal-coordinate and verification options through CLI for both inference and evaluation workflows.

### Description

- Add `src/data/focal_coordinates.py` implementing enums and `canonicalize_focal_coordinates` which returns a `FocalCoordinateBundle` with raw, canonical, physical, mask and metadata fields.
- Update dataset loading (`src/data/dataset.py`) to accept `focal_plane_coordinates` and related metadata fields and to produce canonical coordinate bundles and ranks for each sample.
- Extend focal encoders and processors (`src/models/focal_evidence_encoder.py`, `src/models/focal_processor.py`) to accept canonical coordinates, ranks, coordinate-type ids and physical masks, and to include embeddings/MLPs for these signals.
- Make physical verification protocol-aware in `src/models/physics_modules.py` so `FocalPhysicalVerifier` can run rank-only, coordinate, or calibrated checks; calibrated enables defocus rendering residuals.
- Implement a parameter-free `TraceRefiner` and `RefinementState` plus a joint refinement flow inside `src/pipelines/focal_stack_generation_pipeline.py` that performs iterative, protocol-aware candidate updates, acceptance checks, and preserves model parameters during zero-shot refinement.
- Add CLI flags in `script/inference.py` and `script/evaluate.py` for focal-coordinate type/unit/axis and `--verification-protocol` and `--allow-unknown-ordered` to control runtime behavior.
- Add unit tests `tests/test_focal_coordinates.py` and `tests/test_joint_refinement.py` that validate canonicalization, encoder/model dataflow, verification-protocol behavior, and refiner acceptance criteria.

### Testing

- Ran the new unit tests with `pytest -q tests/test_focal_coordinates.py tests/test_joint_refinement.py` and observed all tests passed.
- Exercised encoder/processor shapes and dataflow by instantiating `FocalEvidenceEncoder` and `FocalSweepEncoder` in tests to ensure batched mixed-coordinate inputs are accepted and produce expected shapes, and these assertions passed.
- Verified protocol branches in `FocalPhysicalVerifier` and primitive acceptance criteria used by the joint refiner through dedicated unit tests that assert accepted/rejected decisions, which succeeded.

body:
Captures Uwe Friedrichsen's "Why resilient software design?" (parts 1–2) — the base's first resilience / distributed-systems anchor.

## Note (`status: notes`)
- Definition of resilience (graceful degradation + timely recovery)
- **Why it became mandatory** — the three-factor shift (distributed peers, faster propagation, never-down) and the infrastructure false sense of security
- **Five failure modes** table — crash / omission / timing / response / Byzantine ("everything fails, all the time", Vogels)
- **Two hard problems** — event ordering and consensus (FLP impossibility, Lamport)
- Takeaway: resilience is a first-class design concern (at-most-once vs at-least-once, idempotency). Patterns come later in the series, so the note can grow.

## Placement
`concepts/` — foundational distributed-systems theory, beside `theory-of-constraints` and `continuous-delivery`. Avoided the retired single-use `distributed-systems` tag; `[architecture, system-design, microservices, reading]`. `source` as a YAML list of both parts; attributed throughout.

author: x-ror
body:
## Summary

Adds **`util.MIMEType`** and **`util.MIMEParams`** — a WHATWG MIME type parser, matching Node.

- **Parsing** lowercases the type, subtype and parameter **names** (values keep their case), trims HTTP whitespace, handles quoted parameter values (backslash escapes, may span lines), and drops empty / no-value / duplicate parameters (first wins).
- **Serialization** re-quotes a value only when it is empty or not an HTTP token, escaping `"` and `\`.
- **`type`/`subtype` setters** revalidate (and lowercase). **`MIMEParams`** has `get`/`has`/`set`/`delete`/`entries`/`keys`/`values`/`toString`/`toJSON` and is iterable; `get` returns `null` when missing, and `set` does **not** lowercase the name (only parsing does).
- Invalid syntax throws **`ERR_INVALID_MIME_SYNTAX`**.

New internal `mime` module (ES classes + `Symbol`-keyed state, like `URLSearchParams` in url.js), registered hidden from the public resolver — `util.MIMEType` is the public surface.

## Validation
Validated against Node: **32** behavior scenarios (parse / serialize / setters / params ops / iteration / `toJSON`) and **9** error scenarios (`code` + the exact message, including the positional `at N`) — exact match. `tests/node-compat/cases/46-util-mimetype.js` is a node-vs-lava oracle on all platforms. Odin type-checks clean.

author: bojanrajkovic
body:
Add an ADR-0020 **CONFIRM** elicitation before eleven high-cost destructive acts: `purge_recipe`, `delete_meal`, `delete_pantry_item`, `delete_meal_type`, `delete_aisle`, `delete_grocery_list`, `clear_grocery_list`, `clear_purchased_grocery_items`, `delete_menu`, `move_grocery_items_to_pantry`, and `delete_recipe_photo`.

Each handler runs `confirmOrCancel(ctx.server.server, {message, cancelled})` after it resolves the target entity and passes its refusal checks, before the destructive write. A **decline** returns a plain "Cancelled" result (never `isError`); **accept** and an **un-elicitable client** both proceed — fail-open, with the host's own tool-approval prompt as the backstop (a capable client can set the confirm to always-allow). Messages name the entity, and the bulk/cascade ones carry the count.

The gated set follows the cost-of-mistake test from ADR-0020 (permanence, blast radius, or mis-selection); reversible acts (`trash_recipe`, `reschedule_meal`), ordinary field edits, and trivially re-addable single items are deliberately **not** gated.

`confirmOrCancel` (`src/shared/tools.ts`) wraps the `confirmGate` primitive. The test harness (`makeTestServer` / `useKernelHarness`) gains a settable elicit responder so a test can drive the decline path; each gated tool gets a "declining cancels without writing" test (asserting the cancel message + that no write spy fired), plus a `confirmOrCancel` unit test.

This completes the R3 elicitation surface (the primitive #309 and the disambiguation PICK #312 already merged).

Closes #310.
Closes #311.

author: georgeakram1234
body:
This PR implements route-based code splitting and optimizes the React Query Client lifecycle to significantly improve the application's initial load performance.

### 💡 What
- Refactored `src/App.jsx` to use `React.lazy()` for all feature routes (Home, Cart, Products, etc.).
- Wrapped the main `Outlet` in `src/Components/Layout/Layout.jsx` with a `Suspense` boundary using the existing `LoadingScreen` component as a fallback.
- Hoisted `QueryClient` instantiation out of the `App` component to ensure the cache is maintained across re-renders.
- Updated `ProtectedRoute` to use `react-router-dom`'s `<Navigate />`, which removes the static dependency on the `Login` component and allows it to be correctly split into its own chunk.

### 🎯 Why
- The monolithic bundle was unnecessarily large (498.69 kB), leading to slower initial page loads.
- Re-instantiating `QueryClient` inside the `App` component is a performance anti-pattern that wipes the cache on every re-render.

### 📊 Impact
- **Main Bundle Size:** Reduced from **498.69 kB** to **273.06 kB** (a **~45% reduction** in the initial JS payload).
- **Time to Interactive:** Improved by deferring the loading of non-critical route logic.

### 🔬 Measurement
- Verified via `npm run build` output comparison.
- Confirmed chunk loading in production mode using `npm run preview` and a Playwright network monitoring script.
- Ensured all modified files pass strict linting rules.

author: jeffrharr
body:
## What

Piece B of the incremental-XML-cache prototype for Gagarin. Classifies every patch as **identity-targeted** (anchored on a specific def, cheaply indexable by defName) vs **wildcard/predicate** (matches by structure/attribute, must be re-tested against changed nodes), builds the cheap-path lookup index, and reports the identity:wildcard ratio.

Stacks on **PR #1** (the build fix — `Fix build: replace C# field keyword with explicit backing field`, commit `2c525d9`, already in this branch's history) and consumes **Piece A**'s `DependencyGraph.json`.

## Why it matters

The future incremental cache must answer "when a def changes, which patches now match it?" on every edit. Identity patches collapse to an O(1) dictionary lookup keyed by node id; wildcard patches have no anchor and must each be re-evaluated against candidate nodes. The **identity:wildcard ratio** is the headline number deciding whether incremental recompute is worth building at all.

## Classification heuristic

For each `patchEdge`:
1. Parse every `defName="X"` / `defName='X'` literal from the xpath.
2. Detect a **structural signal** that could broaden the match beyond one def: `//`, `*`, `[n]`, `text()`, `contains()`, `starts-with()`, `..`, explicit axes (`ancestor::` etc.).
3. defName present **and** no structural signal → **identity**, targeting those defs.
4. No defName but Piece A resolved **exactly one** node → **identity**, defName derived from the node id (part after last `/`). Rescues odd-but-single-def patches (e.g. matched on `label`).
5. Otherwise → **wildcard**, keeping the xpath as the re-test predicate.

Deliberately **conservative**: when unsure, wildcard. Mislabelling a wildcard as identity would silently drop patches during recompute (a correctness bug); the reverse only costs a little extra re-testing.

## Schema (consumed by Piece C)

Emits `PatchClassification.json` exactly per contract: `patches[]` (classification, targetDefNames, predicate), `identityIndex` (nodeId → patchIds, the cheap lookup), and `summary` (identityCount, wildcardCount, perMod breakdown).

## Headline ratio on the sample fixture

Bundled synthetic `DependencyGraph.sample.json` (8 edges covering both classes + edge cases): **50% identity (4 identity / 4 wildcard)**.

| class | patches |
|---|---|
| identity | clean `defName="Steel"`, single-quoted `defName='Plasteel'`, single-node fallback (autopistol matched on `label`), union of two defNames |
| wildcard | structural `[statBases/Mass]`, `//li[text()=...]`, `defName + //` descendant axis (demoted), empty FindMod xpath |

## Delivery shape

Standalone `net481` console tool at `Source/IncrementalCache/`, **kept out of `RocketMan.sln`** (that solution is wired to publicised RimWorld reference assemblies we don't want to pull in). Operates purely on JSON strings, so no RimWorld/Harmony/PatchOperation dependency. Ships a tiny hand-rolled JSON layer instead of a NuGet dep — builds on the repo's mono 4.8-api toolchain with zero restore and runs fully offline.

```bash
FrameworkPathOverride=/usr/lib/mono/4.8-api /home/deck/.dotnet/dotnet build Source/IncrementalCache/IncrementalCache.csproj -c Debug
mono Source/IncrementalCache/bin/Debug/Gagarin.IncrementalCache.exe --selftest        # 25 offline assertions
mono Source/IncrementalCache/bin/Debug/Gagarin.IncrementalCache.exe classify DependencyGraph.json -o PatchClassification.json
```

## Tests

`--selftest` runs 25 offline assertions: defName-anchored → identity, structural/text → wildcard, defName+descendant axis → wildcard, multi-node-without-anchor → wildcard, single-node fallback → identity, union of two defNames captures both, empty xpath → wildcard, identityIndex maps nodes to patches, and an end-to-end pass pinning the 50% ratio.

## Unvalidated until real Piece A output

- Synthetic fixture only; the structural-signal blocklist is tuned to common RimWorld xpath shapes and may need widening against a real patch corpus.
- `PatchOperationSequence` / `Conditional` / `FindMod` classification depends on how Piece A flattens nested ops into edges (we assume each leaf op → its own edge with its own xpath).
- defName + descendant axis is conservatively demoted to wildcard; may over-count wildcards if that pattern is common.

- **Arco verde** = ELD conectado vía Bluetooth

1. Usuario toca el anillo → se abre sheet Bluetooth

3. Selecciona el ELD de la lista

- Al volver a tocar el anillo → sheet muestra el dispositivo conectado y botón "✕ Desconectar ELD"
- Al desconectar, el anillo vuelve a **amarillo** con `GPS ○`

author: richlander
body:
## Hollow-unsafe: requires-unsafe with no directly-visible body op

The **body-axis dual** of opaque-contract (#689, signature-axis). Flags
requires-unsafe methods (`CallerUnsafeMode != None`) whose body shows no
directly-visible unsafe operation — candidates for auditing the `unsafe` surface.

A **realized** unsafe op (a pointer dereference, `calli`,
`localloc`/`cpblk`/`initblk`, or a call into the unsafe surface) is anchored to
an IL offset in `UnsafeEvidence`; **structural** evidence (a pointer in the
signature, a pointer/pinned local) is not. The IL offset is the discriminator —
a method is hollow when none of its evidence carries one.

### What's here

- **`HollowUnsafe.IsHollow` / `HasRealizedUnsafeOp` / `Collect`** — pure over the
  index's `Methods` + `UnsafeEvidence` arrays (mirrors `OpaqueUnsafe` /
  `UnsafeLeverage`); surfaced via `LibraryBodyIndex.HollowUnsafeMethods()` and the
  Analysis.App unsafe report.
- **Docs**: `memory-safety-modes.md` gains a hollow-unsafe section; notes the two
  classifications are orthogonal (signature axis vs body axis) and that their
  intersection is the strongest "this `unsafe` might be reducible" signal — still
  advisory because of the recall gap below.

### An absence claim — deliberately caveated

Unlike the positive opaque-contract claim, hollow-unsafe is an **absence** claim.
It states only that no unsafe op is *directly visible* in the scanned body —
**never** that the method is safe or that its `unsafe` is removable. A pointer
local can be optimized away in Release, erasing the IL trace of a real
dereference: the **`M1`** specimen derefs in source yet records no body op, so it
is reported hollow *despite being genuinely unsafe*. That false hollow is the
standing proof that "no visible op" must never be read as "safe". Consistent with
the thread's principle: honest structural signals, never a verification verdict.

### Verification

- 29/29 `ILInspector.Analysis.Tests` (6 new: pure predicate incl. the
  delegated-call exclusion, ordered collect, integration negative over the
  in-test pointer-deref fixture).
- End-to-end on `UnsafeChainA`: positives **M1** (false hollow), **HollowUnsafe**,
  **SignatureOnlyUnsafe**; excluded — the realized-op methods (RealUnsafePointer,
  ContractUnsafe, EscapingStackPointer), **DelegatedUnsafe** (forwards the
  pointer — a realized unsafe call), and the safe control (Safe).
- Product builds clean; markdownlint clean.

author: rickfelix
body:
## What

Wires the sourcing engine into the universal `scripts/leo-create-sd.js` per the coordinator **PATH_A** ruling (ack 75448f1b — FR-2 warn-only, no auto-register).

- **FR-1**: `--from-roadmap-item <id>` promotes a `roadmap_wave_items` row to an SD (`createFromRoadmapItem`), with a hard double-promote guard (FR-5).
- **FR-2 (warn-only)**: a non-blocking nudge when an SD is created without a preceding roadmap registration; **never auto-registers** — the default-wave/source-id convention is owned by the deferred parent engine and must not be invented on the universal path. Fully try/catch, env-disable via `REGISTER_FIRST_WARN=off`, skips children/fixtures/roadmap-sourced SDs.
- **FR-3**: atomic two-way stamp (`roadmap_wave_items.promoted_to_sd_key` + `conversion_ledger.linked_sd_key`/`promoted_proposal_path`), written together, fail-soft.
- **FR-4**: lane via the shipped `routeCandidate`; `persistLaneFailSoft` skips the **dormant** lane column on PGRST204/42703.

NEW pure `lib/sourcing-engine/register-first.js` + `tests/unit/register-first.test.js` (13 cases).

## Safety

The FR-2 hook runs **after** the SD insert, fully try/caught, return-value-unused — it cannot block or break SD creation. Adversarial review (universal-path-focused) found no Critical/High; the MEDIUM (child false-warn — real child shape is `parent_sd_key`/`parentId`, not `source:'child'`) and LOW (dormant column reports PGRST204 not 42703) are fixed in this PR.

author: mikkel
body:
## What

A **✨ Create app** button in the NaNoodle editor that turns any workflow into a standalone, shareable web app — the primary output of building a flow. The graph becomes the engine; the app is a clean **auto inputs → Run → outputs** UI that users can restyle, fullscreen, share, and export.

New page **`play.html`** (served at `/play`):

- **Auto app from the graph** — unwired source fields (Text prompts, Image-input, model prompts) become editable inputs; sink nodes become outputs. Works the instant you open it, no AI/tokens needed.
- **Customize with gptdiff-js** — describe a change → `generateDiff`/`smartapply` over the presentation (`index.html` shell + `app.css`) → new version, with **localStorage version history** you can flip between. The fixed runtime + graph are hidden from the LLM via a mini-bundler, so a diff can never break execution.
- **Fullscreen**, **Share** (self-contained `#a=` gzip link), **Export** (download a self-contained `.html`), **Open in editor**.
- **Shared/exported output never contains the API key** — recipients sign in with their own. The live in-builder preview gets the key via `postMessage` into a `sandbox="allow-scripts"` iframe.

## How it's built

- `play.html` embeds a **faithful headless copy** of the editor's engine (all 11 `NODE_TYPES` run bodies, `CTX`, video/audio polling, topo run loop) so `index.html` is never refactored or destabilized. Auth reuses `ngpt_key`, so one sign-in spans editor + app.
- `index.html`: only two additions — the `#makeapp` button and its handler (reuses the existing `serializeGraph`/`gzip`/`bytesToB64url`; hands the graph off via the same `#g=` packing as Share). Editor engine untouched.
- Real file at `/play` (Cloudflare serves it like `pictureme.html`); no `_redirects` change.

## Process

Built with a test-and-refine agent workflow (Design → Build → Verify → Refine). The verify phase ran a real **Playwright** headless smoke suite + a runtime-fidelity review + a security review. It caught and fixed: the runtime being injected as bare text (engine never ran), abort-on-first-error diverging from the editor's per-node isolation, and an unescaped `</script>` in the graph-config injection.

## Verification (independently reproduced against the committed file)

- **Playwright smoke suite: 26/26 PASS** — graph handoff, default render, run against mocked NanoGPT, fullscreen/share/export (key-free), the gptdiff customize loop, reload-from-localStorage, empty-graph guard, Image-input file picker.
- Per-node error isolation confirmed (a multi-sink graph still renders its image despite an unrelated empty node).
- `node --check` clean on the extracted module + runtime scripts; editor diff is only the two intended additions.

body:
## Summary

The `events_count` NetworkStats metric is meant to be the calendar's **upcoming** count, but when it resolves **outside** blog 7 (e.g. the extrachill.com/power landing page, blog 1), the cross-site fallback called `count_published_posts()` — which counts **every published event ever scraped**. On prod that's ~90,690 all-time vs ~38,331 actually upcoming.

(The events-site-origin path — `data_machine_events_query_events(scope=upcoming)` — was already correct; it just isn't loaded on other sites, so the fallback is what runs on /power.)

## Fix

- Add `AbstractMetricProvider::count_upcoming_events( $site_key )`: reads blog 7's `datamachine_event_dates` table directly (`post_status = 'publish' AND start_datetime >= start of today, local tz`), matching the calendar's own upcoming boundary in `data-machine-events` `CalendarAbilities` (`current_time('Y-m-d') . ' 00:00:00'`). switch_to_blog + `SHOW TABLES` guard, returns `null` when unavailable (never a fabricated zero).
- Point `EventsCountProvider`'s fallback at it instead of `count_published_posts()`.

## Verification (prod data)
```
upcoming (start today or later): 38,331
all published (old behavior):    90,690
```

## Notes
- The 2 phpcs findings on `EventsCountProvider.php` are the pre-existing PSR-4 PascalCase-filename house-style baseline across the whole NetworkStats dir — not introduced here.

author: lovelle-cardoso
body:
## What

Adds continuous deployment for the **vscode-sparkdown** extension. A push to `main` that touches the extension (or a bundled package) now auto-publishes a new version to the Microsoft VS Code Marketplace.

## How it works

`.github/workflows/publish-vscode-extension.yml`:
- **Triggers** on push to `main` touching `vscode-sparkdown/**`, `packages/**`, or the workflow file.
- **Auto-bumps** the patch version (`npm version patch -w vscode-sparkdown`) so the Marketplace never sees a duplicate version.
- **Builds + publishes** via `vsce publish --no-dependencies` (`vscode:prepublish` runs the full production build; `--no-dependencies` skips vsce's dep-walk, which chokes on the monorepo's `file:` deps — everything is bundled by esbuild anyway).
- **Commits the bump back** to `main` with `[skip ci]`. No publish loop: `GITHUB_TOKEN` pushes don't re-trigger workflows, and `[skip ci]` is a second guard.
- Runs on **Node 24** (build scripts run as `.ts` via Node type-stripping, needs ≥23.6), with a `concurrency` group so publishes never overlap and `--autostash` so the bump push-back is robust.

Per team decision: auto-bump every qualifying push (fast internal updates while the engine is pre-public); we can switch to a manual tag-based release once the extension goes public.

## Also fixes

The `package` npm script ended in `node scripts/esbuild.js --production --devtool hidden-source-map` — but `esbuild.js` doesn't exist (only `esbuild.ts`) and `--devtool` is a stale webpack flag. That step is redundant (the production bundle is already built by `package:self`) **and** would have broken `vsce`'s prepublish. Now it's just `npm-run-all -p package:*`.

## Required before merge

Repo secret **`VSCE_PAT`** must exist (Azure DevOps PAT for the `impowergames` publisher, scoped Marketplace → Manage). ✅ Added.

## Notes

- `packages/**` is a deliberately broad trigger — an occasional change to a non-bundled package will cause an extra publish. Acceptable for fast internal updates; easy to tighten later.
- The first merged run is the real end-to-end test of the full production build in CI.

body:
### Motivation

- The previous publish guard refused to publish whenever `origin/main` advanced from the triggering `${GITHUB_SHA}`, which blocked valid publishes when unrelated bot-generated commits landed (for example `docs/assets/game-launch.png`).
- The workflow must still refuse to publish when resume source or the resume workflow change to avoid publishing stale artifacts.

### Description

- Add a small shell helper `blocks_resume_publish(base, head)` in the `publish-artifacts` job that uses `git diff --name-only` to detect changes limited to `docs/resume/**` and `.github/workflows/resume.yml`, and emits clear `::error::` lines listing each blocking path.
- At the start of `Persist generated artifacts` the job now runs `git fetch origin main`, computes `current_main` and when `current_main != ${GITHUB_SHA}` it checks only the blocking paths; if only unrelated paths changed it checks out the newer `origin/main` (`git checkout --detach`) and sets `publish_base` to the commit used for publishing; if blocking paths changed it fails with an explicit error.
- The step writes `publish_base` to the job outputs and the final `Commit and push generated artifacts` step re-fetches `origin/main`, re-checks the blocking paths between `publish_base` and the new `origin/main`, and either fails (if resume-affecting paths changed) or rebases the generated-artifact commit onto `origin/main` before pushing (`git rebase "${current_main}"`).
- Preserve the existing artifact destinations, bot identity (`github-actions[bot]`), commit subject (`📄 : – refresh generated resume artifacts`), and the `github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'` prevention.

### Testing

- Ran `npx prettier --check .github/workflows/resume.yml` and `npm run format:check`; both passed.
- Ran `npm run docs:check` (link checker reported transient fetch warnings) and `git diff --check`; both completed successfully.
- `actionlint .github/workflows/resume.yml` was not run because `actionlint` is not installed in the environment.
- Simulated the path-aware guard in a temporary git repo to verify that an unrelated `docs/assets/game-launch.png` advance is allowed and that a subsequent change under `docs/resume/**` blocks publishing, and the simulation passed.
- Ran repository checks: `npm run format:write`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test:ci` (Vitest: 1208 tests passed), `npm run smoke` (passed with the existing manual-static-asset warning), and `git diff --cached | ./scripts/scan-secrets.py` (no high-risk secrets found).

body:
# TL;DR

_Patch msgpack to clear a freshly-published CVE that blocks every push._

# Features

| Feature | Audience | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Push gate (`uv-audit`) | Contributors | every push rejected on the new msgpack advisory | push passes; dep patched |

# Before / After

```text
# BEFORE — git push (pre-push uv-audit):
Found 1 known vulnerability in 1 package
msgpack 1.1.2  GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964  1.2.1
error: failed to push some refs

# AFTER:
No known vulnerabilities found
```

# Summary

A new advisory (GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964) affects `msgpack 1.1.2`, fixed in `1.2.1`. The pre-push `uv-audit` gate now rejects every push (main carries the vulnerable version). This bumps it. `msgpack` is the IPC wire format between the CLI and the sidecar, so it's load-bearing — but the bump is a lockfile-only patch.

# Setup

None. Pull and `uv sync`; the lockfile pins the patched version.

# What

- Contributors can push again — the supply-chain audit gate passes instead of blocking.
- The CLI↔sidecar IPC serialization runs on patched `msgpack` with no behavior change.

# Why

The gate exists to stop shipping known-vulnerable dependencies. `pyproject` already allows `msgpack>=1.0`, so only the lockfile + the Snyk-badge `requirements.txt` export needed updating.

# How

- `uv lock --upgrade-package msgpack` → `msgpack 1.1.2` → **1.2.1**; regenerated `requirements.txt`.

# Tests

- `pip-audit` (exact pre-push command): **No known vulnerabilities found**.
- `tests/ipc/` + `tests/sidecar/` green against the bump (msgpack is the IPC wire format) — **131 passed**.

2026-06-20 on the D5 spans task (`sess_1781916669178_3000`).

Four stacked commits land together per
`feedback-devrix-bugfix-pr-grouping` (one PR for one Phase A change):

|--------|----|----|
| `6c489ce` + `17b1f96` | AC5 | feishu card table-count / size precheck + plain-text fallback |
| `14c5212` | AC1 | tool result size cap with disk persistence |

author: lovemansgit
body:
## What & why

**Love's ruling (20 Jun 2026):** the admin merchant list shows **only genuine merchants by default**; the ~1,825 automated-test tenants are **hidden, not deleted**, and the view is reversible with a one-click **"Show all"** toggle. This is a **read-path filter only — no migration, no DB writes, no deletion.**

Origin (from the read-only production diagnosis earlier today): the test tenants are minted by the test + seed suites against the single prod Supabase, each with a random **8-hex slug fragment** for isolation (`r3-test-74a6b577-a`). The `audit_events_no_delete` rule blocks tenant teardown, so they accumulate. `?view=all` is the reversible escape hatch — **nothing is truly hidden.**

## How

- **New contract module** `src/modules/merchants/genuine-merchants.ts` — single source of truth:
  - `GENUINE_MERCHANT_SLUGS` — the six-slug allowlist safety net (`meal-plan-scheduler`, `dr-nutrition`, `fresh-butchers`, `transcorp`, `hem`, `mlp`)
  - `DEFAULT_VIEW_STATUSES` = `active | inactive | suspended`
  - `TEST_TENANT_SLUG_PATTERN` = `[0-9a-f]{8}`
  - `isGenuineMerchant()` — executable spec of the predicate
- **`repository.listMerchants`** gains `excludeTestTenants`: `allowlist OR (status IN default-view AND slug !~ '[0-9a-f]{8}')`. Precedence: **explicit `status` > `excludeTestTenants` > `excludeArchived`** (forensic `?status=archived` path untouched). SQL built from the same constants as the JS predicate so they can't diverge.
- **Page** reads `?view=all` and selects filters via the new pure `selectMerchantListFilters` helper; adds the toggle link, an accurate count label (Genuine / All / Matching), and empty-state copy.

## ⚠️ Two judgment calls for your clearance

1. **Predicate: un-anchored, not your literal sketch.** Your brief wrote `^[0-9a-f-]*[0-9a-f]{8}` — but the random hex fragment sits **mid-slug**, so the `^`-anchored form matches almost nothing. You delegated "the cleanest predicate to the reviewer's call," so this uses the **un-anchored `[0-9a-f]{8}`**, which the diagnosis proved on live data: **matched 1,821 of 1,832 rows; the 11 non-matches were exactly the genuine tenants.**

2. **RED-first = unit, not integration.** A real-DB integration test would **INSERT test tenants into the one prod Supabase**, and the audit no-delete rule blocks teardown — i.e. it would *create the exact pollution this PR hides.* So the behavioural RED test is a pure executable predicate (`isGenuineMerchant`, JS, no DB) plus SQL-surface assertions. **No prod writes.**

## 🔎 Consequence worth your eyes (not a bug)

Per your "exclude provisioning + archived from default view," **a newly-created genuine merchant (which lands as `provisioning`) is hidden from the default view until activated.** It's reachable in one click via **Show all** (the header copy + empty state guide the operator there), and the six known merchants are always shown via the allowlist. If you'd rather genuine `provisioning` merchants appear in the default view, that's a one-line change to `DEFAULT_VIEW_STATUSES` — say the word.

## Tests

RED→GREEN. `genuine-merchants.spec` (predicate behaviour) + `repository.spec` (SQL surface) + `helpers.spec` (toggle): **90/90**. Full unit suite **2196/2196**. `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint` clean.

## Parked

**Do not promote alone** — rides the next consolidated promote per your step 4. Awaiting your clearance.

body:
## What changed? Why?

Added `editor/PLAN.md`, a comprehensive design document for the first milestone of a WYSIWYG MusicXML editor. This plan outlines the architecture, scope, and implementation strategy for building an interactive notation surface where users can add, move, and remove notes on a staff, with MusicXML import/export.

**Key design decisions documented:**

1. **Document-as-source-of-truth**: The live MusicXML `Document` is mutated in place via surgical DOM edits. Untouched elements (dynamics, slurs, lyrics, etc.) survive round-trips by construction—no regenerating serializer.

2. **Single-row MVP**: Builds on the existing horizontal-scroll renderer; traditional line-wrapping and repeat glyphs are deferred.

3. **Self-contained editor**: Lives in a new `editor/` Bun workspace member with a duplicated copy of the sheet-music-display renderer, so it can eventually move to its own repository.

**Scope for step 1**: Single part, single treble staff, 4/4 time, no repeats, no voices/chords. Undo/redo, grand staff, and key/time editing are explicit follow-ups.

**Implementation roadmap** (5 phases):
- Scaffold + build wiring
- Document edits (`dom-edit.ts`): surgical add/remove/move operations with rest rebalancing
- Provenance + coordinate inverses: extend the duplicated parser with source tracking and implement `hit-test.ts` for screen↔music coordinate conversion
- Renderer pointer seam: thin additive layer on `SheetMusicDisplay` for gesture handling
- Editor shell: state management, duration palette, import/export, and gesture dispatch

The plan includes detailed verification steps and explicitly defers follow-up work (undo/redo, chords, `.mxl` import, wrapped layout, Playwright tests).

## How was the change tested?

This is a design document (no code implementation yet). No testing needed at this stage.

author: andymai
body:
Refs #1654.

## The bug
On a multi-color bin, the 3D preview shows the **lid in body color** even when a distinct lid color is set. Reported by @gavinmcfall while testing the multi-color feature ("Lid isn't getting colour").

`LidMesh` rendered the lid with the single body/material `color` prop and never consulted `featureColors` — unlike `BinMesh`, which builds per-zone color groups. Meanwhile the **exporter already paints the lid object `featureColors.lid`** (`uniformColorConfig` in `buildMultiObject3MF`), so the preview and the printed/exported result disagreed.

## The fix
When multi-color is enabled, color the lid with its zone color (`getZoneColor(featureColors, 'lid')`); otherwise keep the existing body-color fallback. The lid is a single color zone (both `LID_BODY` and `LID_RAIL` map to `'lid'`), so a uniform color matches the exporter exactly.

One-file behavior change in `LidMesh.tsx`; no generator or export changes.

## Tests
`LidMesh.test.tsx`: lid uses its zone color (`#ff0000`) when multi-color is enabled, and falls back to the body color (`#cccccc`) when disabled. `tsc -b` and ESLint clean.

## Scope note
This fixes the lid preview color only. The other items in #1654 (label-tab top showing body color, scoop top color on thin walls, lip color uniformity) are separate and not addressed here.

author: natsuume
body:
## Summary

`/goal` 等の **並列 session フロー** で発生していた誤着手と `ai:in-progress` ラベル誤削除事故への構造的対策。 `ai:in-progress` ラベル単独運用には (a) **TOCTOU race** と (b) **「誰が付けたラベルか不明」** という根本問題があったため、 GitHub の確定的な排他基盤を 2 つ組み合わせた:

| 排他基盤 | 役割 |
|---|---|
| (1) **claim comment** | GitHub comment の serial ID + timestamp で先着判定 (= 早期 detection) |
| (2) **branch push** | git server-side で同名 branch は 1 つしか存在できず、 並列 push の片方は確定的に fail (= 最終的な独占権の確定) |

claim comment 本文に `branch=<prefix>/issue-<N>-<slug>` を埋め込むことで「誰の claim か」 を確定的に識別できるようになり、 **他 session の claim / branch / ラベルを誤って削除する事故も構造的に排除** される。

## 追加内容 (`inject-always.sh` セクション 7)

### 着手 7 ステップ
1. **早期判定**: `gh issue view <N> --json labels,comments` で `ai:in-progress` ラベル / 未削除の claim comment 有無確認
2. **claim comment 投稿**: `🔒 ai:claim branch=<prefix>/issue-<N>-<slug> ts=<UTC ISO 8601>`
3. **3 秒待機** (`sleep 3`)
4. **comment 再取得 + 先着 timestamp 比較** で他 session 検知
5. **作業 branch 切る + 空 commit + 即 push** (branch 名 uniqueness の確定判定)
6. push 成功時のみ `ai:in-progress` ラベル付与 (= 人間向け補助マーカー)
7. 通常の implementation フロー (draft PR 作成 → 実装 → after 系自走) へ

### branch 名規約

`<prefix>/issue-<N>-<slug>` (例: `feat/issue-12-add-auth`, `fix/issue-25-null-deref`)

- `<prefix>`: 変更種別 (`feat` / `fix` / `chore` / `docs` / `refactor` 等)
- `<N>`: issue 番号
- `<slug>`: issue タイトルから kebab-case で抽出した短縮形

### ラベル削除規律

- `ai:in-progress` ラベルは **PR が merge された時のみ削除する** (= issue 完了時)
- 着手中断 / 撤退時はラベルを残し、 claim comment と branch のみ削除 (= 後続 session の二重着手保険)
- **他 session の claim comment / branch / ラベルは絶対に削除しない**
- 判定基準: claim comment 本文の `branch=` 値が自分の作業 branch と一致するか

### 撤退時のクリーンアップ

撤退判定 (step 1, 4, 5 のいずれか) が出たら:
1. 自分の claim comment を削除 (`gh api -X DELETE`)
2. 自分が作った branch を削除 (`git push origin --delete`)
3. ユーザに撤退理由を 1 行で必ず報告 (auto mode 中でも省略しない)

### よくある誤操作 (= 過去事例) と回避

- **誤着手** → step 2-5 の二段排他で防ぐ
- **ラベル誤削除** → claim comment の `branch=` 値で持ち主を識別、 自分のものでなければ触らない
- **撤退時の clean-up 忘れ** → step 1-3 を必ずセットで実行

## version bump

v0.1.1 → **v0.2.0** (minor — 後方互換のある機能追加: 新規律のセクション 7 追加)

3 箇所同期: `plugin.json` / `marketplace.json` / repo `README.md` / plugin `README.md`、 配送レイヤを 4 → 5 (排他系を追加) に更新

## Test plan

- [x] `jq empty` で plugin.json / marketplace.json の syntax 検証
- [x] `inject-always.sh` を SessionStart 入力で smoke test → セクション 7 が末尾に追加されていることを確認 (top-level `##` セクションが 7 つ)
- [x] pre-push-review:code-reviewer subagent → バグなし
- [x] pre-push-review:security-reviewer subagent → 脆弱性なし
- [x] pre-push-review:codex-reviewer subagent → regression なし
- [ ] マージ後に install して実際の並列 session シナリオで排他動作を確認
