author: vodongha
body:
Second milestone — full authentication (SPEC §5, §7 Module 1). Builds on M1.

## Schema (Flyway V2)
`USERS`, `USER_DEVICES`, `AUTH_TOKENS` with the Oracle conventions: identity PKs, UUID v7 `RID`, `NUMBER(1)` flags, **nullable** `password_hash` (Google-only accounts), **function-based partial-unique** indexes on `email` / `fcm_token` (live rows only), FK indexes.

## Security
- **Stateless JWT** access tokens (HS256, jjwt). `SecurityConfig` permits `/auth/**` + ping, authenticates the rest.
- **BCrypt** passwords; **uniform login failure** (no account enumeration).
- **Refresh tokens** are opaque, stored **SHA-256-hashed**, and **rotated** on every `/auth/refresh`. Replaying a rotated token ⇒ **reuse detected → revoke all the user's sessions** (Open Decision #7: flat table revokes all sessions, by design for now).
- **Google Sign-In**: server-side ID-token verification (`google-api-client`), configured via `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`.
- **Email verify / password reset** via single-use, short-TTL hashed tokens.
- `AuditorAware` now reads the authenticated user from the `SecurityContext` (M1 left it a stub).

## Endpoints
`POST /auth/register|login|google|refresh|verify-email|forgot-password|reset-password`; `GET/PATCH /users/me`; `POST /users/me/devices`. All use the `{data,error,meta}` envelope.

## Hardening (SPEC §5.3)
Per-IP rate limit on `/auth/*`, request body-size cap, CORS whitelist (no `*` with credentials). 401/403 rendered as RFC 7807 in the envelope.

## Email provider (Open Decision #4)
Shipped a dev `LoggingEmailSender` (logs the link) so verify/reset flows are exercisable now; a real provider (Brevo/Resend free tier) is a drop-in `EmailSender` swap, **deferred to pre-production**. This unblocks M2 without forcing the account decision.

## Verification
- **20 unit tests green** (`mvn test`): JWT round-trip / tamper / wrong-key / short-secret, opaque-token hashing & uniqueness, and `AuthService` security paths (uniform login failure, Google-only account, duplicate-email conflict, **refresh reuse revokes all sessions**).
- **Against the vodongha ADB** (manual, profile `local`): Flyway migrates **V2 into `TRAVEL_MATE`**, Hibernate `validate` passes, and the full flow works: register → `GET /users/me` (200) → no-auth `/users/me` (401 envelope) → login → refresh rotation → **reuse → 401 "all sessions revoked"** → FCM device registration (201). Internal `id` is never exposed; only `rid`.
- `AuthIT` (Testcontainers `oracle-free`) added for CI — runs on `mvn verify` with a Docker daemon (not run here; Docker was down).

## Notes
- `TRAVEL_MATE` schema (underscore) created on the ADB; secrets/wallet/`.env` gitignored.
- JWT secret comes from `JWT_SECRET` (a clearly-insecure placeholder default keeps `mvn spring-boot:run` working in dev; override everywhere real).

author: agenta-asaf
body:
## The bug

Dogfooding v0.46.6: an agent 401s, the user clicks **Login Again**, and **nothing happens** — no browser, no error, no change.

## Root cause (confirmed from live logs)

The click ran `startLaunchFlow()`, whose Phase 2 trusts `CheckCliAuth`:

```
ResolveCli claude            ✓
CheckCliAuth claude.cmd       ✓  → authenticated:true   ← FALSE POSITIVE
needsLogin = false           → login skipped (no browser opens)
ControllerResync force=false → no-op on the running persistent controller
```

`claude auth status` only confirms a credential is **present**, not **valid**. An expired/revoked token still reports `authenticated:true`, so the gated flow trusts it, skips login, and the non-forced resync no-ops. The **401 itself** is the ground truth that auth is broken (and P1.3 already surfaces it) — not the status check.

## Fix

The explicit "Login Again" actions now **force** a login, bypassing the check (the 401 already told us the token is bad):

- **New `forceProviderLogin()`** (`flows/force-login.ts`): runs `runCliLogin` unconditionally → `openOAuthBrowserPane` (in-app browser pane, #1594) → `setAuthUrl`. **Never** calls `CheckCliAuth`.
  - Deliberately **omits the status-check success-poll** the gated flow uses: with a present-but-expired token that poll would "succeed" on the first tick and reap the in-flight login CLI before the user finishes.
- **`useAgentControllerStatus.relogin()`** reads the CLI path + auth env from block meta (`cmd` / `cmd:env`, written at launch) and calls the helper.
- Both **"Login Again" entry points** (failure banner `onLoginAgain`, inline error node `onAgentErrorLogin`) call `relogin()` instead of `startLaunchFlow()`.
- **`/login` refactored** onto the same helper (DRY; also gains the in-app pane).

`startLaunchFlow()` keeps trusting `CheckCliAuth` for **first launch**, where it's reliable (genuinely no credential → correctly returns false). The running persistent agent re-reads its credential per request, so the next message uses the fresh token and clears the failure row.

## Verification

- Diagnosed live on a dev build (logs in spec §11); `/login` was the manual workaround (it already bypassed the gate).
- `tsc` clean, `task build:frontend` green.
- `force-login.test.ts` — 4 cases: runs `runCliLogin` with the right args + opens the URL; **never** calls the auth-status check; warns + no `setAuthUrl` on a null URL; resolves on system-browser fallback.

## Series

P1.1/P1.2 (#1589) · P1.3 (#1590) · P2.3 inline CTA (#1592) · P2.1 browser pane (#1594) · **P2.5 force-login (this PR)** · Spec: `SPEC_REAUTH_FROM_AUTH_ERROR_2026_06_20.md` §11

## Follow-up (noted in spec)

Force-restart / health-revalidate after login so providers that cache the token in-process pick it up without a manual message resend.

author: thorn14
body:
## Summary
This PR improves the user experience for contrast value inputs and fixes a critical bug where renaming color ramps in the palette store didn't update token references, breaking the links between tokens and their ramps.

## Key Changes

- **New `ContrastInput` component**: Replaces raw `<input type="number">` elements with a smarter component that:
  - Maintains a local draft string so users can freely edit and empty the field without it snapping back
  - Commits values live as they parse to finite numbers
  - On blur, clamps out-of-bounds values and falls back to the last committed value if the input is invalid
  - Provides a much better editing experience for contrast ratio and APCA values

- **Fix ramp renaming**: When a color ramp is renamed in the palette store, the vocab store now automatically updates all token references (in `ramp`, `baseRamp`, and `base` fields) to use the new name. This mirrors the existing ramp-deletion remapping logic.

- **Add `renameRamp` action to vocab store**: New public action that remaps all ramp references in the vocabulary when a ramp is renamed.

- **Responsive token grid layout**: Refactored token preview cards from fixed-width flex layout to a CSS Grid with `auto-fill` and `minmax()`, allowing cards to reflow and shrink on narrow panels instead of forcing one card per row.

- **Test coverage**: Added tests for the `renameRamp` functionality to ensure all ramp references are updated correctly and that no-op renames are handled gracefully.

## Implementation Details

The `ContrastInput` component uses a ref to track focus state, allowing it to distinguish between user edits and external value updates. This prevents the common UX problem where a controlled number input becomes impossible to lower because deleting the last digit causes the value to snap back immediately.

The ramp renaming fix ensures data consistency by leveraging the existing `remapPortableVocabularyRamps` utility, which handles all the different ways ramps can be referenced in the vocabulary structure.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Auditor finding

`abundant-number-oq-03` (`Proofs/AbundantOddInfiniteOQ03.lean`) was marked **`status: verified` / `badge: verified` / `axiomCount: 0`** in gallery meta.json, but **did not compile** against the pinned Mathlib.

### Root cause
Line 42:
```lean
refine ⟨(⟨472, by norm_num⟩ : Odd 945).mul (odd_two_mul_add_one k), ?_⟩
```
`Odd n` is definitionally `∃ m, n = 2*m + 1`, so dot notation `.mul` on an `Odd` term resolves against the `Exists` namespace:
```
error: Invalid field `mul`: The environment does not contain `Exists.mul`
```
Elaboration failed, and `#print axioms infinitely_many_odd_abundant` reported **`sorryAx`** — contradicting the "verified, 0 axioms" claim.

### Fix
Call `Odd.mul` explicitly (`Odd a → Odd b → Odd (a * b)`):
```lean
refine ⟨Odd.mul (⟨472, by norm_num⟩ : Odd 945) (odd_two_mul_add_one k), ?_⟩
```

### Verification
After the fix, the file compiles cleanly and the in-file `#print axioms` reports:
```
'AbundantOddInfiniteOQ03.infinitely_many_odd_abundant' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
```
No `sorryAx`, no `Lean.ofReduceBool`. The entry is now genuinely `verified` / 0-axiom, matching meta.json. No meta changes required.

author: dannbleeker
body:
## What

Adds **obstacle-aware branch routing**: a tapered branch bows around an unrelated topic box its straight path would otherwise pass behind. Shared pure geometry (`bowToClear`) → the canvas (stashed on `data.attachBow` in `sync()`) and the SVG exporter compute the **same** bow from the **same** node boxes, so **canvas == export**.

## The contract (why this is safe)

`bowToClear` returns **either** a bow that fully clears every nearby box **or** `0` (leave the branch straight). It **never** returns a bow that displaces a branch yet leaves it still crossing a box. A clear branch is byte-identical to before; only the organic tapered ribbon honours the bow.

Mechanics: search **both** perpendicular directions, keep the smallest clearing `|bow|`; a tight `band(margin)` fast-path returns `0` for a clear branch (the common case) before any wider scan; `band(maxBow+margin)` so no swept-in victim is missed; the cubic is sampled inclusive of its endpoints (a box on an endpoint is un-clearable → straight) and densely enough (~4px) that a short box can't slip between samples. Boxes are passed by id (endpoints skipped internally — no per-edge allocation); the bow is computed only for the tapered ribbon (`isTaperBranch`).

## Honest scope note

With the orientation-axis fix (Fix A, already merged) the **originally reported** `ERHVERV → EAAA`-behind-`Censor på uni` graze **no longer reproduces** — the screenshot tree has 0 grazes. So this router is a **dormant safety net** for denser future layouts, not a constant transform. Shipping it anyway per request.

## Verification

- **Two adversarial review rounds.** Round 1 found 4 defects in the first cut (wrong-direction, missed-victim pre-filter, corridor, O(N²)) — all fixed by the rework. Round 2 found 1 (sampler aliasing) — fixed by densifying the sampler.
- Every confirmed failure mode is a regression test, plus a **4000-case deterministic fuzz** asserting the contract against a dense 800-sample oracle (0 violations).
- `pnpm gate` green (1163 tests); export byte-identical on the clean tree (canvas == export); browser smoke clean.

## Summary
**Compliance-critical slice.** Swaps the VID-03 stub for **real server-side masking**: the backend blurs every detected face before a frame is stored or shown to a vision provider. **Ships dark** behind `feature_flags.video_import_enabled` — merging this code does not enable it. **Enabling the flag in any environment with real PHI additionally requires compliance sign-off** (server-side masking is a new trust boundary: unmasked patient faces exist transiently inside the backend). Plan commit: `docs: plan for VID-04`.

## What changed
- **Backend**:
  - `modules/video_import/masking.py` — real `mask_frame`: OpenCV **bundled Haar cascade** (`cv2.data.haarcascades` — no model binary vendored; detection stays **in-process**, unmasked frames never leave the task), Gaussian-blur each face bbox (expanded margin, size-scaled kernel), re-encode. **Fail-closed**: any decode/detect/blur/encode error drops the frame (never stores the original); `faces_blurred == faces_detected`. Zero-face frames dropped by default.
  - `api/v1/video_import.py` — `_extract_and_mask_frames` stores each masked JPEG to `frames/{sid}/{ts}.jpg` (the key shape the vision pipeline already reads) with a server-issued `MaskingProof` (same `core.types` contract iOS uses) + `SERVER_MASKING_APPLIED`; failures emit `SERVER_MASKING_FAILED`.
  - `core/audit_events.py` — `SERVER_MASKING_APPLIED`/`FAILED` + PHI-free whitelists.
  - `config/schema.py` — `video_import_drop_zero_face_frames` (default True).
- **Deps/Infra**: `requirements.txt` — `opencv-python-headless`, `numpy`. `Dockerfile` — `libglib2.0-0` (opencv-headless runtime).
- **Tests**: 9 new masking unit tests + 2 orchestrator store/audit tests; removed the now-superseded stub test.

## Why
Backlog VID-04 (Stage C). Completes the multimodal path: with masking in place, an uploaded video's frames can enrich the note via Stage 2 — but only once compliance enables the flag.

- [x] **Masking proof preserved (P0-02)**: every stored frame carries a server-issued `MaskingProof` + `SERVER_MASKING_APPLIED`; masking is the same `core.types.MaskingProof` contract the iOS path validates

- [ ] **⚠️ Compliance sign-off required to ENABLE** — server-side masking is a new trust boundary (transient unmasked PHI in-backend). Detection is local (no managed CV API), fail-closed, zero-face-drop default, fully audited. **Do not flip `video_import_enabled` in a PHI env without sign-off.** Human-verify.

author: whynotmetoo
body:
## Summary
Migrate the improved wave gathering dynamics and bulge recoil physics from `docs_local/liquid-animation-improved` to the main library's liquid controller.

## Changes
- **Cycle Timing:** Increased the cycle duration from `4000ms` to `5400ms` to prolong the gathering phase while keeping subsequent phases' absolute speed identical.
- **Wave Gathering:** Reimplemented wave generation using localized cosine pulse wave equations that travel inward toward the drip location.
- **Catmull-Rom Path Generation:** Sampled the wave at 17 key points and interpolated them via a Catmull-Rom-to-Cubic-Bézier spline, preventing horizontal jitter/drift.
- **Flicker Fix:** Shifted the wave Y baseline up by `1.0px` (`drip.targetBottom - 1.0`) to ensure the flat wave lies completely above the clip rect boundary in `opacity` and `none` transparency modes.
- **Wave Amplitude Tweak:** Increased active wave heights by `2.0px` to compensate for the baseline shift, keeping waves visually prominent.
- **Bulge Recoil & Continuity:** Added a residual bulge in Phase 3/4 to maintain a solid visual presence under the gooey filter, aligned gravity equations at pinch-off for continuous velocity, and converted the recoil to a linear decay ending at the cycle's close.

## Risk / Rollback
- **Risk:** Low. Only affects the SVG liquid layer rendering (`src/dom/liquid.ts`).
- **Rollback:** Discard changes to `src/dom/liquid.ts`.

## Notes / Follow-ups
- All existing 68 unit tests compile and pass successfully.
- Manual verification shows smooth waves and recoil transitions without sub-pixel flickering in all transparency modes.

body:
The Heading levels picker in the outline builder went only to 3. Now it offers **1–7 plus "Auto (as deep as needed)"**.

## Why & what changed
Markdown has only 6 heading levels (`#`…`######`) and the outline reserves `#` for the page title, so real headings run `##`→`######`. The old rule hard-stopped at `####`.

- Extracted `buildHeadingRule(levels)`; the picker now offers Auto + 1–7.
- Levels map `##` (section) → `###` (sub-section) → deeper, down to `######`.
- For 6/7 (beyond what headings allow), real headings cap at `######` and deeper nesting uses **bold lead-ins + nested bullet lists**.
- "Auto" (0) lets the model go as deep as the material needs; level 1 stays flat, and Auto no longer collapses to flat.

Tests cover depth scaling, the h6 cap, and Auto. CI green on the source commit.

author: almatraderscom-byte
body:
## Problem (owner-reported)
A staff task's elapsed/working time was counting from the moment the task was **dispatched** (often the night before, when the owner assigns it via the agent) instead of from when the staff member **checks in** the next day.

## Root cause (verified in code)
`worker/src/staff/proof-timeout.mjs` applied the attendance gate **only to staff with a linked ERP `user_id`**. Staff without that link fell through to `anchorTime()` = `created_at`/`sentAt` = dispatch time. A prior partial fix gated only linked staff, so the bug persisted.

`productivity-monitor.mjs` already does this correctly; `proof-timeout.mjs` diverged.

## Fix
All staff have ERP accounts and must check in to start work, so the gate now applies to **everyone**: no check-in today → task not tracked/chased yet; once checked in → `effectiveAnchor = max(anchorTime(task), check-in)`.

## Verification
- `node --check` passes on the worker file.
- Strict tightening: only staff without a check-in today lose the old "count from dispatch" path — exactly the bug.

## Deploy note
Worker file (VPS, pm2 `agent-worker`). After merge: VPS `git pull` + `pm2 restart agent-worker`.

body:
## Summary
v0.2 로드맵 'OPA Rego 정책 평가' 항목.

`Policy.engine = 'builtin'` (기본, severity threshold) 또는 `'opa'` (Rego). OPA v1.17.1 정적 바이너리를 backend Docker 이미지에 함께 빌드(amd64/arm64). external OPA 서버 의존 회피 — Helm/Compose 추가 설치 불필요.

## 동작
- `engine='opa'` 정책에 `definition.rego` 코드와 (선택) `definition.query` 지정
- simulator/게이트에서 OPA subprocess(8s timeout)로 평가
- `deny`가 1건 이상이면 blocked, deny 메시지가 `matched`로 노출
- OPA 바이너리 다운로드 실패/미설치 시 graceful disable — engine 'opa' 정책만 비활성, 나머지는 정상

## 마이그레이션
lightweight: `ALTER TABLE policies ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS engine VARCHAR(16) DEFAULT 'builtin' NOT NULL`. 기존 설치 자동 호환.

## 신규
- `backend/app/services/opa.py` — `is_available`/`opa_binary`/`evaluate(rego, input, query)`

body:
## Summary

Implements declarative deep graph relationships for catalog/sourcegen-backed sources so cheap sources can emit assets plus their resource relationships, not just flat runtime nodes.

### What changed

- Extends `connectordefinitions.ProjectionSpec` with:
  - `entity` to converge the primary entity to a stable spine URN.
  - `relationships` to declare durable graph edges from emitted event attributes.
- Adds validation guardrails:
  - v1 relation allowlist: `belongs_to`, `contains`, `owned_by`, `member_of`, `attached_to`.
  - endpoint `entity_type`, `urn_kind`, and `id_attributes` required.
  - rejects audit-event relationships, unstable anchors like event IDs/cursors/run IDs/timestamps, and non-emitted attributes.
  - caps relationships at 8 per family.
- Adds `catalogrelationships.go`, a shared projection augmenter used by catalog runtime and generated projectors.
- Updates sourcegen to:
  - carry projection specs into generated projection code.
  - merge `projection.fields` into generated JSON API attributes.
  - wrap generated projectors with the shared relationship augmenter.
- Adds validation, runtime projection, and sourcegen tests.
- Retrofits the first high-value secrets slice:
  - Doppler secrets `belongs_to` Doppler projects.
  - HashiCorp Vault secrets `owned_by` Vault users.

## Validation

author: rlaope
body:
## Summary

Adds a wrapper-facing worktree executor binding contract so OMH can turn an observed prepared worktree into a safe executor launch or attach recipe without starting the executor itself.

## Why

Hermes can already prepare isolated worktrees and coding sessions, but wrappers still needed a deterministic bridge between an observed worktree and an executor-specific session start. This PR adds that bridge while preserving the key OMH boundary: a prepared worktree is isolation evidence only, and a binding recipe is session-start guidance only.

## What changed

- Adds `omh worktree bind --path <worktree> --executor <executor>`.
- Introduces `worktree_executor_binding/v1` from `src/wrapper/worktree_binding.py`.
- Reuses the canonical worktree isolation planner instead of duplicating isolation policy.
- Keeps `src/worktree_creator.py` focused on prepare/list/ledger behavior.
- Exposes resolved launch templates for Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, and oh-my runtime profiles without launching anything.
- Adds wrapper actions for open, attach, and record-observed-runtime steps.
- Syncs README, architecture, capabilities, installation, chat wrapper examples, parity, and probe output.

## Boundary behavior

- Does not launch Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, or runtime profiles.
- Does not claim implementation, review, CI, merge, or live executor evidence.
- Missing worktree paths block with `blocked_missing_worktree`.
- Existing filesystem paths without an OMH ledger are labeled `ready_filesystem_only` rather than overclaimed as observed OMH worktrees.

## Verification

Observed locally:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest tests/test_worktree_creator.py tests/test_wrapper_sessions.py -v
PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
uv run python -m src.cli docs workflows --check
uv run python -m src.cli harness validate
uv run python -m src.cli release skill-content-smoke --json
uv run python -m compileall -q src tests
git diff --check
```

All passed.

## Review notes

- Code review found no must-fix issues; LSP/Pyright was unavailable to that reviewer.
- Architecture review initially flagged cross-layer coupling and duplicated isolation policy.
- Follow-up changes moved binding assembly into the wrapper layer and reused the canonical isolation plan.
- Final architecture review status: CLEAR.

## Risks and rollout

- Live Hermes chat rendering and real executor process launch were not tested; this PR intentionally stops at deterministic local binding recipes.
- Future launcher/rendering behavior should stay in wrapper/session modules, not worktree ledger modules.

author: sjparthi
body:
## Summary

The options **expiries+contracts metadata pull** showed a progress bar frozen at `0/N` for the whole pull even though the registry was filling (operator-observed). Two fixes (`docs/MIGRATION.md` #850):

- **Live progress** — the pull now emits incremental progress the `/universe` bar already polls, reusing the SPOT pull's `sync_from_ledger` resync (DEC-SPOT-WINDOW-PROGRESS-001). Bar fills 0→100% per expiry cell (Phase 1) + per contract job (Phase 2).
- **Honest label** — `contracts pulled = 0` is annotated "metadata-only by design" (the lean universe parses then discards the ~89k legs — DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001), not "broken". No leg is persisted.

**Decision ID:** DEC-METADATA-LIVE-PROGRESS-001 (MIGRATION.md #850).

## Z+ 15-row matrix (requirement → implementation → test)

| # | Requirement | Implementation | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Metadata pull emits progress | `pull_expiries_contracts(on_progress=...)` (`metadata_pull.py`) | `test_metadata_pull` collector climbs 1→total |
| 2 | Route stops discarding the hook | route maps it onto `sync_from_ledger` (`app.py`) | `test_...route` job-progress |
| 3 | Mapping is correct (no arg-swap) | lifted to module-level `_metadata_progress_sync` | `test_metadata_progress_sync_maps_onto_sync_from_ledger` |
| 4 | Total = cells + contract jobs | phase-boundary rescale reuses `contract_jobs_from/to_pull` | `test_...phase_boundary` rescale |
| 5 | `completed ≤ total` always | per-cell/job ticks + `PullProgress.sync` clamp | rescale + clamp tests |
| 6 | Zero-cells → no emit (no div0) | guard before emit | `test_progress_no_cells_emits_nothing` |
| 7 | Failed cell ticks but adds no job | `exc is None` gate on `expiries_seen` | `test_progress_failed_cell_ticks_but_adds_no_contract_jobs` |
| 8 | `on_progress=None` is a silent no-op | `_emit_progress` early-returns | non-dashboard caller tests |
| 9 | Honest note only on expiries_only+0 | `_contracts_note` truth table | `test_completeness` 6-combo + default + CSV |
| 10 | Note is XSS-safe | rendered via `esc()` | template `esc()` |
| 11 | Lean universe intact (no leg stored) | progress/label only; no persist change | unchanged upsert paths |
| 12 | Reuse spot resync (no reinvent) | same `sync_from_ledger(bars=0,failed=0)` | mapping test |
| 13 | Bars=0 (no candles) | metadata pull has no bars | mapping test asserts bars=0 |
| 14 | CSV carries the note | new `Notes` column | CSV test |
| 15 | Scope guard holds | dashboard progress+label only | full dashboard sweep green |

## Z+ 7-row resilience matrix

| Failure mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Hook raises | route hook only calls lock-guarded `sync_from_ledger` (can't raise on valid ints) |
| Zero cells | no emit → bar shows the placeholder, never `total=0` div0 |
| Failed expiry cell | ticks `completed`, adds NO contract job → total stays exact |
| Non-dashboard caller (`on_progress=None`) | byte-identical no-op |
| Mixed-year underlying that DID persist contracts | gets `""` (no false "by design" note) |
| Re-poll mid-Phase-1 | `total` re-scales on the final cell; clamp prevents overshoot |
| Order of `as_completed` (production) | rescale reads accumulated `expiries_seen` → order-independent |

## Z+ 7-layer audit

1. Lint — `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean.
2. Types — `pyright` 0 errors on the 3 changed modules; `mypy --strict` clean (lone error is pre-existing `cma` in untouched `stage3_refine.py`).
3. Unit — `metadata_pull` + `completeness` + route tests pass; broad dashboard sweep **1,234 passed**.
4. Coverage — `metadata_pull.py` 100% line+branch; `completeness.py` 100% line+branch; the route-glue mapping now **line-covered + asserted** (lifted out of the pragma).
5. Reuse — same `sync_from_ledger` resync the spot pull uses (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON).
6. Ledger — MIGRATION.md #850 added; numbering validates (unique).
7. Scope — lean universe untouched (no leg persisted); brute-force engine untouched.

## 4-agent hostile review

author: napieraj
body:
Improves `scripts/amalgamate.sh`, grounded in how SQLite's amalgamation builder (`tool/mksqlite3c.tcl`) actually works — fetched and read, not recalled. The key reference principle: **weave each local header exactly once and leave its include guard intact** (SQLite never strips guards). Both of the script's self-documented fragilities dissolve under it.

## What changed

**1. Guard-stripper removed.** `strip_file` no longer collapses the `#ifndef MOS_*_H / #define / #endif` wrapper — it drops only the library-local quoted includes and leaves guards in. Because each header is woven once, the guard is a harmless no-op, so an interior `#if` inside a header is no longer something the weaver must reason about. This deletes the guard-count safety loop that previously *refused loudly* any header with more than the 1+1 include-guard pair — the landmine is gone, not just guarded.

**2. One authoritative header list.** `WEAVE_HEADERS` now feeds both the weave loop and the include-stripper (`STRIP_NAMES` is derived from it), so the four hand-written awk drop-patterns can no longer drift from the `for hdr in …` order. A **completeness guard** fails loudly, naming the file, if any `src/*.h` is missing from the list — replacing the old silent-strip-but-never-weave path that surfaced only as a confusing undefined-symbol link error downstream in CI. It runs **before any output is written**, so a validation failure never leaves a half-written `dist/`.

**3. CONTRIBUTING link example fixed.** It listed three frameworks and omitted **DiskArbitration** — a default build fails to link at `mos_da.c`'s `DADiskCopyDescription`. Now matches the README, the MANIFEST, and the script's own header comment (four frameworks, with the `-DMOS_USE_DISKARBITRATION=0` opt-out noted).

## `dist/mos.c` impact

Regenerated; the only content change is the three header guards now appearing in the woven output (**9 lines**) — a compiler no-op since each is woven once.

## Verification (local, non-macOS)

- `sh -n` clean; deterministic across runs (identical SHA-256); `dist/` byte-identical to a fresh regen.
- `--check` green and side-effect-free; `--check` correctly detects drift (exit 1); bad arg → exit 2 + usage.
- Completeness guard fires on an unlisted `src/*.h`, names it, exits 1, **and leaves `dist/mos.c` untouched**.
- All 30 section banners present (27 `.c` + 3 `.h`), zero leftover local includes, `#if`/`#endif` balanced, key symbols from each layer present in the weave.

The macOS compile/link + amalgamated-test-suite legs run in CI (Apple frameworks aren't available locally) — but leaving woven-once guards in is trivially valid C, so the risk is minimal.

**Not done** (deliberately): a full SQLite-style recursive-inline rewrite. It would remove the explicit header list but scatters header bodies through the output (hurting `dist/` readability), and SQLite itself confirms a manually-curated order is the norm.

author: bkearns
body:
## Summary

Teacher-side and transport halves of the MaaS P2P layer, building on the pack schema (T-24) + AEAD crypto (T-33) + learner ingest (T-27) landed in #78.

### MAAS-T-26 — `replication.rs` (selective pack build + emit) — `t_afc3cb85`
- `build_pack` copies **exactly** the teacher selection — **no neighbour bleed**. Out-of-selection edges/temporal events are dropped, **counted, and logged** via `BuildReport` (never a silent truncation). → MR-P2P-07
- **Summary-first** redacts every full body before hashing: `TeachingItem.body` → `None`, `FoldEntry.raw_trajectory` → empty; summaries preserved. → MR-P2P-08
- Provenance envelope (teacher+learner fingerprints) + per-item rows recorded on build. → MR-P2P-09
- Postcondition: never emits a pack that fails `validate()`; `build_and_seal` round-trips through the real T-33 `seal`/`open`.

### MAAS-T-25 — `peer_transport.rs` (transport core) — `t_a24e426b`
- Built over a small `DataChannel` trait seam (the exact `webrtc-rs` `RTCDataChannel` surface) — **no heavy dependency added**.
- State machine `Verified→Open→DataFlow`; send-before-open **errors, never drops** (MR-P2P-03).
- Bounded framer + `ChunkAssembler`: oversized peer → typed error, **not OOM** (MR-P2P-04).
- `buffered_amount` backpressure before each send (MR-P2P-05).
- Cancellation-safe: counters advance **only after** the atomic send `Ok`, so drop-mid-send leaves no partial state and is resumable (MR-P2P-06).
- Fuzzed framer/assembler (`peer_transport_fuzz.rs`, 4000 cases): never panics, respects byte budget.

## Gates
- 45 sync tests green · `clippy --all-targets` 0 warnings · fmt clean.
- Module-level `deny(unwrap/expect/indexing/panic)` on both files; transport also `deny(await_holding_lock)`.

## Deferred (captured on the board)
- `t_1bd8b19e` — **MAAS-T-25b**: concrete `webrtc-rs` `DataChannel` impl behind the seam. Deferred because adding `webrtc` is a **suite-wide, hard-to-reverse dependency decision** — separated from the unit-testable security logic. Needs sign-off before wiring.

Refs MAAS-T-26, MAAS-T-25

author: ewindisch
body:
## #326 — param-server delta aggregation: a real reducer (replace DO-Merge)

**Scope: reducer only.** Param-server *transport* and held-out-eval *host infra* are explicitly out of scope (deferred, gated follow-ons). Implements the resolved decisions in `docs/plans/2026-06-18-326-delta-reducer-spike.md`.

### What DO-Merge got wrong (what this replaces)
`training/merge.rs` `do_merge` / `additive_merge` assert **shape equality** on the raw LoRA A/B factors, so the moment two contributors carry different per-layer ranks — the normal case once the rank oracle assigns non-uniform ranks, or workers run with different `layer_overrides` — N-way merge hard-fails. DO-Merge is also non-associative (path-dependent blend + direction renorm), so an N-way merge would depend on contributor order. The 1-vs-1 save-time DO-Merge path is left intact; this adds the **N-way** path.

### Reducer design (trait + stack + truncated SVD)
- **`DeltaReducer` trait** — order-independent N-way merge, swappable (held-out-eval variants, future native reducers) with zero consumer churn.
- **`StackSvdReducer`** — for each layer key, stack contributors' factors in **delta-space**:
  `B_stack = [w_1·B_1 | … ]` `[out, Σr]`, `A_stack = [A_1 ; … ]` `[Σr, in]`. This is exactly the weighted sum of rank-1 updates `ΔW = Σ_i w_i·(B_i·A_i) = B_stack·A_stack`, with **no dense `[out,in]` materialization** and **no requirement that the `r_i` agree**.
- **ONE truncated SVD per round to a fixed rank R**, computed via two economy SVDs on the tall-skinny stacks (`Σr` small): SVD of `A_stack`, fold into `C = B_stack·Uₐ·diag(Sₐ)` `[out, Σr]`, SVD of `C`, recombine `Vh`. Exact rank-Σr SVD of `ΔW`, truncated to R (zero-padded if `Σr < R` to keep checkpoint shapes invariant). Output is expressed at `scaling = 1.0` (weights + per-contributor scaling folded in).
- **Order-independence:** `ΔW` is a plain sum; permuting contributors permutes stack columns/rows identically and leaves the product (hence its SVD) unchanged up to fp.

### Validation / provenance gate (secure multitenant)
- Aggregation is over an **explicit** contributor set — the reducer never discovers or mixes deltas across tenants.
- **`ContributionGate`** gates + weights each contributor by **signed host id trust (Phase-2 #354) × f(`delta_norm_ratio`) × per-key scaling**, folded into the stack weights. Over-norm / untrusted contributors are **rejected with a clear error** (named host, bound) — never silently dropped or clamped to zero (a quiet drop would let a poisoned host shrink the merge invisibly).
- **`ValidationHook`** trait is the pluggable held-out-eval seam; default `NoopValidation` (the real eval-host is the deferred follow-on).

### Other resolved decisions
- **Static rank↔quant cap:** `TenantDeltaConfig::from_profile_with_quant_caps` clamps the oracle's per-layer rank by stored dtype (FP8/int8 → 8, FP16/BF16 → 16, FP32 → uncapped) via `rank_cap_for_dtype_bytes`. **Static only** — applied once at config build, NOT in the live `auto_adapt` path. `from_profile` delegates with `None` (backward compatible).
- **Optimizer state:** Muon momentum **dropped** at aggregation (fresh optimizer post-checkpoint) — `reduce_state_dicts` emits only `lora_a`/`lora_b`, no `__muon_momentum` / `__effective_rank` metadata.

### Send/Sync handling
tch `Tensor` is `!Send`. The reducer keeps **all** tensor work on one device/thread (`reduce_key` validates uniform device, errors otherwise). `Provenance` / `ContributorState` are plain-old-data; contributions cross thread/host boundaries as **serialized delta bytes + POD provenance**, deserialized on the reducer thread — never as live `Tensor`s.

### Deferred (out of scope)
- Param-server **transport** (cross-host all-reduce / signing verification wiring).
- Held-out-eval **host** (only the `ValidationHook` seam lands here).
- **No capnp/RPC surface added.**

### Files changed
- `crates/hyprstream/src/training/delta_reducer.rs` (new) — trait, `StackSvdReducer`, gate, validation seam, `reduce_state_dicts`, `rank_cap_for_dtype_bytes`, 10 tests.
- `crates/hyprstream/src/training/mod.rs` — register module + re-exports.
- `crates/hyprstream/src/training/tenant_delta.rs` — `from_profile_with_quant_caps` static rank cap; `from_profile` delegates.

### Verification (build env `OPENSSL_NO_VENDOR=1 LIBTORCH_USE_PYTORCH=1 LIBTORCH_BYPASS_VERSION_CHECK=1`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` = pytorch libtorch)
- `cargo build -p hyprstream --lib` — clean.
- `cargo test -p hyprstream --lib training::` — **82 passed, 0 failed** (incl. 10 new reducer tests):
  - `test_order_independent` (permute contributors → identical ΔW)

author: slepp
body:
## Summary

Direct construction of `#[opaque]` handle types (e.g. `Handle {}`) now produces a clean `E_OPAQUE_CONSTRUCT` diagnostic at the checker layer instead of falling through to a misleading `E_NOT_YET_IMPLEMENTED: MIR lowering for record type '...' (not registered in field-order table)` error with a "checker bug" note. Opaque handles are pointer-shaped runtime resources with no user-visible fields; they carry no constructible record layout and are produced exclusively by their stdlib FFI constructors. The check short-circuits before any `lookup_type_def` call with a message that names the type and explains how to obtain one.

Changes: `hew-types/src/check/expressions.rs` adds the opaque-guard before the struct-init lookup path; `hew-types/src/error.rs` adds `TypeErrorKind::OpaqueDirectConstruct`; `hew-types/src/check/tests.rs` adds unit coverage for the new variant; the `opaque_handle_construct` vertical-slice reject fixture is updated to assert `E_OPAQUE_CONSTRUCT` is present in the output, not just that `hew check` exits non-zero.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p hew-types -- opaque`: all new unit cases pass
- `tests/vertical-slice/run.sh` opaque reject fixture: exits non-zero AND `grep -q E_OPAQUE_CONSTRUCT` passes
- Preflight: ready-to-push
- Cross-ecosystem review: accepted

## Out of scope

- Display formatting and help-text links for `E_OPAQUE_CONSTRUCT` — handle type names in diagnostics are already self-documenting and no issue is open for this yet
- Extending the opaque guard to other expression forms (e.g. tuple-struct init) — opaque handles are only reachable via record-init syntax today

## Summary

## Key Changes

- **New unified screen** (`ProfilesContextsScreen.kt`): Hosts both `SettingsViewModel` (profiles) and `ContextsViewModel` (rules); orchestrates import/export, profile management, and context-rule editing via modal.

- **Extracted reusable bodies**:

author: wrlee567
body:
Addresses five findings from a backend code review.

## Changes

| Finding | What changed |
|---|---|
| **P1** No auth / tenant isolation | JWT bearer auth (HS256, PyJWT) with an `org_id` claim. New `app.auth` (`create_access_token` + `current_org` dependency). All `/api/*` routes except the public trust center now require a token; every CCF, vendor, and AI-governance query is scoped by `org_id`, created rows are stamped with it. Unauthenticated → 401, cross-tenant resource access → 404. |
| **P1** Prod seeds demo data | New `SEED_DEMO_DATA` flag (default false). Reference data (frameworks, controls, ISO 42001 catalog) seeds under `SEED_ON_STARTUP`; sample vendors + demo AI records are gated behind the new flag. AI seeder split into `seed_ai_reference` / `seed_ai_demo`. `render.yaml` sets it false. |
| **P2** `create_all` on startup | New `AUTO_CREATE_SCHEMA` (defaults off in production). Added Alembic baseline `0001_initial_schema` (dialect-correct, incl. JSONB); Dockerfile runs `alembic upgrade head` before boot. |
| **P2** Frontend hides API failures | `getOrDemo` only falls back to demo data when `VITE_DEMO_MODE=true`; otherwise API errors propagate so the UI can show a real error state. |
| **P2** Loose payload validation | Vendor questionnaire answers validated by question type (boolean / single_select / text); AI classification rejects unknown keys and non-boolean values (so `"false"` can't flip a risk tier). |

Also fixes a pre-existing duplicate `Vendor` import that was failing ruff in CI.

## Verification
- Backend: 108 tests pass, coverage 96.6% (gate 70%), `ruff check app tests` clean, bandit clean
- Frontend: `npm run lint` + `npm run build` clean

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
The frontend sends no `Authorization` header and has no login flow, so with auth enforced it will get 401s against the real API in production. Wiring auth into the frontend is a separate feature and is intentionally out of scope here.

author: prosolis
body:
Matrix clients struggle to load threads that grow too deep. This tracks the ISO week each deal thread belongs to and creates a fresh thread root when the week changes, so Game Deals, DLC Deals, and Epic Free Games threads reset every Monday.

- Thread titles include the week's Monday.
- Existing threads roll over once on deploy.

author: sparlit
body:
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Launched Phase 1 of Autonomous AutoTrader with multi-agent architecture for intelligent trading decisions. * Added global dashboard for real-time monitoring, strategy signals, and performance metrics. * Implemented risk management with news event awareness, session filtering, and drawdown protection. * Introduced position management with trailing stops and partial profit-taking at 1R. * Added comprehensive technical analysis including market structure detection, volatility analysis, and candlestick pattern recognition. * **Documentation** * Simplified README with quick-start guide and technical overview. * Added project roadmap outlining three development phases. * Finalized Phase 1 completion checklist and handover documentation. * **Configuration** * Added news schedule and trading symbols configuration files.

Greptile Summary

 This PR introduces the MVP of the Chart Analyst Autotrader, adding a full Python trading engine with multi-timeframe market analysis, risk management, a TCP bridge server, and MQL5 Expert Advisors for MetaTrader 5 integration. - **New execution layer** (`ledger.py`, `manager.py`, `risk_manager.py`): tracks trades in SQLite, manages positions with trailing stops and partial TPs, and validates trades against session, news, drawdown, and daily-count limits — but the `PositionManager` crashes at runtime due to a missing method name, the entry-price approximation is built on point-distance values instead of actual prices, and the daily trade counter is never incremented. - **New analysis engine** (`brains/`, `analyst/`): a `ConsensusEngine` combines SMC price-action, RSI/ATR indicators, and VSA volatility in a thread-pooled pipeline to produce a scored BUY/SELL/WAIT decision per tick. - **New bridge & orchestration** (`bridge/server.py`, `hive/coordinator.py`): async TCP server routes messages from MT5 to the coordinator, which applies veto logic and dispatches analysis to a `ProcessPoolExecutor`.

Confidence Score: 2/5

 Not safe to merge in current form — position management crashes on every active trade tick, and risk controls have two silent failures that could allow overtrading with incorrect stop/TP levels. The `PositionManager.monitor_and_manage` calls `self.ledger.get_active_trades(symbol)` which does not exist on `TradeLedger`; this raises `AttributeError` on every data push when any position is open, meaning trailing stops and partial TPs never execute. The `trade["sl"]` and `trade["tp"]` stored in the DB are point distances not price levels, so all R-multiple and stop-adjustment calculations produce nonsensical values. The daily trade counter is never incremented, leaving the 5-trade daily cap inoperative. Failed-trade cache pollution further corrupts the correlation-exposure check. src/python/execution/manager.py and src/python/execution/ledger.py need the most attention; src/python/execution/risk_manager.py needs the daily-counter wiring reviewed.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/python/execution/manager.py | Calls non-existent `ledger.get_active_trades()` (should be `get_active_trades_db`), causing a guaranteed AttributeError crash; entry price approximation uses point distances instead of actual prices, making all position management calculations wrong. | | src/python/execution/risk_manager.py | Daily trade limit check exists but `daily_trades` is never incremented anywhere in the codebase and has no daily reset; the 5-trade cap is effectively dead code. | | src/python/execution/ledger.py | Failed trades (ticket=0) are inserted into the active trades cache without status filtering, polluting correlation-exposure checks and silently overwriting prior failure records. | | src/python/hive/coordinator.py | Core orchestration logic for message routing, trade decisions, and position management is well-structured; uses deprecated `asyncio.get_event_loop()` inside an async context. | | src/python/bridge/server.py | Adds latency stats tracking and a 16 KB read buffer; overall async TCP bridge logic is clean and well-structured. | | src/python/brains/specialized.py | New specialized brain types (HTF/LTF analysis, correlation, context); `DecisionBrain.process` and `LTFTriggerBrain.process` are both unimplemented placeholders. | | src/python/brains/consensus.py | Multi-analyst consensus engine with vectorised scoring; thread pool used correctly for parallel sub-tasks. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% sequenceDiagram participant MT5 as MT5 (MQL5 EA) participant Bridge as BridgeServer participant Coord as HiveCoordinator participant Risk as RiskManager participant Pool as ProcessPoolExecutor participant Worker as StrategyWorker participant Ledger as TradeLedger participant PosMan as PositionManager MT5->>Bridge: JSON message (TCP, newline-delimited) Bridge->>Coord: on_message_cb(client_id, message) alt "t == HB (heartbeat)" Coord->>Ledger: update_peak_equity(equity) Coord-->>MT5: HB_ACK else "t == DP (data push)" Coord->>Risk: is_session_active() / is_news_safe() Coord->>Pool: run_in_executor(process_task, raw_msg) Pool->>Worker: update_and_analyze(data) Worker-->>Pool: analysis (action, score, atr, ...) Pool-->>Coord: analysis result Coord->>PosMan: monitor_and_manage(symbol, price, atr) Note over PosMan,Ledger: Calls get_active_trades() — method does not exist Coord->>Risk: validate_trade(symbol, action, equity, atr) alt trade approved Coord->>Ledger: record_intent(symbol, action, lots, sl_pts, tp_pts) Coord-->>MT5: "DEC {act: BUY/SELL, lts, sl_p, tp_p}" else vetoed Coord-->>MT5: "DEC {act: WAIT}" end else "t == T_ACK (execution confirmation)" Coord->>Ledger: update_execution(id, ticket, status) Coord-->>MT5: ACK else "t == SYNC (position reconciliation)" Coord->>Ledger: get_active_trades_db(symbol) Coord->>Ledger: close_trade(ticket) if not in MT5 Coord-->>MT5: SYNC_ACK end ``` ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {"darkMode": true, "background": "#0d1117", "primaryColor": "#21262d", "primaryTextColor": "#e6edf3", "primaryBorderColor": "#8b949e", "lineColor": "#8b949e", "textColor": "#e6edf3", "edgeLabelBackground": "#161b22", "actorBkg": "#21262d", "actorBorder": "#8b949e", "actorTextColor": "#e6edf3", "actorLineColor": "#8b949e", "signalColor": "#8b949e", "signalTextColor": "#e6edf3", "noteBkgColor": "#373320", "noteBorderColor": "#d4a72c", "noteTextColor": "#f0e6c0", "labelBoxBkgColor": "#21262d", "labelBoxBorderColor": "#8b949e", "labelTextColor": "#e6edf3", "loopTextColor": "#e6edf3", "activationBkgColor": "#30363d", "activationBorderColor": "#8b949e"}}}%% sequenceDiagram participant MT5 as MT5 (MQL5 EA) participant Bridge as BridgeServer participant Coord as HiveCoordinator participant Risk as RiskManager participant Pool as ProcessPoolExecutor participant Worker as StrategyWorker participant Ledger as TradeLedger participant PosMan as PositionManager MT5->>Bridge: JSON message (TCP, newline-delimited) Bridge->>Coord: on_message_cb(client_id, message) alt "t == HB (heartbeat)" Coord->>Ledger: update_peak_equity(equity) Coord-->>MT5: HB_ACK else "t == DP (data push)" Coord->>Risk: is_session_active() / is_news_safe()

author: kevinjohn
body:
## What
Wishlist item 6: any day where a person is **over capacity** now gets a **clearly red background**.

- **Threshold (review focus):** "over" is **strictly greater** — `allocated > available`. Exactly **at** capacity (e.g. 8h booked / 8h available) is **NOT** red; just-over (9h/8h) and any work on a zero-capacity day are red. This predicate already existed and is unchanged — the item was really about making the visual unmistakably red.
- **The red:** new theme token `--color-danger-cell` (~50% danger in light → `rgb(251,158,161)`, ~60% in dark → `rgb(147,73,86)`), replacing the faint ~12% tint that didn't read as red. Keeps the `border-danger` top band.
- **a11y:** the over cell carries no text and allocation bars paint their own opaque WCAG-tuned fills on top, so the saturated red is **axe-safe** (light + dark green); the non-colour cues (`title="Overbooked"`, sr-only "Over capacity on N days", the border band) remain.

## Also
- Corrects stale docs/comments (CLAUDE.md, DECISIONS.md, code) that described the per-day over-marker as "work on a zero-capacity day" — it has always been `allocated > available`; the three over-signals stay separate.
- Fixes a **latent e2e bug**: Chromium serialises `color-mix(oklab)` as `oklab(...)`, so the prior colour assertion parsed L/a/b as fake rgb — it now reads true sRGB via canvas and gates real red saturation (`r − max(g,b) > 60`).
- **Per-day only** (a week reads red via its over-days); whether a distinct *week-aggregate* red band is wanted is flagged in `NEEDS-INPUT.md` for the owner.

## Verification
- `npm run gate` green — tsc + eslint + **762** vitest + build. (No `shared/`/`server/` — server gate N/A.)
- `npm run e2e` green — **144** Playwright (Chromium), incl. axe light+dark and the tightened red-background assertion.
- Boundary pinned: `8v8 → over:false`, `9v8 → over:true`, zero-cap-with-work → over; render-layer test asserts the red bg renders only for over days. Visual oracle (screenshots) confirms a clear rose-red (light) / dark red (dark).

Reviewed across boundary/correctness, redness/theme/a11y, and test-integrity; the first pass caught that the initial `danger-soft` swap was still a faint pink (acceptance unmet) — strengthened to a genuine red and re-verified.

author: jaiafoster
body:
## Summary

Two bugs found downstream of the account-scoping fix (PR #72, confirmed working — 3 option positions now fetched). The detector receives the correct raw data but fails to classify it.

### Bug 1 — Vertical leg side inference misses real Robinhood fields

`_infer_robinhood_option_side()` in `robinhood_provider.py:1163` checked keys (`side`, `direction`, `position_type`, etc.) that **don't exist** in real Robinhood option position payloads. The actual direction field is `clearing_direction` (and/or `clearing_intraday_direction`).

**Result:** All 3 legs got `side="unknown"` → `longs` and `shorts` both empty → `if not longs or not shorts: continue` in `_detect_vertical_spreads()` silently dropped every vertical.

**Confirmed from production logs:**
```
sample raw option position keys: ['account', 'account_number', 'average_price', 'chain_id',
'chain_symbol', 'clearing_cost_basis', 'clearing_direction', 'clearing_intraday_direction', ...]
```
None of the previously checked keys (`side`, `direction`, `position_type`, etc.) are present.

**Fix:** Added `clearing_direction` and `clearing_intraday_direction` to the key list. The existing substring checks (`"buy"` → long, `"sell"` → short) should match. Added diagnostic logging when side still resolves to `"unknown"` so the exact field values are captured if further mapping is needed.

### Bug 2 — Pickle path malformed, session never persists

Production error log:
```
Error during login verification: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'/root/.tokens/robinhood/app/data/rh_user_1.pickle'
```

`robin_stocks.login()` has two params: `pickle_path` (base directory override) and `pickle_name` (appended to `"robinhood"` for filename). The code was passing a full path (`app/data/rh_user_1`) as `pickle_name`, causing robin_stocks to concatenate its default directory (`~/.tokens`) with the path-containing name.

**Fix:** Use `pickle_path=data_dir` to set the directory, `pickle_name=f"_user_{user_id}"` as a simple suffix. Resulting file: `{DATA_DIR}/robinhood_user_{user_id}.pickle`. Updated `session_cache_available()` to check the matching path.

## Files changed
- `app/providers/robinhood_provider.py` — `clearing_direction`/`clearing_intraday_direction` added to side inference key list + diagnostic log
- `app/services/broker_provider.py` — both login calls fixed: `pickle_path` for directory, `pickle_name` for suffix only
- `app/services/robinhood_queue.py` — `session_cache_available()` checks correct pickle path

## What was NOT touched
- `app/services/open_options_service.py` — `_detect_vertical_spreads()` grouping/pairing logic is correct
- Account-scoped options fetch loop (PR #72) — confirmed working, do not modify

## Test plan
- [ ] Deploy and trigger `/api/user/run` — check Railway logs for `[side_inference]` diagnostic output (should NOT fire if `clearing_direction` mapping works)
- [ ] If `[side_inference] unknown side` DOES appear: log shows the actual `clearing_direction` values for manual mapping adjustment
- [ ] `options_count` > 0, `has_open_verticals: true` on `/api/advisor/positions`
- [ ] Pickle error (`/root/.tokens/robinhood/app/data/...`) no longer in logs
- [ ] `session_cache_available: true` on `/api/user/status` after successful run
- [ ] Second run completes fast without fresh device approval (pickle persisted)
- [ ] FF dry_run confirmed, trade_execution disabled

author: bawes
body:
## Root Cause
The Next.js web server crashes under concurrent test load in CI. With 2 workers per shard × 4 shards = 8 workers hitting the server simultaneously, the server runs out of memory and dies mid-run, causing cascading ECONNREFUSED failures on all remaining tests in that shard.

## Fix
Reduced Playwright workers from 2 to 1 in CI. This halves the concurrent request load on the web server, preventing OOM crashes.

## Impact
This addresses ~30% of E2E flaky failures (the ECONNREFUSED category). Combined with the PrismaClientValidationError fix (PR #1784, already merged), we've fixed ~50% of E2E CI failures.

## Verification
- tsc --noEmit: ✅ pass

- E2E CI will validate on this PR

author: hhugo
body:
Fixes the remaining `wasm_of_ocaml` / WASI CI failure on `master`. After #2352 stopped the `prefix_match` crash from aborting the WASI test run, three `tests-jsoo/test_unix.ml` tests turned out not to pass under node's WASI runtime.

## 1. `empty path is ENOENT` — was returning `ok` under WASI
`d27c7a42f` left an empty path empty in `make_absolute`, intending it to "match no preopen" and fail with ENOENT. But an empty path **does** match the current-directory preopen (its normalized prefix is empty), so `stat ""`/`open ""` silently resolved to the cwd under the Wasm runtime — unlike native and the JS backend (#2354).

Reject the empty path in `wasi_resolve_path`, before `make_absolute`, where the original argument is still available (`make_absolute` would turn `""` into `current_dir`, indistinguishable from `"."`). The `fd=-1` result flows through the existing not-found path, so Unix ops raise `Unix_error(ENOENT)` and Sys ops raise `Sys_error`, each matching native.

Validated under the `wasi-with-native-effects` profile locally: `Unix.stat "" → ENOENT`.

## 2. `is_directory follows symlinks` / `utimes follows symlinks` — EPERM under WASI
Both create symlinks whose **target is an absolute path** (`Filename.temp_file`). WASI's capability model forbids that, so `Unix.symlink` raises `EPERM`. Moved them to `test_unix_symlink.ml`, in a library disabled under the wasi profiles (and quickjs, like the other Unix tests). Symlink tests with **relative** targets work under WASI and stay in `test_unix.ml`.

(The earlier `prefix_match` crash was fixed in #2352; the JS-backend half of the empty-path fix is #2354.)

author: dotcoocoo
body:
## Summary

Closes a further set of concurrency races where a fulfillment or customer-data action read a row, checked its status in application code, and then performed an irreversible side-effect (open an inventory hold, create shipments, restock received stock, create an order, reparent customer records, requeue a print job, mint child carts) before an unconditional update committed — so two concurrent calls could both pass the check and both perform the side-effect. Each now claims the transition with a single conditional update and performs the side-effect only when that claim wins, reverting the claim if the side-effect then fails so a row is never stranded. Approving an exchange opens its replacement hold once; executing a split-shipment plan creates the parcels once; recording a partial purchase-order receipt restocks each line once (claimed per line); completing a pick list creates its shipment once; converting or launching a pre-order creates the order once and a reservation can't oversell its cap; merging or rolling back a customer reparents the records once; an impersonation notice, a duplicate-suggestion link, a print-job retry, and a cart split each happen once. Behavior for a single sequential caller is unchanged.

- [x] `node test/smoke.js`
- [x] codebase-patterns + asset-manifest + changelog checks
- [x] gitleaks
- [ ] CI green

## Summary
Extend audio file loading to support more formats (MP3, OGG, FLAC, etc.) by adding an ffmpeg fallback when soundfile cannot decode a file. This allows the transcribe command to work with a wider variety of audio formats.

## Key Changes
- Renamed `load_wav()` to `load_audio()` to better reflect its expanded capabilities
- Created `load_audio()` as the main entry point that tries soundfile first, then falls back to ffmpeg if available
- Extracted soundfile logic into `_load_with_soundfile()` helper function
- Added new `_load_with_ffmpeg()` function that pipes audio through ffmpeg to decode unsupported formats
- Maintained backwards compatibility by keeping `load_wav` as an alias to `load_audio`
- Updated CLI and documentation to reflect support for multiple audio formats (WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, etc.)

## Implementation Details
- The fallback mechanism catches exceptions from soundfile and attempts ffmpeg decoding if the binary is available
- If both methods fail, a helpful error message suggests installing ffmpeg or upgrading soundfile
- ffmpeg is invoked with specific flags to output mono float32 PCM at the target sample rate
- Audio data is read from ffmpeg's stdout and converted to numpy array

author: chance6706
body:
## Context

**Thread 2 of three** addressing the intuition that the system lacks the precision of natural systems. Thread 1 found the constants are mostly independent (no hidden lattice). This thread is where the *fractal/scale-free* instinct actually cashes out: the episodic forgetting curve was a single exponential `e^(-λt)`; **human forgetting fits a power law better** (Wixted & Ebbesen 1991), and a power law is **scale-free** — self-similar across timescales. That's the recursive quality the project was missing.

It replaces the decay term with `D(t) = (1 + t/τ)^(-β)` and — per a direct request — **establishes a standard for flagging deliberate deviations** (from pure math derivations *and* from standard lexicon connotations).

## The math (generalizes, never contradicts)

- `forgetting_shape` (β, default **2**) is a new **free** parameter; `decay_tau` is **derived** as `halflife/(2^(1/β)−1)` to pin `D(0)=1` and `D(29 days)=0.5` for **every** β.
- The exponential is recovered exactly in the β→∞ limit (verified to 6 decimals); `decay_lambda` is retained as that limit rate, so the Thread-1 locks stay green.
- `salience.accessibility` swaps `exp(-λt)` → `(1+t/τ)^(-β)`. **No DB migration** — accessibility is computed live from stored `(s0, timestamp, access_count)`.

## Behavior change is tail-only (verified)

Every test/validation corpus consolidates within ~1 h of each turn (`drift_trajectory.py:358`) or at age≈0, where `D(age) ≈ 1` for **both** curves and temporal eviction never fires. So gist formation, the 0.00 trait overlap, and the **self-validating drift harness are curve-independent** — confirmed: the harness exits 0 with every detector (EROSION/THRASH/DIFFERENTIATION) firing. The deviation lives entirely in the long tail:

| | exponential (old) | power-law (new) |
|---|---|---|
| 1-year retention | 0.016% | 2.6% |
| floored catastrophe (S0=3) evicts | day 142 | day 313 |
| low-salience noise evicts | day 46 | day 51 |

Reproduce: `python tools/forgetting_ab.py` (captured in `docs/validation/forgetting_curve/`).

## The standard (per request)

`docs/DEVIATIONS.md` is a new register: **whenever CDMS departs from a pure derivation or uses a term against its typical connotation, flag it in-line and register it** (standard form → what we do → why → what we disclaim). Seeded with:
- **Math:** power-law forgetting (M1), activity-based gist decay (M2).
- **Lexicon** (from the external review): personality, scar, ego, trusted/untrusted, genotype/phenotype — each with its scoped meaning and the connotation we explicitly disclaim.

`CLAUDE.md` #11 makes flagging the rule going forward; `docs/PARAMETER_BASIS.md` is the companion discipline for constants.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_forgetting_curve.py tests/test_parameter_basis.py tests/test_salience.py tests/test_consolidate.py` — pass (anchors across β, monotone, heavier tail, faster early decay, β→∞ limit, eviction-horizon closed form, robustness).
- Full offline suite — pass; drift harness exits 0, all detectors fire.
- Default β=2 is overridable via `CDMS_FORGETTING_SHAPE`.

author: mvillmow
body:
## Summary

New skill documenting how to diagnose and fix Docker containers accumulating gigabytes of log data in their overlay2 writable layer.

- Traefik v2.2 on HomelabOS (apollo) accumulated 76.3 GB over 5 years in its writable layer
- Root cause: log filePaths in traefik.yaml pointed to internal container paths, not bind-mounted to host
- Fix: add bind-mount in docker-compose.yml, recreate container (drops writable layer)
- 72 GB freed; container healthy; logs now on host and manageable by logrotate

## Verification Level

**verified-local**

Executed on apollo. Container came back healthy, logs confirmed writing to host path. CI validation pending.

## Key Findings

**What Worked**:
- `docker diff <container>` reveals files added inside container vs image — the right tool for this diagnosis
- `docker stop && docker rm` (not `docker restart`) drops the writable layer and reclaims disk
- Bind-mounting the log directory in docker-compose.yml routes logs to host filesystem

**What Failed**:
- `docker restart` → does not drop writable layer, no disk reclaimed
- Host `find` for large files → files inside container writable layer invisible on host
- `docker system prune` → only removes stopped containers, not running ones
- Relying on daemon.json log-opts → only covers stdout/stderr, not internal file writes

## Test Plan

- [ ] Validate with `python3 scripts/validate_plugins.py`
- [ ] Verify markdownlint passes
- [ ] Verify skill appears in marketplace with docker/traefik/overlay2 tags
- [ ] Test skill discovery with keywords: docker, writable-layer, log-bloat, disk, traefik

## Summary
Final slice of the encounter-video import feature — the **clinician-facing upload UI** for VID-01…04. A clinician uploads a recorded encounter, watches it process, and reviews the produced note in the existing `/portal/notes/[id]` screen. Matches the backend's single presigned-PUT, clinician-only `/me/video-imports` surface; **inert until the backend `video_import_enabled` flag is on** (calls 404 while dark). Plan commit: `docs: plan for VID-05`.

## What changed
- **Web**:
  - `lib/portal-api.ts` — `createVideoImport` / `processVideoImport` / `getVideoImportStatus` typed `fetchWithAuth` wrappers + types.
  - `components/portal/VideoImportClient.tsx` — phased UI (form → uploading → processing → redirect): drag-drop + file picker (mp4/mov/webm, ≤2 GB) with inline validation, **required consent-attestation** checkbox, metadata (specialty, encounter type [`doctor_patient` / `doctor_team_patient`], note language), raw-S3 PUT via XHR with upload progress, processing stepper polling status (~4 s), hard-nav to the note review screen on completion.

Backlog VID-05. Completes the user-facing path. Reuses the existing `NoteReviewClient` for the result (origin-agnostic) and the `fetchWithAuth` bearer/refresh plumbing.

author: asigdel29
body:
## Problem
Session replay is a blank **white screen**: the experience is a full-screen React Three Fiber WebGL canvas, and rrweb does not record `<canvas>` content unless canvas recording is explicitly enabled — so the replay captures only the (near-empty) DOM overlay.

## Fix (code)
- **`src/lib/analytics.js`** — enable PostHog canvas capture: `session_recording.captureCanvas: { canvasFps: 4, canvasQuality: "0.4" }`. The canvas is recorded as periodic images; modest fps/quality keep the upload light.
- **`src/Experience/Experience.jsx`** — set `gl={{ ..., preserveDrawingBuffer: true }}` so the WebGL buffer can be snapshotted; without it the captured frames read back blank (a black/white frame).

## ⚠️ Dashboard step (required — can't be done in code)
Canvas recording must **also** be toggled on in the PostHog project:
**Settings → Replay → "Capture canvas" / canvas recording → enable**
(direct link: https://us.posthog.com/settings/project-replay#replay).
Until that is on, PostHog will not store canvas frames even with this client config. Once enabled, new sessions will replay the 3D world.

## Verification
`npm run lint`, `npm test` (79), `npm run build` pass. After deploy + enabling the dashboard toggle, record a fresh session and confirm the replay shows the world instead of white. (Existing/old replays stay white — only new sessions are affected.)

Closes #109

author: daniel3303
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #3845. `RecipientNameNormalizer.Normalize` is documented to strip trailing legal-entity suffixes and return null "when nothing meaningful remains", but a pure legal suffix that is itself ≥ 4 characters (e.g. `Corporation`, `Company`, `Limited`) survived as a generic key.
- Such a key would exact-match any other entity normalizing to the same word, risking a federal contract being attached to the wrong company — the false positive the conservative, never-fuzzy design avoids.

## Code changes

- `src/Equibles.GovernmentContracts.HostedService/Services/RecipientNameNormalizer.cs` — the trailing-suffix loop was guarded by `tokens.Count > 1`, so it never removed the last remaining token. Changed to `tokens.Count > 0` so a name that is nothing but suffixes reduces to an empty key and falls through to null. Multi-word names keep their real tokens (the loop stops at the first non-suffix), so existing behavior is unchanged.
- `tests/Equibles.UnitTests/GovernmentContracts/RecipientNameNormalizerSuffixOnlyTests.cs` — un-skipped and broadened the GH-3845 repro into a theory across `Corporation`, `Company`, `Limited`, `Incorporated`, and `The Company`; fails before the fix, passes after. Full module suite (38 tests) green.

author: janelholm
body:
Fixes #58.

## Problem
New or "parked" subscriptions that Cost Management has not onboarded yet return HTTP 404 with a **string-coded** `error.code` of `NotFound`:

```
GtmDimensionDataProvider.GetAzureSubscriptionsById returns null or empty list for id: <subscriptionId>
```

The CostManagement rule set tolerated the numeric `404` ("created recently") and two specific `NotFound` messages, but not this one. The call therefore fell through to the generic `Stop` handler and **aborted the entire run** (observed in Azure Governance Visualizer `-DoAzureConsumption` with a parked CSP subscription).

## Fix
Treat this `NotFound` message like the existing numeric-404 "created recently" case: skip the subscription and return an empty collection (`action = 'returnCollection'`).

Changes were made under `pwsh/module/dev` and the module was rebuilt with `buildModule.ps1 -test`, so `pwsh/module/build` is regenerated accordingly.

## Notes
- No version bump (rule-set tolerance change only).
- Script parses cleanly; style matches the surrounding CostManagement handlers.

body:
## Problem
Bot je tvrdio *„danas je 18. lipnja 2026."* iako je bilo **20. lipnja** — pa je krivo računao „za koliko dana počinje Ljeto valpovačko".

## Uzrok
Prompt **nije sadržavao današnji datum**. Kad korisnik pita za vrijeme, model je uzeo najbliži datum iz konteksta — a to je **„provjereno: 18.06.2026."** uz plakat (datum kad je izvor zadnji put dohvaćen/ingestiran) — i od njega računao „danas".

## Lijek
- **`lib/prompt.ts`**:
  - `todayHr()` — današnji datum u **Europe/Zagreb** (DD.MM.GGGG), računa se **po svakom upitu** (`buildUserPrompt` se poziva u ruti za svaki zahtjev, pa je `new Date()` uvijek aktualan).
  - `buildUserPrompt` sada na vrh poruke dodaje `Današnji datum: …`.
  - **Pravilo 8** u sistemskom promptu: za izračune vremena koristiti ISKLJUČIVO navedeni današnji datum, a **nikada** „provjereno" datume izvora kao „danas".

## Provjera
`todayHr()` → `20.06.2026.` ✅ · `npm run typecheck` ✅ · `npm run build` ✅

Nakon merge, pitanje „za koliko dana počinje Ljeto valpovačko" treba dati točan broj (od stvarnog današnjeg datuma do 22.06.).

## What

The unit-system layer the international slice needs, built so it **cannot regress the live US product**. The record stays °F internally; cards format through pure converters whose **imperial branch is the exact identity**.

- **`src/lib/units.js`** (new, pure/dep-free) — `convTemp`, `convTempDelta`, `convDist` + unit labels (`tempUnit`/`tempRateUnit`/`distUnit`) + `fmt*` conveniences. Imperial in → same number out, byte-for-byte. `convTempDelta` scales a per-decade slope by 5/9 with **no** 32° offset, and is a separate function from `convTemp` so the classic "converted a trend with the absolute formula" bug is unrepresentable at the call site.
- **`ui.jsx`** — `UnitsContext` (default `"imperial"`) + `useUnits()`. **`CityDashboard`** provides `unitsOf(city)` to the subtree. A city opts into metric with `units: "metric"`; every current (US) city omits it → **no behavior change**.
- **`tests/units.test.mjs`** (new, plain node, wired into CI's `build` job) — pins the conversion math: imperial identity, °F→°C offset+scale, the delta rule, miles→km, and the formatters. The render smoke test checks that cards *mount*, not that temperature strings are correct, so this is the net under the math.
- **`GlobalContextCard`** — the migrated **reference** card (chart bars + tooltip + prose trends via `convTempDelta`/`tempUnit`). Imperial output verified byte-identical (`+1.2°F per decade`, bars `0.36`, tooltip `°F`); published-figure citations keep their cited units.
- **`WORLDWIDE.md`** — foundation marked done + the staged per-card rollout recipe.

## Why this shape

Temperature is woven through ~25 card files in prose, chart labels, tooltips, and constants — a genuinely prose-aware migration, not a mechanical swap. So this PR lands the **get-it-right-once core** (conversion math + context + the imperial-identity safety property, all CI-tested) and proves it on one reference card. The remaining ~24 cards are a **staged rollout** best finished alongside the first metric city, so each card's *metric* output is visually verified — the converters already guarantee the US side can't move.

## Safety

- Imperial is the converter identity ⇒ the live US product is unchanged by construction.
- Any mistake in a future card migration can therefore only affect **metric** output.
- `units.test.mjs` gates the math in CI; `build` + `render` gate that cards still compile and mount.

## Validation

- `node tests/units.test.mjs` → **UNITS TEST PASSED** (local) — now a CI step.
- `npm run build` → clean (683 modules).
- Render smoke (browser) runs in CI (playwright not available in this sandbox).

author: williamhuynh
body:
## Problem

Every authenticated page navigation was running 5+ sequential Appwrite network calls before rendering anything, causing the 2-3 second delay.

## Root cause

Two issues in the critical path:

**1. Sequential membership + workspace fetch in `getApiContext`**
`listDocuments(WORKSPACE_MEMBERS)` and `getDocument(WORKSPACES)` were running sequentially, but both only need `activeWorkspaceId` (known after `account.getPrefs`). One was idle while the other ran.

**2. Redundant `getWorkspaceById` call in the layout**
`getApiContext` already fetches the workspace document to read `plan` and `featureOverrides`. The layout then called `getWorkspaceById` again (a second `getDocument` for the same record) just to get `homeCurrency`.

## Fix

1. Parallelise membership check + workspace fetch in `getApiContext` with `Promise.all`
2. Add `currency` to `ApiContext`, return it from `getApiContext`
3. Remove `getWorkspaceById` from the layout — use `context.currency` directly

## Before vs after

```
Before: session → [user, prefs] → membership → workspace → getWorkspaceById → [nav, sidebar]
After:  session → [user, prefs] → [membership, workspace] → [nav, sidebar]
```

Saves ~2 sequential Appwrite round-trips (~300-600ms) per page navigation.

## Verification
- TypeScript: 0 errors
- Tests: 412/412 pass
- 5 test files updated to include `currency: "AUD"` in mock ApiContext objects

author: seonghobae
body:
🎨 **Palette: Improve keyboard focus management for editors and modals**

### 💡 What
This PR adds focus management to the application's modals (the Task Editor and the Gantt Chart view). When these modals open, focus is shifted into them. Crucially, when they are closed or saved, focus is restored to the element that originally triggered them.

### 🎯 Why
Without this, when a user opened an editor and then saved or canceled it, focus would drop to the start of the document (or `body`), requiring keyboard or screen reader users to tab all the way back through the interface to get to where they were.

### ♿ Accessibility
This directly improves the experience for screen reader users and users navigating via keyboard. It adheres to the fundamental accessibility pattern of returning focus after a modal interaction is completed.

### 📸 Before/After
*(Playwright visual verification complete)*
- Before: Opening editor -> close -> focus jumps to document body.
- After: Opening editor -> focus moves to first input -> close -> focus returns to the "최상위 작업 추가" or "편집" button that triggered it.

author: justinbeckwith
body:
## Summary

Fix Yarn Plug'n'Play dependency auto-loading for nested Zorilla plugins.

`@zorilla/puppeteer-extra` previously resolved every auto-loaded plugin dependency from its own package context. That is too broad for strict package managers: when a stealth evasion declares `user-preferences`, and `user-preferences` declares `user-data-dir`, those imports should be resolved from the declaring plugin package, not from `@zorilla/puppeteer-extra` or the application root.

This keeps the normal consumer contract intact: users can install `@zorilla/puppeteer-extra` plus `@zorilla/puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth`, and nested plugin dependencies are loaded through the packages that actually declare them.

Resolves #102.

## Changes

- Track the construction module URL for plugin instances.
- Resolve auto-loaded dependencies from the plugin that declared them when Yarn PnP is active.
- Preserve the existing workspace-relative fallback for normal monorepo development.
- Add focused tests for PnP issuer-based resolution and existing dependency loading.
- Add a changeset for `@zorilla/puppeteer-extra` and `@zorilla/puppeteer-extra-plugin`.

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @zorilla/puppeteer-extra-plugin build`
- `pnpm --filter @zorilla/puppeteer-extra build`
- `pnpm --dir packages/puppeteer-extra-plugin test`
- `pnpm --dir packages/puppeteer-extra exec vitest run src/dependency-resolution.test.ts src/dependency-loading.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec biome check packages/puppeteer-extra/src/dependency-resolution.ts packages/puppeteer-extra/src/dependency-resolution.test.ts packages/puppeteer-extra/src/index.ts packages/puppeteer-extra-plugin/src/index.ts packages/puppeteer-extra-plugin/src/index.test.ts .changeset/pnp-plugin-dependencies.md`

author: t-cordoba
body:
This PR addresses the token expiration issues that were causing users to lose work when filling long forms. Sessions were silently expiring after 15 minutes of idle activity, and when users submitted a form after that window the request would fail with a 401, clear the session, and redirect to login — discarding everything they had typed.

### Reactive 401 retry (`auth.interceptor.ts`):

- Added a `catchError` handler to the admin auth interceptor that catches 401 responses, triggers a token refresh, and transparently retries the original request with the new token — mirroring the pattern already in place in the guest interceptor.
- Removed the `req.headers.has('Authorization')` early-exit condition that was silently bypassing this entire path for any request made through repositories that set auth headers manually (e.g. `PropertyRepositoryImpl`). This was the root cause of form submissions failing without a refresh attempt.
- Exported `refreshAccessToken` and `getJwtPayload` from the interceptor so they can be shared with the scheduler without duplicating logic.

### Proactive background refresh (`token-refresh-scheduler.service.ts`, `app.ts`):

- Added `TokenRefreshSchedulerService`, a root-level service that reads the JWT `exp` claim on login and schedules a silent refresh 120 seconds before the token expires, so the session stays alive even during idle periods with no HTTP activity.
- The scheduler reuses the interceptor's `refreshInFlight$` deduplication guard, so if a request and the scheduler both try to refresh at the same time only one HTTP call is made.
- The service is eagerly initialized in `App` so it starts watching from the first moment the app boots, including when a user already has a stored session from a previous visit.

author: mvillmow
body:
## Summary

New skill documenting how PCP (Performance Co-Pilot) pmlogger silently
accumulates unbounded archive files on Debian/PureOS systems.

- pmlogger writes ~1.9 GB/day to `/var/log/pcp/pmlogger/<hostname>/` with no retention policy
- Installed by default on some PureOS/Debian systems; no warnings until disk hits 90%+
- Fix: `sudo systemctl disable --now pmlogger pmcd` + delete archives to recover space
- Alternative: `sudo pmlogger_daily -k 3 -x 3` to cap retention if PCP dashboards are in use

## Verification Level

**verified-local**

Executed on apollo (PureOS/Debian HomelabOS server). 36 GB freed and confirmed via `du -sh /var/log/pcp`. CI validation pending.

## Key Findings

**What Worked**:
- `sudo systemctl disable --now pmlogger pmcd` stops immediately and disables at boot
- `sudo rm -rf /var/log/pcp/pmlogger/<hostname>/*` reclaims all archive space
- `pmlogger_daily -k 3 -x 3` as an alternative for servers that need PCP metrics

**What Failed**:
- Using `systemctl is-active` to confirm disable → may still show "active" briefly; use `systemctl is-enabled` instead

Ajoute un premier publisher réel Nostr avec garde-fous stricts.

# Description
Adds comprehensive unit tests for `olake/types/state.go` as requested in #659 by @vaibhab-datazip.
 
`state.go` is a core component used throughout the connector framework for managing incremental sync checkpoints, CDC offsets, and backfill progress. It previously had no test coverage. This PR adds 66 sub-tests across 16 test functions covering all critical behaviors so that future modifications to state handling cannot silently break incremental syncs, CDC syncs, backfill logic, or recovery logic.

Fixes # 659

## Type of change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

All tests are in `types/state_test.go` and run with:
 
```
go test ./types/... -run "TestState" -v
```
Result: **66 sub-tests across 16 test functions — all passing.**
 
- [x] **Group 1 — Basic State:** `isZero`, `SetType`, `GetGlobal`, `SetGlobal`, `ResetStreams` — verifies state initialization and global state behavior
- [x] **Group 2 — Cursor Management:** `SetCursor`, `GetCursor`, `ResetCursor` — verifies cursor storage, retrieval, namespace isolation, and deletion
- [x] **Group 3 — Chunk Management:** `SetChunks`, `GetChunks`, `RemoveChunk` — verifies chunk creation, replacement, removal, and FULLREFRESH no-op guard
