body:
Closes #102.

Binds the studio editor's current variant draft to the render page so the preview renders exactly what a save would (`preview == render`).

## What changed
- **`DraftStore`** (`src/preview/server/draft-store.ts`): a transient in-memory holder for the editor's current draft, re-validated with `variantDefSchema` before binding (an invalid draft is never bound); no file write.
- **`server-plugin`**: additive routes `GET /api/draft` (returns `VariantDef | null`) and `PUT /api/draft` (validate + bind, `400` on invalid). Independent of the `/api/render` block (#109).
- **render page** (`main.tsx` + `draft-input.ts`): when not renderer-seeded (studio context), fetches `/api/draft` on mount and resolves the draft + the `?format=` query into the SAME `MagRenderInput` the headless renderer consumes. The seeded headless path stays fully synchronous — determinism and the `window.__MAG_RENDER__` wait are unchanged.

## Tests
- Store PUT/GET round-trip + validation (invalid rejected, prior draft preserved).
- Frame-hash equivalence: `draftToRenderInput(variant, label)` deep-equals the CLI's saved-file render job (`jobsForVariant`) per format — so, given the existing determinism guarantee, the preview frame hashes equal the saved-file frame.

## Verify
`npm run verify` green (158 tests), `npm run build` green, and a live `/api/draft` HTTP round-trip smoke test (empty → `null`; PUT valid → echo; GET → draft; PUT invalid → `400` with prior preserved).

## Problem
Premium & Standart students had their **payment receipt** (to'lov cheki) uploaded into the **"Contract Document"** field (`profiles.contract_url`, private `student-documents` bucket) instead of their **Payment** section. As a result the payment record showed an empty receipt, while the contract slot held the receipt image.

## What was done (live data migration on `Hanguk 2026` / `lysjdtyanhdfphqyijsr`)
For **48** premium/standart students with a `contract_url`:
- Copied each file from `student-documents` → public `payment-receipts` bucket.
- Attached the public receipt URL to that **same student's** payment row.
  - **40** already had a payment → receipt attached.
  - **8** had no payment row → created an `initial_deposit` payment (premium 10,000,000 / standart 5,000,000 UZS, `completed`, intake `bafc30e2…`) and attached the receipt.
- Cleared `contract_url`.

### Integrity & safety
- Matched strictly on `user_id = student_id`; every destination key is prefixed with the owner's `user_id` → **no cross-user mixup** (verified: 0 mismatches).
- Source files in `student-documents` were **not deleted** (copy, not move).

### Verification
- `still_have_contract = 0`, `migrated = 48`, `receipts present = 48`, spot-checked URLs return HTTP 200 `image/jpeg`.

> The cross-bucket copy ran server-side from Postgres via `pg_net` because the execution environment has no egress to `*.supabase.co`. This PR only adds the documented SQL + rollback script for traceability; no application code changed.

author: dotcoocoo
body:
## Summary

Redeeming a reward for points debited the customer's balance, then checked the per-customer redemption cap with a separate count and minted the reward coupon as separate steps. Two problems followed. The cap was a read-then-act check: two redemptions arriving together both read a count under the cap and both succeeded, so a customer could exceed a lifetime cap (for example mint two of a once-ever coupon). And if the coupon mint failed after the points were debited — the coupons primitive erroring, or a transient fault — the points were gone with no redemption row recorded, so no refund path could return them; the customer was charged for a reward they never received. Redemption now claims the cap slot in a single conditional insert that recomputes the live count, so concurrent redemptions can't both exceed the cap, and it reverses the points debit (and removes the claimed row) if the coupon can't be minted, so a failed redemption always leaves the balance whole. No API change.

## Test plan

- [x] `node test/smoke.js`
- [x] codebase-patterns + asset-manifest + changelog checks
- [x] gitleaks
- [ ] CI green

- Introduce a Playwright-driven External Journey Mapper to create structured, journey-led external audits that work without internal platform access.
- Define stable data contracts and decision records to separate evidence, inference, and recommendations and to enable future scoring and benchmarking.

author: tehomcd
body:
## Summary

Implements the **scene highlight reel** (#1241): a collapsible "what mattered here" panel at
the top of the scene view, surfacing one **fully sealed** featured moment + a ranked index of
the rest.

This was originally scoped as a #1240+#1241 bundle. During design we concluded **#1240
(GM nomination of event-scoped dramatic-moment types) doesn't hold up** — it would fork a
parallel catalog next to the staff one and dilute the renown economy, and its latent needs
(type discovery / catalog gaps) aren't felt pains. **#1240 is closed not-planned** (rationale on
the issue); this PR delivers #1241 alone.

## What it does

- **Featured selection:** the highest-reacted GM-tagged pose headlines — and a tagged pose
  headlines **even with zero reactions** (storyteller curation has primacy). With no tags, falls
  back to the single most-reacted pose.
- **Index:** remaining poses with ≥1 reaction, ranked by reaction count (ties → most recent),
  capped at 10.
- **Fully sealed:** the collapsed featured card shows only `✦ Top moment of this scene — reveal`
  — no pose, type, participants, or reaction count until the viewer reveals it. The whole reel is
  a collapsible section, collapsed by default.
- **Privacy:** the source set is drawn through a new shared `Interaction.objects.visible_to`, so a
  pose the viewer can't see **never appears — not even as a sealed slot**.

## Design decisions (resolved with @TehomCD)

- **Public reactions only** drive the ranking. `InteractionFavorite` is a *private bookmark* with
  no count exposed; feeding it into a public reel would leak aggregate private-bookmark behavior.
- **GM tags headline, reactions rank the rest.**
- **Fully-sealed** collapsed teaser (strongest spoiler posture).

## Implementation

- **Shared visibility filter:** extracted the interaction read-visibility union out of
  `InteractionViewSet.get_queryset` into `InteractionQuerySet.visible_to(account, persona_ids,
  since)` (mirrors the existing `SceneQuerySet.viewable_by`; idmapper-preserving). Both the
  viewset and the reel call it — no parallel privacy logic. **No behavior change** (626 scenes
  tests green).
- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/scenes/{id}/highlight-reel/` → thin, ids-only `HighlightReel` payload.
  Ranking via a queryset-level `Count("reactions")` annotation — **no denormalized count column**.
- **Frontend:** `HighlightReel` component; reveal lazily fetches the pose via the existing
  `/api/interactions/{id}/` endpoint and renders it with the standard `PoseUnit` (no duplicate
  pose rendering).
- **No new models, no migration.**

## Testing

- Backend (`world.scenes.tests.test_highlight_reel`, 7 tests): featured selection (tagged
  highest-reacted, 0-reaction tagged still headlines, multi-tagged, no-tags fallback), index
  filter/cap/exclusion, empty reel, and visibility (a very-private pose is absent for an outsider,
  present for its writer).
- Full `world.scenes` fast tier: **626 passed**. Frontend `src/scenes`: **244 passed** (incl. 3
  new `HighlightReel` tests). `pnpm build` green; `schema.json` + `api.d.ts` regenerated.

Closes #1241.

author: mpecan
body:
## Summary

The lexer scans the source as a `Vec<char>`, so token positions and AST `Span`s are **character indices**. But span *ends* were computed as `pos + value.len()` — adding the token value's **byte** length to a **character** position. For any token containing multibyte UTF-8, the end overshoots by the byte/char delta, so `Node::source_text` returns the wrong slice for every **non-final** token.

The existing `source_text_multibyte_utf8` test never caught this because its multibyte word was the *last* token, where the overshoot clamps harmlessly to the source end.

### Example (before)

```
echo "✓ valid" || echo "✗ bad"
  Command 0..16  source_text = `echo "✓ valid" |`   ← wrong (bleeds into the `||`)
```

### After

```
  Command 0..14  source_text = `echo "✓ valid"`     ← correct
```

## The fix

Use `value.chars().count()` at the four sites that derive an end offset from a start position:

- `lexer/mod.rs` — `last_token_end` (the source of most node ends via `parser/mod.rs:134`)
- `parser/simple_command.rs` — word-node span
- `parser/case_select.rs` — pattern word span
- `token.rs` — `Token::adjacent_to`

…and correct the `Span` doc comment to state offsets are character indices.

## Downstream impact

body:
### Motivation

- Make the Turtle tiling interactive demo more robust by formalizing marking segments, fixing symmetry handling, and reducing incorrect frontier/candidate recalculation during incremental search updates.
- Improve the UI/UX for demo staging and view fitting so the seed tile centers and the correct demo stage follows scroll and resize events.

### Description

- Updated the article HTML (`GCTS-I.html`) to add introductory paragraphs and reposition the floating demo inside the rendered markdown flow, and added minor UI state like `activeDemoStage` and `initialTileAreaFraction`.
- Reworked marking and lattice geometry code: introduced `primitiveSegment`, `cotangentMarkSegmentFromSpec`, `cotangentComponentForSegment`, and `transformCotangentComponent` to compute marking components consistently on the A2 lattice, replaced ad-hoc `turtleMarkSegments` with `turtleMarkSegmentSpecs` and mapped them to concrete segments.
- Fixed symmetry representation and parity handling by replacing `markSign`/`permutation` logic with `planeSign` and `symmetry.permutation` helpers, and adjusted `transform3`/`transformCotangentComponent` accordingly.
- Improved frontier and trial bookkeeping: replaced the quadratic incremental frontier update with a targeted update that computes changed point/marking keys, added `trialIsValidAgainstState` and `trialTouchesChangedSection` for precise edge pruning, optimized `placementCoronas` to BFS-style propagation, and added marking-conflict aggregation in `visibleMarkVectors` and `markStateAt` so conflicting marking values are reported and displayed.
- UI/UX and drawing tweaks: better hover tooltip layout and conflict display, seed-centered view with `centerSeedView`, automatic demo-stage syncing on scroll/resize via `demoStageForScroll`/`syncDemoStageToScroll`, and other minor canvas/scale adjustments.
- Adjusted markdown loader (`assets/markdown-article.js`) to insert the floating demo into the rendered node list and removed the unused `learning` stage rule.

### Testing

## Part 2 — Go quality pass

- **Stricter linting** — enabled `errorlint`, `revive`, `gocritic`, `misspell`, `unconvert`, `gocyclo`; fixed all 101 findings.

### Motivation
- Users need RSVP to pause at sentence boundaries (., ?, !) and choose whether pauses are manual or timed. 
- Sentence-ending detection should avoid pausing on abbreviations like `etc.` where the next non-space character is lowercase. 
- The RSVP view should reflect the current text in the insert box immediately, not only after file import. 

### Description
- Added a `Settings` tab with a `Pause` section and radio options for `Until Space is pressed` and timed pauses (`1s`, `2s`, `5s`, `10s`) via `RSVP_SENTENCE_PAUSE_DURATIONS_MS` and `RSVP_MANUAL_SENTENCE_PAUSE`. 
- Implemented `build_rsvp_tokens(text: str)` that tokenizes text with `re.finditer(r"\S+")` and returns `(words, pause_flags)` where a pause flag is set when a token ends with `.`, `?`, or `!` and the next non-space character is uppercase. 
- Wired the text area to immediately update RSVP tokens by binding `<<Modified>>` to `handle_text_modified` which calls `refresh_rsvp_words_from_import`; import flows also call `refresh_rsvp_words_from_import`. 
- Added playback control to handle sentence pauses: `should_pause_after_current_rsvp_word`, `start_rsvp_sentence_pause`, `advance_rsvp_word_after_pause`, and logic in `advance_rsvp_word`/`toggle_rsvp_playback` to honor manual or timed pauses and to ignore space presses originating from the text box. 
- Updated `README.md` to document the new Settings and that RSVP reads the current text in the Import area.

- Ran a targeted tokenization check by calling `FastReadingApp.build_rsvp_tokens(...)` with a sample string to verify pause flags for abbreviations and sentence ends, which passed after fixing the detection logic.

## Summary

- Fixes #223. `stream_agent` unconditionally used `SubprocessCliTransport::one_shot`, which runs `claude` in `--print` mode without stdin. With `sdk_mcp_server` registered, the CLI's MCP `initialize` handshake never completes and the toolbox is marked `failed`, so the model never sees the custom tools.

author: uwezkhan
body:
term_to_json_value reads each map key and the list tail through get_type, which forwards the raw iterator to ei_get_type with no bounds check. The list and tuple paths run through write_sequence, which calls invalid_end right after its advance, but the ERL_MAP_EXT branch and the ERL_LIST_EXT tail read skip that check, and eetf_to_json calls decode_version before confirming the buffer is non-empty. A truncated map whose header declares an arity but carries no entries, a list missing its NIL tail, or an empty buffer each leave the iterator at end and the next ei_* read runs past it.

Before, those inputs returned whatever error the over-read happened to produce (or faulted against an unmapped page); after, each ei read is gated on it < end and they return unexpected_end / no_read_input deterministically. The guards sit in eetf_to_json next to the reads they protect rather than in the shared ei wrappers, because ei_get_type and ei_decode_version must read the tag byte to do their work and cannot validate end on their own. read_eetf already rejects empty input upstream, so only the eetf_to_json entry point needed the version guard.

author: netliomax25-code
body:
1. saslBindTokenExchange reads serverSaslCreds at protocolOp.Children[3] for a saslBindInProgress (result code 14) response, but the length check ahead of it only required three children.
2. serverSaslCreds is the optional [7] field that follows the three LDAPResult components, so a server that returns code 14 with only those components makes the index out of range and panics the bind goroutine mid GSSAPI handshake.

Require at least four children before reading the creds child, so a short response falls through to GetLDAPError instead of indexing past the slice. Added a regression test that drives the exchange with a three-child in-progress response.

author: jensholdgaard
body:
## RFC 0018 — OTLP log-spec compliance amendments

One compliance push closing the six OTLP-fidelity gaps from the 2026-06-20 audit (three areas: receiver, schema, DSL/querier), each graded against the spec's own **MUST/SHOULD** via the OpenTelemetry knowledge base.

| # | Gap | Spec level | Amends |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scope.attributes` + resource/scope `schema_url` dropped at ingest | **MUST** (AnyValue must be stored; scope = name/version/schema_url/attributes) | RFC 0003 + 0005 |
| 2 | transient WAL/storage failure → non-retryable `INTERNAL`/`500` (clients drop data) | retry table (SHOULD, real data-loss) | RFC 0003 |
| 3 | `event_name` stored + returnable but not a DSL filter | top-level field | RFC 0002 |
| 4 | non-finite doubles (`NaN`/`±Inf`) → `null`, don't round-trip | lossy | RFC 0005 |
| 5 | `SeverityNumber` not range-validated (`u8` 0..255 vs 1..24/0) | normalized values | RFC 0003 |
| 6 | `body` column doc says "raw bytes" but holds UTF-8 JSON for Structured | doc only | RFC 0005 |

**Refuted by the spec check** (not in scope): the audit's "structured AnyValue body is type-erased" — the stored canonical JSON *is* the OTLP protobuf→JSON mapping and preserves the discriminator.

### Invariants / hazards touched
- **§3.5 schema migration** — the three new columns are **OPTIONAL**; readers tolerate their absence in historical files (RFC0018.2). Additive, no breaking schema change.
- **§3.7 multi-tenancy** — new columns are per-tenant like all data.
- **H6** — the new `event_name` DSL field leaks no DataFusion/SQL surface (RFC0018.4).
- **§3.3/§3.4 durability** — the retry-mapping fix (#2) protects WAL-before-ack: a transient failure must not be reported as non-retryable.

`status: specified` — §5 scenarios RFC0018.1–.6. **Held for maintainer sign-off**: amends accepted RFC 0003/0005 and green RFC 0002. Per the standing directive, spec fidelity outranks downstream API stability (pre-release), so the implementation will take the resulting type/schema changes.

## Problema
`findTemplate` elegia la plantilla **equivocada** por colisiones de keywords genericas. Reportado: un **finiquito** mostraba un documento de **prescripcion de deuda** (ambas plantillas tenian la keyword generica `cobro` y empataban). Tambien: alimentos caia en licencia de conducir; isapre/sernac caian en plantillas duplicadas. Esto afectaba el preview Y el documento final generado.

## Solucion
### `findTemplate` (scoring)
- **Ponderacion por especificidad**: una keyword mas larga pesa mas (`finiquito`=9 le gana a `cobro`=5). Antes todas valian 1 y empataban.
- **El tipo de documento (materia) pesa x3**: es la señal mas confiable de que quiere el cliente.
- **Deduplicacion**: keywords que normalizan igual (`prescripcion`/`prescripción`) ya no se cuentan dos veces.

### Limpieza de keywords genericas
Quite palabras demasiado amplias que se robaban casos: `cobro`, `reclamo`, `empresa`, `servicio`, `alimentos`/`pension` (de licencia), `desalojo` (de la carta de desahucio), `cotizaciones` (de finiquito), `sernac`/`reclamo` (de las plantillas duplicadas #70 y #71). Y reforce keywords especificas (finiquito, cotizaciones, cobro de dinero, demanda desalojo).

## Pruebas
Bateria de 17 casos de la demanda real (finiquito, alimentos, licencia, TAG, deuda bancaria, cotizaciones, despido, desalojo, cobro de dinero, divorcio, VIF, ISAPRE, SERNAC, querella, proteccion, multa transito, union civil):
- **16/17 eligen la plantilla correcta.**
- El restante es un caso ambiguo legitimo (reclamo multa transito vs recurso de reposicion, ambos ante Juzgado de Policia Local).
- `npm run build` pasa.

## Seguimiento
Las plantillas #70-83 son en parte duplicados de plantillas anteriores (dos "Acceso a Informacion Publica", dos VIF, dos Contraloria, etc.) con keywords genericas. Conviene consolidarlas en una limpieza futura.

body:
## Summary

Two `chunkMarkdown` correctness bugs found by the retrieval audit, both in `flush()`. Low severity — cleaning up the chunk index.

### Bug 4 (LOW) — empty-body chunks
`chunkMarkdown` flushes on every `#`/`##` heading, so a top-level `#` title immediately followed by `##` yields a chunk with `body:""`. **4 such chunks existed in the real corpus** (all troubleshooting files), indexed at title weight 10 with no content.

Their heading keywords ("401 403", "token invalid") are already repeated by the child sections that carry the body, so dropping them loses nothing.

Fix: `flush()` skips a chunk with empty body. Chunk count **135 → 131**.

### Bug 5 (LOW, latent) — slug collision
Two identical `##` heading texts in one file produced the same chunk id (`source#slug`). 0 collisions in current docs, but latent. Fix: de-duplicate slugs within a file (append `-2`, `-3`...).

## Verified

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Empty-body chunks | 4 → 0 |
| Duplicate headings | distinct ids, both bodies preserved (`t#sub-a`, `t#sub-a-2`) |
| `#` title WITH a body | still kept (not dropped) |
| Tests | 459 pass + 4 new guards |

author: l-qing
body:
Fixes #10323

# Changes

StepActions are resolved concurrently in `GetStepActionsData`
(`default-step-ref-concurrency-limit`, default `5`). Each goroutine runs the
parameter-substitution helpers against the same `TaskSpec`. The replacement
builders `replacementsFromDefaultParams` / `replacementsFromParams` returned the
object parameter's shared `ObjectVal` map **by reference**, so when a caller merged
the TaskRun value onto a default it mutated that shared map in place. With
concurrent resolution this crashed the controller with `fatal error: concurrent map
writes`; even single-threaded it corrupted the Task's object-param default.

This clones the object map at the source with `maps.Clone`, so the builders never
hand out an alias and every downstream merge (StepAction resolver params,
`applyStepActionParameters`, `getTaskParameters`) stays private. Affects `v1.4.0+`.

body:
## Summary
- Replace public auth with `requestOneTimePassword` + `verifyOneTimePassword`, removing password sign-up/sign-in/reset/change-password mutations.
- Move local auth from `cognito-local` to real AWS Cognito EMAIL_OTP, including Terraform user-pool/client settings and IAM for unconfirmed-user recreation.
- Remove `AWS_COGNITO_ENDPOINT`, Cognito API/JWKS endpoint overrides, and the local `GlobalSignOut` skip path so the API always uses real AWS Cognito.
- Replace mobile sign-in/create-account/password screens with one email-first OTP flow using an 8-digit `OneTimePasswordInput` that matches AWS Cognito EMAIL_OTP behavior.
- Update request-log redaction, Maestro auth onboarding, runbooks, and harness docs for unified OTP auth.

## Why
AWS Cognito EMAIL_OTP sends an 8-digit email code and supports passwordless sign-in via `USER_AUTH`. The previous 6-digit/password UI and local Cognito assumptions caused local E2E mismatch and unnecessary owner friction. Keeping `AWS_COGNITO_ENDPOINT` also left a local-auth footgun where JWT verification and Cognito API calls could point at incompatible endpoints.

## Product Axes
- Dog experience: no direct change.
- Walk data: no direct change.
- Owner contribution: improves login/onboarding recovery by removing password and account-mode decisions.

- API tests from current worktree: passed.

author: adnaan
body:
Fixes #292 — three browser E2E tests that flaked in the cross-repo "Test Tinkerdown against Core Changes" job. Two distinct, unrelated root causes (a third item surfaced two more tests sharing cause #2).

## 1. `TestActionButtons` — `SQLITE_BUSY`
SQLite's `busy_timeout` defaults to **0**, so a read racing a concurrent write fails immediately with "database is locked". The library now opens every SQLite connection with `busy_timeout=5000` (new `sqliteDSN` helper in `internal/source`, used by `SQLiteSource` and the schema probe), and the test's own verification connection gets the same pragma. The read now waits for the action's write to commit. Unit test asserts the pragma actually takes effect.

## 2. Checkbox toggles never reflected the server's new state
`TestAutoTasks_BasicToggle` / `_NoFullReload` and `TestLvtSourceMarkdownToggle` / `ToggleBack`: the server toggled correctly and broadcast `checked` (visible in WS frames), but the checkbox's `.checked` **property** never updated. Root cause: the client's morphdom pass preserves live `<input>` state over server-rendered values — backwards for a server-authoritative `lvt-on:click="Toggle"` checkbox.

Fixed **generically upstream** in `@livetemplate/client` **v0.14.3** ([livetemplate/client#135](https://github.com/livetemplate/client/pull/135)): an `lvt-on:click` checkbox/radio is now server-authoritative by default. This PR bumps `@livetemplate/client` `0.11.9 → 0.14.3` and rebuilds the embedded bundle — **no per-template attribute needed**. Documented in [livetemplate#461](https://github.com/livetemplate/livetemplate/pull/461).

(Chose the upstream fix over sprinkling `data-lvt-force-update` on every toggle template, since the whole ecosystem — lvt toggle component, datatable, tinkerdown — writes this pattern expecting server authority.)

## E2E hardening
Switched auto-task interactions from `chromedp.Click` to JS `.click()` (CDP click is unreliable for delegated handlers in headless Docker Chrome, as `action_buttons_e2e_test.go` already documents) and replaced fixed sleeps with `waitForDOM` polling for the actual expected state.

## Verification
Local Docker Chrome against `@livetemplate/client@0.14.3` (attributes removed, relying on auto-detection): `TestActionButtons`, all six `TestAutoTasks_*`, both markdown toggle tests green on repeat runs. Full `-tags=ci` suite green.

author: hangyuanliu
body:
## What

M4 — the redo of **gap2** (transitive equi-join predicates for join reorder), the original motivation of the whole scalar-IR / unified-plan-node arc. The reorder graph could not see transitive edges: for `WHERE a.x=b.y AND b.y=c.z` it built only A–B and B–C edges, so any order joining A⋈C directly was costed as a penalized cross-join. This makes a transitively-connected atom pair a real equi-join candidate.

The earlier gap2 was reverted because it filled host memory on TPC-DS q72 (it computed the **full C(k,2)** pairwise closure of **deep-cloned** `TypedExpr` predicates **inside the flattener, per reorder candidate**). This redo is memory-safe by construction.

## How

Recon-first (`docs/design/notes/2026-06-20-m4-gap2-recon-findings.md`) pinned the precise gap: the transitive **column** closure already exists as an **O(k) union-find `EquivalenceClasses`** on logical_props, and literal/constant propagation is already fully implemented — the *only* missing piece is making the **reorder enumeration** consult that closure.

- `flatten` derives the chain's `col=col` closure via the shared `EquivalenceClasses` union-find (scoped to the chain) and stores it on `MultiJoinGraph::equi_classes` as per-atom representative **interned** `ColumnRef` scalars — O(atoms-in-class), never C(k,2).
- The enumeration's `connecting_condition_scalars` reduces a partition's connecting condition to **at most one equi per equivalence class**: a literal equi is preferred, otherwise one `leftRep=rightRep` is synthesized from the class (reusing interned scalars). This both closes the gap *and* prevents the selectivity double-count a path cut like `{A,C}⋈B` would otherwise introduce — dropping the redundant `b=c` is safe because the `{A,C}` sub-plan already enforces `a≡c`.

**Why this can't reproduce the gap2 OOM** — the three blowup vectors are structurally absent: no C(k,2) (O(k) reps + one-equi-per-class), no deep clone (interned scalars), no per-candidate recomputation (derived once in `flatten`). Search-space stays bounded by the existing reorder caps (#321 bushy bound, `cbo_max_groups`, explore-cap).

**Design note (StarRocks is a reference, not a target):** StarRocks materializes the transitive equalities into the plan (`equivalenceDerive`) because its FE has no normalized equivalence class at that stage. NovaRocks already computes one in-memo, so the architecturally healthier choice is to keep that class the single source of truth and consult it on demand (no plan-tree denormalization → no consistency tax, no selectivity double-count). See the findings doc.

## Verification (dev-opt, `-j1`, iceberg-rest SF1 fixture)

- `cargo test --lib`: **5128 pass** (+8 new reorder unit tests: class build, synthesis, same-class dedup, simple-join no-op, candidate reachability, k=12 bounded-ness).
- **TPC-DS 99/99 verify PASS** (runner exit 0 ⇒ `grand_failed=0`) — no correctness regression.
- **TPC-DS q72 (the rolled-back gap2's OOM query): PASS, 33.99s, rows=100**, peak server RSS ≈6.6 GB single-run / ≈12.6 GB across the full serial sweep — bounded execution memory, no planning explosion, far below host memory. **The gap2 red line holds.**
- optimizer plan-golden suite **63/63 PASS** — zero plan-shape churn (the suite's joins are below the multi-join reorder threshold, so they never enter this path).
- `cargo clippy --lib`: no errors (two pre-existing `collapsible_if` warnings on `main`).

**Deferred:** a fine-grained `enable_transitive_predicate` session toggle was not added — the feature is safe by construction and `SET disable_optimizer_rules='MultiJoinReorder'` already gates the whole pass. Branch-vs-`main` runtime A/B not run (needs a separate `main` rebuild); the capability is unit-proven and correctness is covered by 99/99.

author: prule
body:
## Why

When the ACC broadcasting connection stays alive across two back-to-back races, all laps were recorded into a single session — `ClientInitializer` created one session on the first session-phase update and never closed it. A "2 races of 5 laps" weekend was stored as one 10-lap session, corrupting every downstream insight.

## What changed

- **`SessionTracker`** (pure, unit-tested) segments the live `RealtimeUpdate` stream into discrete sessions:
  - composite identity key `(sessionIndex, sessionType)` is the primary "new session" signal — robust even if terminal frames are missed;
  - terminal phases (`SESSION_OVER`/`POST_SESSION`/`RESULT_UI`) finalize the active session with an end time.
- **`EndSession` use case** + `SessionEnded` event. `Session` gains an idempotent `end()`/`endedAt` and a nullable `ended_at` column (migration, no backfill — legacy rows stay null).
- **Per-session state isolation** — `SessionState` is replaced on each new session so lap counts/validity don't leak across sessions.
- **API surface** — `SessionEnded` forwarded over the `/api/1/events` WebSocket; `endedAt` exposed on `SessionResource`. Frontend types, mock data, and `LiveScreen` updated.
- **Docs** — `real-time-updates.md` and `user-guide.md` describe session segmentation.

## Testing

- `./gradlew :app:build` — green (full test suite + ktfmt)
- Frontend `pnpm typecheck` clean, `pnpm test` — 28 passed

author: tineprogramming
body:
## What

Turns `session-desktop` into the **Apocentro** desktop client.

### 1. Closed-ecosystem magic-bytes protocol layer
Every snode-bound message payload is prefixed with the 4 Apocentro magic bytes (`0x41 0x50 0x43 0x01` = `"APC"` + v1) *after* libsession encryption; incoming messages without it are dropped. Isolates Apocentro from the public Session network and makes desktop interoperate with the existing Apocentro **web** and **Android** clients.

**Why it interoperates:** desktop, Android, and (for DMs) web all wrap the **same layer** — the output of libsession's `encodeFor1o1` / `encodeForGroup`. Android does exactly this in `MessageSender`/`MessageParser`. Mirrored byte-for-byte, so **desktop ↔ Android groups-v2 and DMs work natively** (same libsession), and DM with web works too.

- `ts/session/crypto/MagicBytes.ts` (new) — `wrap`/`has`/`strip` (port of web + Android).
- `ts/session/sending/MessageWrapper.ts` — prefix `encryptedAndWrappedData` (1o1 + group).
- `ts/session/apis/snode_api/swarmPolling.ts` — strip before `decryptFor1o1`/`decryptForGroup`; drop non-Apocentro messages. Config namespaces left unwrapped (matches Android).

### 2. Package-identity rebrand
`package.json` (`name`, `productName` "Apocentro", `description`, `author`, `appId` `com.apocentro.desktop`, macOS cam/mic strings, Windows `publisherName`), matching `main_node.ts` AUMID, `background.html` `<title>`, and `repository` → this fork (so the auto-update feed is inferred from **our** releases, not Session's).

### 3. Icons & brand art
Every app icon / brand asset swapped for the Apocentro logo (green-on-dark mark, same as Android launcher + web), generated from the 1024px source: `build/icon.ico`, `build/icon-mac.icns`, `build/icon-linux.icns`, `build/icons/icon_*.png`, `images/session/session_icon*.png`, and the `brand.svg` / `session-text.svg` (Apocentro wordmark).

### 4. UI string rebrand
The displayed "Session" name → "Apocentro" across **all** localized strings, via a single word-boundary replacement at the `LocalizedStringBuilder.toString()` funnel (capital-S brand only — never the common noun "session"). `ts/localization` is vendored from its git submodule (which this fork can't push to) so the rebrand is self-contained; on-disk files are otherwise unchanged.

## Remaining (follow-ups)
- [ ] `build/installer-sidebar.bmp` — NSIS install-wizard sidebar art (BMP; couldn't be generated here). Cosmetic.
- [ ] **Build / sign / package** the Electron installers and smoke-test.
- [ ] Confirm releases publish under this repo (or set `build.publish` explicitly); ensure `win.publisherName` matches the real signing cert if `verifyUpdateCodeSignature` is later enabled.

> ⚠️ I can't build or run the Electron GUI in this environment, so everything here is verified against the Android/web protocol spec, the icon files validated (`file`), and the brand regex unit-checked — but **not yet run on a desktop build**. Please `git submodule update --init dynamic_assets && pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm build-release` and test locally. Easiest interop check: sign in with a fresh seed and DM an existing Apocentro web/Android account.

body: ## What The **`DOCS`** product tag in the docs navbar now renders in **real Geist SemiBold** — the exact typeface `coach.saturday.fit` uses for its **`COACH`** tag. Before, `DOCS` used a generic `-apple-system,…` `` stack, so it fell back to the viewer's OS font and looked nothing like `COACH`. ## How - The portal tag is `text-[11px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.2em] text-brand-teal`, and `--font-sans` is **Geist** (`next/font/google`). Reproduced exactly: instanced the variable Geist at **`wght=600`** and baked `DOCS` to **vector paths**. - Paths (not a `font-family` ref) are mandatory — Mintlify serves the logo via ``, which can't load a webfont, so a named-font reference silently falls back again (the original bug). - **Geometry unchanged** — size `31` (=11px), tracking `6.2` (=0.2em), baseline `34`. Only the glyph *source* changed: system-sans → Geist-600. - Tag fill **`#1aabb8`** in both modes = the portal's `text-brand-teal`, which is also the docs site's own `colors.primary`. - `viewBox` width `464.0 → 466.5` (Geist `S` right edge is `464.48`; the old box clipped it ~0.5u). ## Verify Rendered both light/dark variants on white + navy navbar backgrounds — Geist letterforms, semibold weight, 0.2em tracking, vertical centering with the wordmark all match the portal lockup. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: saagpatel
body:
## What

Third structural collapse. The `rebuild` and `rererestore` hotspot selectors share one group/dedup/filter/sort algorithm differing only in the per-tier persistence/churn keys, the `just-*` mode token, and the holding/sustained status set. Extract `_hotspots_base` + a `_HotspotsTierSpec`; both public selectors become thin wrappers.

The two tiers had *also* drifted on **defensive coercion** — rebuild wrapped score/age/label in `float()`/`int()`/`str()`; rererestore was bare. Identical on real numeric data; the base unifies on rebuild's safer coercion (verified byte-identical).

**−72 net lines.**

## Verified (three proofs)

1. **Differential test** — real selectors vs. base+spec over the net's targets × all 9 modes → byte-identical for both tiers, before touching the file.
2. **Composer golden byte-identical** to `main` — a correct collapse changes no output.
3. **Full suite green** — `2539 passed, 2 skipped`.

`ruff` + `mypy` clean. Public signatures unchanged, so callers (the summaries that read these keys, the apply-chain) are untouched.

## Campaign progress

Three of four clean rebuild↔rererestore families collapsed: persistence (#82), churn (#83), hotspots (this). **`refresh_recovery` remains** — it's the genuinely complex one (intricate branching, implicit-concat reason strings, output-keys-that-are-also-vars), so it gets a dedicated careful pass rather than a rushed one.

author: lingyun1010
body:
# Phase 3: Airtable Ingestion

This PR adds Airtable as an optional ingestion source for the TikTok Content Agent.

The main goal of Phase 3 is to move beyond sample CSV input while keeping the pipeline modular, safe, and testable. CSV remains the default source for local development and public demo usage, while Airtable can now be used when the required environment variables are configured.

## What changed

- Added an Airtable ingestion adapter under the backend ingest layer.
- Added source selection support so the pipeline can run with either CSV or Airtable input.
- Kept CSV as the default source to ensure the public demo workflow still works without external API access.
- Mapped Airtable records into the existing canonical TikTok post schema.
- Added environment variable support for Airtable configuration.
- Updated `.env.example` with Airtable-related placeholders.
- Updated documentation to explain how Airtable ingestion should be configured and used.
- Updated the current checkpoint to reflect Phase 3 progress.

## What this PR does not do

- This PR does not add OpenAI integration.
- This PR does not add DeepSeek integration.
- This PR does not add TikTok upload or draft publishing.
- This PR does not add image or video generation.
- This PR does not commit real Airtable data.
- This PR does not commit secrets or API keys.

## Testing

The existing sample CSV pipeline was kept working.

Verified command:

```bash
python -m src.backend.pipeline --mode export_only --input examples/sample_recent_posts.csv --limit 10
```

Expected demo outputs:

outputs/demo/metrics_summary.md
outputs/demo/content_plan.json
outputs/demo/script.md
outputs/demo/caption.txt
outputs/demo/hashtags.txt

## Security notes

 Airtable credentials are read from environment variables only.

 Required environment variables:

AIRTABLE_API_KEY
AIRTABLE_BASE_ID
AIRTABLE_TABLE_NAME
AIRTABLE_VIEW_NAME

No real API keys, tokens, Airtable exports, TikTok analytics, or generated private outputs should be committed to this repository.

## Engineering note

This phase keeps ingestion separate from analysis.

Once Airtable records are mapped into the canonical TikTok post schema, the existing deterministic metrics, rule-based signals, and manual strategy outputs can continue to run without knowing where the data originally came from.

author: guillempuche
body:
## What

Makes batuda's local dev sign-in work out of the box. Surface: **Auth origin trust** — `server` (the derived/trusted origins) plus `internal` (the Vite dev API proxy and the Playwright harness). `portless` can't bind privileged port 443 without root, so it falls back to a non-privileged port (e.g. `:1355`); the browser origin becomes `https://batuda.localhost:1355`, but the dev origin derivation stripped the port. Better Auth's origin matcher is port-sensitive and validates the `Origin` whenever a cookie is present (browsers always send one), so every sign-in returned `403 Invalid origin` on a fresh clone.

## The fix

- Keep portless's assigned port in the derived dev origins (drop only the default `:443`, which the browser omits), and fold the derived **app** origin into `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` so CORS, Better-Auth `trustedOrigins`, and the `APP_PUBLIC_URL` boot check all accept the real browser origin — no per-machine env edit.
- Tightened the dev-marker check to a label boundary, so a lookalike host like `xbatuda.localhost` can't self-derive a trusted origin (least-trust; came out of the security review).
- Point the Vite dev API proxy and the Playwright base URL at portless's actual port. The SSR hard-reload session check proxies through the same target, so the "reload-logs-you-out" path is fixed too.
- The security-sensitive `matchOrigin` is left unchanged — the merged exact literal covers ported origins via exact match, so a wrong port (`:9999`) still 403s.

## Impact

- **`ALLOWED_ORIGINS` / CORS — dev-only, no production change, no coordinated deploy.** The port-carrying origin is derived from `PORTLESS_URL` and gated on the non-routable `.localhost` TLD; production keeps its explicit literal origins (no derivation, no wildcard, `strict` rate limit, secure cookies). An adversarial review confirmed no value of `PORTLESS_URL` can broaden production trust — every derived origin stays under `.localhost`.
- No migration, no RLS / `organization_id` change, no MCP↔HTTP wire-shape change, no new env vars (`PORTLESS_URL` already existed and is dev-only), and no change to the prod auth / route-protection boundary.

## Review guide

- Start at `apps/server/src/lib/portless-origins.ts` (port kept, `:443` dropped, label-boundary guard) and `env.ts` `mergeWorktreeOrigin` (only the app origin is trusted, deduped, returns unchanged off a worktree).
- Riskiest part is the dev/prod boundary. I ran an adversarial security review — prod-injection of a stray `PORTLESS_URL`, port/parser confusion (`:0443`, userinfo, case, trailing dot, IP-literal), and the Better-Auth-vs-repo matcher divergence — and found **no path that broadens production trust; must-fix: none**. `snyk_code_scan` not run (tool unavailable in this environment).
- Full design + security analysis lives in #124.

## Tests

- Unit (`@batuda/server`): port preserved / `:443` dropped / https pinned / lookalike host rejected; `mergeWorktreeOrigin` prepend + dedup, and the merged list passing the `APP_PUBLIC_URL` boot check.
- Real-browser E2E (Playwright + Chromium): sign-in flows + session-persistence, including the SSR-hard-reload-while-authed path.

## Verification

- Gates run green: `pnpm install` (no lockfile drift), `check-types` (12/12), `test` (371 server tests + all packages), `build` (12/12 — including the `internal` SSR bundle that exercises `vite.config.ts`).
- Live: **12/12 real-browser E2E with zero manual config** — the Playwright config auto-derived `https://batuda.localhost:1355` from `~/.portless/proxy.port`. API matrix with a cookie present: trusted `:1355` → 200, untrusted origin and wrong port `:9999` → 403.
- No visual change (dev proxy + test config only), so no screenshots — the real-browser E2E is the behavioral proof.

## Deferred

- Evaluate removing the now-largely-redundant `https://*.batuda.localhost` wildcard from `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, since each worktree derives its own exact origin.
- Reconcile the Better-Auth-vs-repo wildcard matcher divergence (multi-label vs single-label; dev-only).
- Harden `findUnsafeWildcardOrigin` against suffix-confusion (pre-existing defense-in-depth; prod config is already explicit).

Closes #124.

## 🛠️ Solution Summary
The original code had a bug where any exception thrown during the file upload would be caught and re-thrown as a `RetriableActivityException`, but the original exception was being lost. This fix adds a separate catch block for `RetriableActivityException` to preserve the original exception, and also adds a separate catch block for any other exceptions that may occur during the `s3Client.read(s3Path)` call, which would also be wrapped in a `RetriableActivityException`.

The original code only handles the 'IN_PROGRESS' state, but the 'FAILED' state is also returned by the external API. The patch adds a check for the 'FAILED' state and throws a more specific exception in that case, while keeping the original exception handling for other unexpected states.

Implement the `write` method to allow writing data to S3.

The original code was missing the local file path parameter in the `uploadFile` method call. The fix adds a `localPath` variable and passes it to the `uploadFile` method.

author: nishantyadav0042-glitch
body:
## Problem

Supabase ignores `emailRedirectTo` when the target URL isn't in its allowed redirect URLs list. It falls back to the configured Site URL (domain root), so the magic link in the email lands at e.g. `/?code=<code>` instead of `/auth/callback?code=<code>`. The callback route was never reached, so users always ended up on the home page unsigned in.

## Fix

Added a guard at the top of `src/proxy.ts` (Next.js 16 middleware) that intercepts any request carrying Supabase auth params (`code` for PKCE, or `token_hash`+`type` for token-hash flow) on any path other than `/auth/callback`, and redirects to `/auth/callback` with those params preserved.

This works regardless of which URL Supabase chooses as its redirect target — as long as it's on the same domain.

## What changed

- `src/proxy.ts` — 16 lines added before the session-refresh logic

## M2·P2.3 — Grocery Scan & Go session/cart

Replaces the demo client-minted cart with a real server-issued session, and adds a name-search fallback for unknown barcodes.

### What changed
- **Real Scan & Go session.** `/grocery` mints its cart via `useTableSession("scango")` — the same anon-auth `table_sessions` / `session_members` / `qr_carts` + membership-authz the dine-in/pickup flows use. The demo `crypto.randomUUID()` (which `assertCartMember` rightly rejected) and the dishonest *"Scan & Go opens with grocery sessions (M2)"* placeholder are gone, so `scanAdd` now works end-to-end into `/cart` + Stripe. Prices/taxes stay server-derived; the client never sends a price.
- **Name-search fallback** (`searchGroceryItems`): a debounced public read of the public-RLS `grocery_items` (available + non-weighed only, LIKE-metacharacters escaped, Zod-bounded `.min(2).max(40)` query). Tapping a hit adds it through the **same** authorized `scanAdd`. EBT-eligible hits are tagged. Verified live — "tea" → Pickled Tea Leaf (Laphet), $8.49, EBT.
- **Fixed in passing:** the barcode scanner restarted the camera on every render (a fresh `onScan` each time) → memoized so it starts once; and `/grocery` had two live regions (scanned-lines `aria-live` + the status toast) → collapsed to one.

### Verification
- Gate green (`turbo lint typecheck build`). Search filters confirmed against the live catalog (all 6 SKUs searchable; weighed/unavailable excluded).
- **Pre-PR adversarial subagent: GO-WITH-NITS → nits fixed → GO** (verdict posted as a PR comment). No blockers; auth path, scanner-restart fix, and search safety all verified. Fixed its findings: focus-return after a tapped hit, honest "Search unavailable" vs "No matches" copy, and a duplicated ROADMAP line.

### Notes
- `searchGroceryItems` is intentionally a **public** (no-auth) read — it exposes only the public catalog `/menu` already does, no PII; every *mutation* still routes through `scanAdd` → `assertCartMember`.

author: noe-charmet
body: Containerize `apps/client` as the end-user-facing image: nginx (alpine) serving the prebuilt Vite `dist/` that `turbo build` produces outside Docker. Unlike the api/runner images there is no `pnpm install` and no `turbo prune` — the client is a static artifact, so Docker only assembles it. The defining requirement is **runtime config injection**: the API endpoint must not be baked at build time, so one redistributable image works for any self-hoster. A `/docker-entrypoint.d/` script rewrites `/config.js` from environment (`SHIPFOX_API_URL`) on each container start (the stock nginx entrypoint runs it before nginx). The client reads `window.__SHIPFOX_CONFIG__.apiUrl` and falls back to the build-time `VITE_API_URL`, so dev and tests are unchanged. nginx adds an SPA fallback and serves `config.js`/`index.html` with `no-store` so an env change or new deploy is picked up on the next load; fingerprinted `/assets/` stay immutable. The `image` script wires `shipfox-docker` in plain (non-prune) context mode. Also adds the `.dockerignore` scoped to the static context and OCI labels, mirroring the api image (#248). ## Verification - `turbo build --filter @shipfox/client` → `dist/config.js` present; built `index.html` loads `/config.js` before the app bundle. - Built the image and ran it twice with **different** `SHIPFOX_API_URL` values on the **same image**: `/config.js` reflected each value (no rebuild), `/` and a deep route both served the SPA shell, `config.js` returned `Cache-Control: no-store`. - `turbo build test check` and `turbo type --filter '...[origin/main]'` green across affected packages. The `ApiClientOptions.baseUrl` widening to `string | undefined` is backward-compatible. ## Note The acceptance's `turbo image --filter @shipfox/client` needs the turbo `image` **task** in `turbo.jsonc`, which is owned by ENG-526 and not added here (the merged api PR followed the same boundary — script only). Verified via the `image` script directly; once ENG-526 lands the task, `turbo image` drives this script unchanged. Refs ENG-524 --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a self-hostable Docker image for `@shipfox/client`, served by nginx, with runtime API endpoint injection so one image works across environments without rebuilds. Improves SPA routing and caching; dev and tests remain unchanged. Refs ENG-524. - New Features - Dockerfile: nginx (alpine) serves the prebuilt Vite `dist/`; no Node or install steps in the image. - Runtime config: entrypoint script writes `/config.js` from `SHIPFOX_API_URL`; app reads `window.__SHIPFOX_CONFIG__.apiUrl` and falls back to `VITE_API_URL`. - Nginx config: SPA fallback; `config.js` and `index.html` served with `Cache-Control: no-store`; `/assets/` cached immutable. - Client API: supports runtime base URL resolution; widened `ApiClientOptions.baseUrl`; added tests. - Tooling: minimal `.dockerignore`, OCI labels, and an `image` script using `@shipfox/docker` (ENG-526 will add the `turbo image` task). author: joewaller
body:
## Why

The `UserPromptSubmit` tray dumped **every** active/stale session (a 5-day window) with its full task text and every per-edit `file-change` broadcast — thousands of tokens injected per turn with ~20 sessions open.

Worse, "active" was a pure **heartbeat timer**, which can't distinguish an *idle* session (user asleep, terminal still open) from a *dead* one (reboot / crash / `kill -9`, where no `SessionEnd` fires). So ghosts lingered as `active` for 5 days — **and their file claims kept blocking live edits** via the `PreToolUse` gate.

## What

**Tray (context load)**
- One line per session, most-recent-first, capped (`DISPLAY_MAX_SESSIONS`); the rest collapse to `… and N more`. No per-session task/working_on text.
- `file-change` broadcasts collapse to a single deduped line; directed messages (info/breaking-change) stay verbatim.
- Genuine collisions (another live session claims a file you've claimed) get detail; a gated same-cwd "potential clash" hint points at `claustrum show`.

**Liveness (fitness for purpose)**
- New `_reap_dead()` runs on prompt / start / status / gc. A same-host session is dead if its **boot epoch** predates the current boot, its **tmux pane** is gone, its **label** is absent from live tmux sessions (legacy-row fallback), or its **pid** is gone. Reaping **releases the dead session's file claims**.
- Cross-host / unverifiable sessions fall back to the `last_seen` timer.
- New `sessions` columns: `host`, `tmux_pane`, `pid`, `boot_id` — non-breaking `ALTER`-based migration; existing rows backfill on next heartbeat.

**New command**
- `claustrum show <name|uid>` — full on-demand detail for one session (task, working_on, claimed files, cwd, live-state): the drill-in the trimmed tray points at.

**Docs** — README example tray, CLI reference, and liveness design principle updated.

## Verified
- All reap paths in isolation (boot mismatch, dead pane, live pane, legacy label fallback, cross-host, pid) + non-breaking migration of a pre-upgrade DB.
- Real DB: roster trimmed, file-change feed collapsed, clash hint gated at the monorepo root; `gc` cleaned 73 stale sessions + 416 messages with **zero live sessions wrongly reaped** (23 active in DB == 23 live tmux sessions).

author: rosvend
body:
## Summary

Adapts **@sararuaga's multi-objective angular/sectorial clustering** (from PR #6) into the unified benchmark harness as a first-class `sectorial` solver, re-runs the full 6-algorithm benchmark, and updates the paper accordingly.

This **supersedes #6**, which couldn't be merged as-is (CONFLICTING state from unrelated repo-structure churn — moving `pyproject.toml`/`README` into `src/` and deleting `src/clustering.py` — plus it was a standalone script, not a `Solver`). Here we take only the algorithm and integrate it cleanly. **Recommend closing #6** in favor of this PR.

## What's included

**Adapter** (`src/benchmarks/adapters/sectorial.py`)
- Ports Sara's `GeographicClusterer` clustering core behind the `Solver` interface: angular+radial multi-objective scoring → capacity-bounded angular sweep → min-cost-flow medoid refinement → per-cluster OR-Tools TSP (reusing `solve_tsp` from `kmedoids_ortools`, no duplication).
- Bug fixes vs. the original: `assert` → `ValueError` validation + `capacity>0` guard; removed the **duplicate `_assign_with_min_cost_flow`**; dropped dead methods, `visualize()`/CLI helpers, and per-call `print`s; made the iteration count configurable.
- Registered in `SOLVER_REGISTRY` as `sectorial`.

**Paper** (`docs/latex/optimization.tex`, `refs.bib`, figures)
- Adds the algorithm (now **6 algorithms / 72 runs**), refreshes **both result tables** and the scalability + comparison-grid figures from a coherent full re-run on current `main` (post polygon-clipping fix, so all rows are consistent — not just the new one).
- Adds a real **bibliography** (SBRP reviews, cluster-first-route-second, TSP heuristic) pulled via Mendeley, with citations woven into the intro and methods.
- Credits Sara Ruaga in the author line.

## Headline result
Under full coverage, **k-medoids+TSP and sectorial are the two best methods and are statistically tied**; sectorial reaches the lowest fleet distance at N=400 (464 vs 465 km) and the highest silhouette (tightest clusters) at scale, at the same latency as k-medoids.

## Verification
- `python -m py_compile` clean; adapter smoke test (N=50): full coverage, 0 capacity violations, valid depot-anchored routes.
- Full sweep: **72/72 runs `ok`**, no errors.
- Paper compiles (`latexmk` + bibtex), all 6 citations resolve, 4 pages.

author: johnramberger
body:
## Problem
The Webnovel **Popular** tab showed a romance-heavy list (mafia/werewolf/BL titles), not the main power ranking — and titles rendered with HTML entities like `Alpha's Regret`.

## Root cause
- `m.webnovel.com/ranking/.../power_rank` renders with **`sex=2`** (female-lead section) when no section param is given. Verified via the page's `__NEXT_DATA__` (`sex: 2`) and by fetching `?sex=1` vs `?sex=2`. Not a User-Agent issue.
- The `'` came from the JSON-LD `url` slug (`alpha's-regret-…`) being used as a title fallback when the `__NEXT_DATA__` title lookup missed — also explaining the wrong Title-Casing.

## Fix
- Pin the ranking section explicitly: `?sex=1` (male-lead, matching webnovel.com's default). UA-independent — works on the default mobile UA, no csrf needed for page 1.
- Add a `ConfigurableSource` **Switch** ("Female-lead Popular ranking", default off) so users can opt into the female-lead list.
- Parse the server-rendered `<a title="…">` anchors first (`parseBookList`) → clean, rank-ordered titles; JSON-LD / `__NEXT_DATA__` kept as fallbacks.
- `unescapeEntities()` the slug fallback as a backstop.

## Verification
Built + installed on emulator. Popular now: Slime Evolution → Investing in My Crippled Wife: … → Second Genesis → My Kingdom Building Done Right! → As A Mafia Boss… → THE GOD EATER → Last Gun Alchemist → … — matches webnovel.com, clean titles.

author: robotmarvin2026
body:
## Summary

`Memory MB` was the **only** anomaly metric in `health-monitor.sh`'s detection loop with `min_threshold=0` — every other metric already has an absolute floor below which a σ-deviation is never worth alerting (`CPU%`=80, `Load 1m`=2×vCPU, `Processes`=200). As a result the memory 2σ check would alert on *any* positive deviation regardless of how much RAM was actually in use.

The daily-peak baseline has been drifting slowly upward as the Marvin-Brain Docker stack caches settle — **1293→1392 MB over 2026-06-10..19, ~10 MB/day**. The lagging 7-day rolling baseline kept sitting just below the instantaneous reading, and with the stddev floored at 2% the current value poked past 2σ on **two consecutive days**:

```
2026-06-19  Memory MB = 1392  avg=1336.14  2.1σ
2026-06-20  Memory MB = 1410  avg=1347.14  2.3σ
```

…at only **~36% of 3915 MB total RAM, with 2.6 GB free**. Marginal, non-actionable noise that also feeds the log-alerting error-rate detector and the lessons-learned scanner.

## Change

Floor the memory alert at **60% of total RAM**, computed dynamically from the live `.memory.total` metric — exactly the way `_load_min_threshold` is computed from `nproc`:

```bash
_mem_total=$(echo "$metrics" | jq -r '.memory.total // 0' 2>/dev/null)
_mem_min_threshold=$(( _mem_total * 60 / 100 ))   # ≈ 2349 MB on this box
```

The 2σ check now fires only when memory is **both** statistically unusual **and** absolutely elevated.

## Why this is not weaker monitoring

- Genuine memory **pressure** is independently caught by the swap manager (available-MB check) and the resource-forecast in `metric-aggregate.sh`.
- The anomaly check's real job is catching a **sudden jump**; a slow leak is the forecaster's job, and the rolling baseline would track it anyway.
- **Fails safe:** `.memory.total // 0` → threshold `0` → prior no-mask behaviour if jq ever fails. Never crashes (bash treats empty as 0 in `$(())`).

## Verification

- `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S warning` clean.
- Isolated harness reproducing `_anomaly_check`'s threshold+σ logic: today's **1410** and yesterday's **1392** now **SUPPRESSED** (below 2349); a synthetic sudden spike to **2600 MB** still **ALERTs** at 46.5σ; the old threshold-0 path reproduces the actual logged 2.3σ WARN.
- Full `agent/self-test.sh`: **134 pass / 0 fail / 2 warn**, grade A, security A 95/100. Both warns are pre-existing and **not** regressions: the intentional `.gnupg` #737 tripwire (Pavel-gated), and the `config drift: cron` tripwire that the already-open **#793** fixes (deliberately untouched here).
- Did **not** run `health-monitor.sh` live mid-session (it writes `data/` every 5 min and can trigger a web rebuild); the change is pure threshold arithmetic in the anomaly branch, validated in isolation.

author: georgi
body:
## Phase 1 of the mobile improvement plan — reliability & networking foundation

The mobile app's feature surface (chat, workflow editor, assets, jobs) has outgrown its networking/error foundation. This phase hardens that foundation so the existing features survive real mobile networks. No user-facing features change; this is about resilience.

### What's in this PR

**1. Unify the WebSocket transport** (`services/WebSocketService.ts`)
The app shipped two divergent WebSocket stacks: `WebSocketManager` (chat — exponential backoff, jitter, connection timeout, outgoing message queue) and `WebSocketService` (workflows/jobs — `setInterval` polling to detect connection, linear backoff capped at 5 attempts, no queue). `WebSocketService` is now a thin multiplexing router over a single `WebSocketManager`, mirroring web's `GlobalWebSocketManager`. Its public API is unchanged, so `WorkflowRunner` needs no edits but inherits the robust transport. Multi-key routing (`workflow_id`/`job_id`/`thread_id`) invokes each handler at most once even when several ids match. New unit test covers reuse, routing/dedup, unsubscribe, send delegation, and path switching.

**2. Harden the HTTP client** (`services/api.ts`)
`request()` used a bare `fetch` with no timeout (could hang forever), no retry, and a stringly-typed error that hid the HTTP status. Added `ApiError { status, body }`, an `AbortController` timeout, and exponential-backoff retry for idempotent GET/HEAD on network errors and 5xx (4xx fail fast). Fixed `uploadAsset()` — the hand-set `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` dropped the boundary so the server couldn't parse uploads; it's now derived by React Native's fetch.

**3. Configure TanStack Query defaults** (`queryClient.ts`)
Was constructed with no options (`staleTime: 0`, blanket 3x retry incl. 4xx). Now: 30s staleTime, 5min gcTime, refetch on reconnect, and a retry policy that backs off transient failures but never retries 4xx.

**4. Chat error recovery** (`stores/ChatStore.ts`)
Added `clearError()` so an error state can be dismissed and retried, and changed the 5-minute send safety-timeout to surface a visible "response timed out" error instead of silently resetting status.

### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx oxlint src` — clean (one pre-existing warning, untouched)
- `npx jest` — **20 suites / 362 tests pass** (added 11 tests across `WebSocketService` and `ChatStore`)

### Follow-ups (later phases)
Moving the WS auth token out of the URL into a header and adding a 401 → re-auth interceptor are intentionally deferred to **Phase 2 (security & auth hardening)**, which stacks on this branch.

body:
Triage saw only each card's `indicators` + `distinguishingTest` — never the `benignLookalike`. But the dataset deliberately plants benign look-alikes (high-turnover business, salary/rent) that triage must **not** escalate, so the first pass couldn't discriminate and leaned entirely on the verifier to catch false escalates — depressing `accuracyVsLabels`.

## What changed
- Render each card's **benign look-alike** alongside its distinguishing test in the triage prompt.
- Instruct `_SYSTEM` to **rule out the benign look-alike before escalating** (data without instruction gets ignored).
- `dataSignals` left out — a separate field-mapping lever, out of scope here.

## Design notes
- **No ADR-0001 conflict:** the verifier's value is the *independent adversarial re-read on a different model*, not exclusive access to the look-alike — it stays meaningful.
- **Effect lands on the next `python -m data.precompute`** (committed `results.json` untouched; the demo serves it). Sharper triage could shift HERO-001's flagged outcome on regeneration — and `test_hero_cases.py` (the hero guard) verifies the demo narrative still holds, failing CI before a broken demo ships.

## Tests
1 new test asserts the triage prompt now carries the matched card's benign look-alike; existing triage test unchanged. Full backend suite: **69 passed**. Built TDD under the karpathy guidelines (surgical: a one-line system-prompt addition + one render line).

author: gpiroux
body:
## Epic 37 — Classic Offset+Total Paginated Team Listing

Replaces the merged cursor-paginated `GET /teams` backend with classic
offset+total pagination per ADR-032 (which supersedes ADR-031). `master` tip
(73993ae) shipped the cursor endpoint (`limit`/`cursor`/`next_cursor`); this
branch removes that cursor machinery and delivers a numbered-page contract:
`page`/`size` query params plus a `total_count` of the full owned set.

### Stories

- [x] 37-1-offset-total-paginated-get-teams — classic offset+total `GET /teams` (Relates to #319)

### What changed

- **Boundary model** — `TeamListResponse` gains required `total_count: int`; `next_cursor` removed (typed Pydantic, no `dict[str, Any]`).
- **Service** — `MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 500`; `TeamService.list_teams(*, user_id, page=1, size=250) -> tuple[list[Process], int]`: loads the full owned set via the existing `event_store.list_teams(user_id=...)`, sorts `(created_at, team_id)` DESC, computes `total = len(rows)` before slicing, clamps `size` to `[1, 500]` and `page` to `>= 1`, slices `rows[(page-1)*size : (page-1)*size + size]`, returns `(slice, total)`. Stateless; out-of-range page → `([], total)`.
- **Route** — `GET /teams` takes optional `page: int = 1` / `size: int = 250`, unpacks the tuple, returns `TeamListResponse(teams=[...], total_count=total)`.
- **V1 adapter** — `list_processes` requests `size=MAX_PAGE_SIZE` and ignores `total_count`, preserving its flat list-all behaviour.
- **Cursor machinery removed** — `TeamCursor`, `InvalidCursorError`, `_seek`, `DEFAULT_PAGE_LIMIT`, `MAX_PAGE_LIMIT`, `_MAX_CURSOR_LEN`, `next_cursor`. The merged Story-36.1 cursor tests were migrated/replaced with offset+total tests (page-1/total, page-N slice+order, out-of-range, ordering with `team_id` tiebreak, size clamp lo/hi/250, default/clamped page, statelessness incl. cross-replica).

### Review status

APPROVE (Rex). No HIGH/MEDIUM findings. AC #1–#16 all implemented; cursor backend fully removed with no dangling references; V1 list-all contract preserved.

**Local gate (submodule config):**
- `pytest packages/akgentic-infra/tests/` — 1578 passed, 39 skipped, 130 deselected; coverage 90.43% (≥ 80%).
- `ruff check packages/akgentic-infra/src/` — clean.
- `mypy --strict packages/akgentic-infra/src/` — no issues in 114 files.

### Scope guard

All changes are inside `packages/akgentic-infra/` (Golden Rule #4). The
`akgentic-team` `EventStore.list_teams` is consumed through its existing public
API only — no cross-submodule edit. The Phase-2 store-side offset/count pushdown
stays deferred to a separate `akgentic-team` epic.

### Replaces the merged cursor backend

This PR REPLACES the cursor-paginated `GET /teams` (Epic 36 / PR #318, merged to
`master`) with classic offset+total per ADR-032, which supersedes ADR-031. The
diff intentionally removes the cursor code and migrates its tests.

### Epic 37 slice complete

Epic 37 has a single story (37-1), delivered here. With this PR the epic's
infra-side contract (`page`/`size`/`total_count`) is complete. The frontend
classic paginated-table epic (akgentic-frontend Epic 28, ADR-032 §Decision 3)
consumes this `total_count` contract and is a separate submodule/epic.

Closes #319

body:
## 📚 Description

Bump `phel-lang/phel-lang` to `dev-main` (`0e032f0`) to get the latest Phel features (native-int arithmetic fast path, ^:pure inlining, bug fixes). The bump carries one breaking change: Phel removed the bare `argv` CLI-args var in favor of the earmuffed `*argv*`, so `main.phel` is updated to keep the build resolving.

## 🔖 Changes

- `composer.json`: `phel-lang/phel-lang` `^0.44` → `dev-main`
- `main.phel`: `argv` → `*argv*` (#2494 breaking)
- Verified: format + lint + 2291 tests + build green; game renders + runs

## ⚡ Free speedup (no code change)

The new native-int fast path (#2458/#2459) covers `+ - * / < =` **and `quot/rem/mod`**; #2460 drops the per-op `apply` round-trip on arithmetic + `bit-*` (~1.8-8x / ~26%). This makes every **native** numeric helper in warm per-frame code faster automatically: `mod` in render fade/scanline, `pos?`/`zero?`/`max` in combat/enemy/AI, native `+` in physics step. Captured just by bumping the version - no rewrite.

## 🧪 Hot-loop note

The tightest 4800-cell DDA/paint loop already uses `php/` interop, untouched. Measured native Phel arithmetic vs interop on dev-main: 100x slower (33.4s vs 0.33s, 3M ops) - so the fast path does NOT change the deepest loop, and converting interop→native would regress. engine/render carry zero native arithmetic. Only actionable hot-loop edit left (per-row `(mod r 2)` → `(php/& r 1)`) is marginal + risks floor-vs-trunc semantics; skipped.

author: groganz
body:
## What

The **GO/NO-GO gate** an operator runs **before** the owner arms `CINATRA_EXTENSION_REQUIRE_SIGNATURES=true` in production — the one remaining open item on the SDK-P0 trust-gate floor (eng#162).

It **simulates the flip** (`resolveSignatureVerdict(..., { required: true })`) over every live (`active|locked`) verdaccio install row **without touching any env or any row**, and reports a fleet-level `VERDICT: READY` / `VERDICT: NOT-READY`. The existing signature backfill *writes* signatures onto legacy rows; this *proves* the fleet would survive the flip. They are complementary (repair vs. confirmation).

## Why this is the remaining code work

The signing mechanism, the v2/closure downgrade-refusal, the backfill, and the marketplace-bootstrap-trust auto-flip (`allowMarketplaceBootstrapTrust = !signaturesRequired(env)`) are all already built. What was missing was a way to **confirm every active install carries a verifying signature** before the destructive flip — without it, arming the lever could deny activation to any still-unsigned (or zero-trusted-key) live install at next boot, fleet-wide.

## How

- `src/lib/extension-signature-readiness.ts` — read-only `assessSignatureReadiness()`. Uses the **exact** activation verdict path over the **canonical `packageName` column** (matching `runtime-package-loader.ts`, which feeds `rec.packageName`), threads stored `closureHash`/`signature` through unchanged, and:
  - hard-refuses a canonical-vs-`source.packageName` **identity drift** (`verdict: identity-drift`) before the crypto verdict;
  - **fail-closed key guard**: zero trusted keys => `ready: false` (with zero keys nothing verifies, so the flip would deny everything).
- `scripts/extensions/signature-readiness.mjs` + `pnpm extensions:signature-readiness` — prints the report + `VERDICT`, exits `0` (READY) / `1` (NOT-READY) / `2` (any throw → fail-closed NOT-READY), mirroring the ops `gatekept-install/preflight.sh` ergonomics. Runs with `--conditions=react-server` so the transitive `server-only` marker resolves to its no-op export.
- Unit tests: fleet verdict, key guard, per-row classification (verified/unverified/unsigned), identity-drift short-circuit, canonical-identity threading, fail-closed enumeration throw.

## Safety

Read-only by construction: no writes, no env mutation, no secret-value I/O (counts trusted keys by presence; reads only public, already-persisted anchor fields).

## Owner action (separate, queued)

Arming `CINATRA_EXTENSION_REQUIRE_SIGNATURES=true` in prod remains the irreducible owner action (a production security lever) — copy-paste-exact steps queued separately. A related ops `.env.template` parity fix (the template ships `REQUIRE=true` with empty signing keys) is queued too.

## Verification

- 15 new unit tests pass; full signature/trust suite (63 tests) green.
- ESLint clean; `tsc` clean on the new files.
- CLI empirically driven end-to-end past the `server-only` import chain into the real DB query (fail-closes to NOT-READY on an unreachable DB).
- codex-converged (GO; two HIGH concerns raised + fixed: server-only condition, identity drift).

Assisted-by: Codex (gpt-5.5)

author: mvillmow
body:
## Summary

Adds a new **planning-methodology** skill (`planning-bash-eval-to-positional-args-injection-fix`, v1.0.0, category `architecture`) capturing how to safely PLAN a bash shell-injection remediation that replaces `eval \"\$cmd\"` with positional-parameter expansion `\"\$@\"` in a retry/wrapper helper. Sourced from Odysseus meta-repo issue #190 (`retry()` in `e2e/lib/common.sh`).

This is a CREATE (no existing skill covered planning an `eval`→`\"\$@\"` injection fix; the existing `bash-command-substitution-eval-silent-failure-untestable` skill covers a different topic — untestable command-substitution failure paths).

## Verification

- `verification: unverified` — this captures a plan that was authored but **never executed**: no commands ran against the working tree, the canary test was authored but not run, and `pixi run just lint` / shellcheck were never invoked. The workflow section carries a prominent unverified/"Proposed Workflow" warning banner. (The literal `## Verified Workflow` heading is retained because the repo's `scripts/validate_plugins.py` requires that exact section name.)
- `python3 scripts/validate_plugins.py` → **470/470 valid**, including this new skill.
- Pre-commit hooks passed on commit.

## Key Findings (durable learnings)

1. **Signature reorder is mandatory.** `\"\$@\"` can only capture an arbitrary-length command if it is the trailing varargs slot, so the helper must become `func MAX SLEEP COMMAND...` and `shift`. Mirror an existing in-repo `\"\$@\"` idiom (here `_agamemnon_curl_retry`).
2. **\"Zero call sites → reorder is free\" is the highest-risk, grep-fragile claim.** A plain `grep -rn retry` conflates DEFINITION with INVOCATIONS, may not descend into submodule working trees, and misses dynamic/out-of-repo callers. Distinguish def vs invocation and widen with `git submodule foreach --recursive`; reviewer should re-run independently.
3. **Reusing an existing lint gate (DRY) is sound only after verifying coverage** — confirm the `justfile` shellcheck gate's awk path filter includes `e2e/` and the new tracked test file.
4. **Prove safety with a positive canary test**, not by grepping that `eval` was removed: pass a `\$(touch <mktemp -u sentinel>)` argument and assert the sentinel file never exists.

## Test Plan

- [x] `python3 scripts/validate_plugins.py` passes (470/470).
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass.
- [x] Frontmatter complete (name, description with `Use when:` triggers, category `architecture`, date 2026-06-20, version 1.0.0, user-invocable false, verification unverified, tags).
- [x] All required sections present (Overview, When to Use, Verified Workflow incl. `### Quick Reference`, Failed Attempts table with 4 rows, Results & Parameters).

author: danielpolowork
body:
## Summary

Adds a new trilingual blog post analysing **Mistral's physics AI** (built on the absorbed Emmi AI team) — learned surrogate models that predict full physical fields in seconds where CFD/FEM solvers took cluster-hours.

- **Slug:** `mistral-physics-ai` · **Date:** 2026-05-27 · **Themes:** AI, machine learning, engineering, manufacturing
- Four-section architect-voice analysis (Deep dive / Debate / Critique / Summary) in **en / ja / zh**
- `posts/index.json` regenerated via `tools/reindex.mjs` (now 19 posts)

## Angle

The distinct spine: **physics made affordable, not new.** The constraint was never the math — "true design-space exploration is mathematically possible but economically impossible" — it was cost. Physics AI is the engineering-simulation instance of the pattern running through the whole series: recast an exact, expensive computation as a fast approximation **plus a verification tail**, and the bottleneck moves to verification.

Threads from the authoring brief:
- **AI vs. solver advantages/limits**: PDE/mesh/HPC hours-to-weeks vs. seconds on one GPU.
- **Exploratory design**: the precision-first → recall-first phase change (cheap evaluation flips the search strategy).
- **Accuracy vs. PDE solvers**: the crux — solvers have error guarantees; surrogates are accurate only in-distribution, and the dangerous failure is a confident wrong prediction on the out-of-distribution geometry exploration most wants.
- **Can it fully replace solvers?**: no — parasitic on them (they generate training data *and* verify); hybrid by design.
- **Manufacturing efficiency**: joint tooling/process optimization, defects predicted before any tool is cut.
- **Real-time digital twins**: the genuinely new capability — physics extended from design-time into run-time.
- **Under-sold prize**: inverse design (a fast forward model makes performance→geometry optimization viable).

Completes a three-piece Mistral arc (Search Toolkit → Vibe → physics AI = retrieval, agent, engineering surrogate, one enterprise stack), and the verification-tail thesis links back to the Co-Scientist and AlphaFold posts.

## Notes

- Only `posts/**` changed — no `src/dist/**` edits, so no version bump / pre-push hook needed.
- Branched off current `master` (PRs #16–#27 merged).

body: ## Summary This PR completes the backend support for product autocomplete from user history. The API now returns product suggestions from the authenticated user’s purchase history, prioritizing frequent products and exposing pricing data required by the mobile autocomplete flow. ## Type of change * [x] Backend * [ ] Mobile * [ ] UI ## Related issue Closes #44 ## What was done? Implemented and aligned the product suggestion backend flow. ### Product suggestions Updated: ```http GET /api/product-suggestions?query={q} ``` The endpoint now supports: * authenticated user scope; * required `query`; * history-first product suggestions; * most frequent products first; * `source` field using `history` or `ai`; * `estimatedPrice` from user history when available; * `lastPrice`; * `averagePrice`; * `purchaseFrequency`. ### Product history Added: ```http GET /api/product-history ``` The endpoint returns the authenticated user’s product history as a read-only dataset. Product history is still derived from confirmed expenses with item details and is not created or edited directly. ### Error handling Added backend handling for: * `401 Unauthorized`; * `400 Bad Request` when query is invalid; * `429 Too Many Requests` when the rate limit is exceeded; * `502 Bad Gateway` when AI fallback is unavailable. ### API contract Updated `Contracts/openapi.yaml` to match the implemented product suggestion and product history response shapes. ## Files changed Main files: * `ProductSuggestionsController.cs` * `ProductHistoryController.cs` * `ProductSuggestionService.cs` * `ProductSuggestionMapper.cs` * `ProductSuggestionRepository.cs` * `ProductSuggestionResponse.cs` * `ProductHistoryQueryRequest.cs` * `ProductHistoryResponse.cs` * `PaginatedProductHistoryResponse.cs` * `ProductSuggestionRateLimitException.cs` * `ProductSuggestionServiceUnavailableException.cs` * `IProductSuggestionRepository.cs` * `IProductSuggestionService.cs` * `Contracts/openapi.yaml` ## Evidence Swaguer endpoints ## Notes for reviewer There was no existing AI provider available in the backend. author: rbaumier
body:
Closes #4842

`no-duplicate-comments` flagged the identical `///` doc-comments that RustCrypto/block-ciphers carries on its parallel AES backends (`fixslice64.rs` vs `fixslice32.rs`, etc.), where each file re-exposes the same-named function (`aes128_decrypt`, …) with the same description. That description documents the same item across parallel implementations, not a copy-paste that drifts.

Empirically the firing collisions are all cross-file between two same-named declarations in parallel backend files — the variant token (128/192/256) sits inside the prefix bucket key, so different key sizes never collide; only same-name-across-backends does.

## Fix
- Capture, per comment, the name of the declaration it immediately precedes — only for doc-comments (`///`, `//!`, `/**`, `/*!`), not plain `//` / `/*` (incidental prose).
- In the bucket-matching loop, skip a near-duplicate match when it is cross-file and both comments document a declaration of the same name.

## Still flagged (guards)
- Intra-file duplicate doc on the same name (botched copy-paste before rename).
- Identical doc over differently-named declarations across files.
- Copy-pasted free-floating (non-doc) rationale above a same-named decl.

## Tests
6 module tests added/updated (Rust + TS); 31/31 in `comment_duplicate_detection` pass. Self-reviewed via quality-bar: no blockers/majors.
