author: sukarenormous-ship-it
body:
## Summary
Adds a small, self-contained demo (`kalman_q_demo.py`) that illustrates the
process-noise (`Q`) tuning trade-off when using a Kalman filter to estimate a
time-varying hedge ratio in a pairs-trading / statistical-arbitrage setting.

The script builds a controlled synthetic cointegrated pair (known half-life,
slowly drifting true hedge ratio) and runs the Kalman filter at three `Q`
levels, reporting:

- **beta jitter** (daily noise in the estimated hedge ratio)
- **beta turnover** (Σ|Δβ| — proxy for re-hedging cost if you re-hedge daily)
- **number of signal-driven trades** and net P&L (hedge locked at entry)

### Key takeaways the demo makes concrete
- High `Q` makes beta ~6× more jittery → ~6× re-hedge turnover.
- Locking the hedge ratio at entry keeps cost negligible regardless of estimate churn.
- Too-high `Q` doesn't cause whipsaw here — it inflates the innovation variance
  and compresses the z-score until it never triggers (signal dies).
- Low `Q` tracks the true beta smoothly and captures the mean-reversion edge.

A comparison plot is saved to `kalman_q_demo.png`.

> Note: this is an illustrative synthetic demo — P&L is in raw spread units, so
> absolute returns are not meaningful; only the *relative* comparison across `Q`
> (jitter, turnover, trade count) should be read as the lesson.

author: inafev
body:
## Residual drift after PR #401
After the PR Guardian drift fix, the only remaining `develop ↔ master` diff in `v2-docs/` was a 1-line **`<lastBuildDate>`** in `feed.xml`: `src/rss_generator.py` set it to `datetime.utcnow()`, so every republish rewrote it even when the digest was unchanged.

## Fix
Derive `lastBuildDate` from the digest's **`_meta.last_updated`** (the actual analysis date) — falling back to the most recent item date, then a fixed constant. The feed is now a **pure function of its input**: regenerating unchanged content yields byte-identical output. Mirrors the existing `v2_optimizer` pattern that prefers `_meta.last_updated` over file mtime.

## Validation
- Ran `python -m src.rss_generator` twice (2s apart) → **byte-identical `feed.xml`** (sha256 match).
- The feed now only changes when the digest content actually changes (weekly), reconciling cleanly at each release.

author: jhosm
body:
## In plain English

We're closing the old task to fold the EventCatalog "static site" into our single GitHub Pages site, because that site no longer exists — it was replaced by Backstage, which is a separately-running portal, not a static site you can stitch into a web page. This PR just updates the one ADR whose text still described the old plan as pending, so the docs match reality. Nothing about how the site is published changes.

## Summary

Closing bd `ra1u` ("compose EventCatalog into the docs-site Pages artifact") surfaced stale prose in **ADR-PC-026 §P5** and its row-3 commitment, which still named the EventCatalog-on-Pages composition as pending future work ("revisit when G.4 lands"). That premise was retired when G.4/PR #110 superseded **ADR-IC-008** (EventCatalog) with the Accepted **ADR-IC-015** (Backstage). Backstage is a separately-deployed runtime portal (host deploy deferred under `s4ol.1`), not a static artifact that can be composed into a Pages subpath, so the task can never trigger.

- **§P5** — appended a dated `*Revised 2026-06-20*` line recording the supersession and withdrawing the EventCatalog-on-Pages task (bd `ra1u`), and **generalised the still-live invariant**: this workflow owns the one Pages slot; any future catalogue portal published to Pages composes under a subpath — never a second `deploy-pages`.
- **Verifiable-commitments row 3** — re-worded the commitment prose to the generic invariant; **deliberately kept** the `DOCS_PAGES_SINGLE_SLOT` Test ID and the `Gap` (review-discipline) status, because the invariant is still live and honoured by construction (`docs-site.yml` is the sole Pages publisher; EventCatalog's deploy is retired; Backstage never targets Pages).

No status flip and no row removal: the single-Pages-slot invariant is still load-bearing, so `Gap` (review-enforced) remains the honest status — only the dead EventCatalog premise is dropped.

## Testing

- `make docs-verify` — green ("reference/ is up to date (17 pages)"); title/status/links unchanged so no generated-reference drift.
- lychee `--offline --include-fragments` on the amended ADR — 18 OK, 0 errors (both new ADR-IC links resolve).
- Single-file diff (12 insertions, 1 deletion).

## ADRs touched/honoured

- **Amends ADR-PC-026** (Proposed) — §P5 + row 3 prose, via an appended dated `*Revised*` line (honouring the §D5 append-not-rewrite convention even though Proposed status doesn't strictly require it).
- **Honours ADR-IC-015** (Accepted, EventCatalog→Backstage supersession) — the change records this supersession rather than diverging silently from it.
- **Honours ADR-PC-020 §D3** (explicit-drift gate) — this is the paired drift-acknowledgement that lets bd `ra1u` close without leaving the catalogue asserting a dead premise.

author: lemmit
body:
Within-architecture refinement to the Angular `Action(inst.op)` renderer, applying an external reviewer's "dumb template" feedback. **Stays DI-native** — no TanStack (the deliberate, test-enforced Angular data-layer decision is untouched; `project-shape.test.ts` still asserts `@tanstack/angular-query-experimental` is absent).

## What

Both Action shapes (with / without `then:`) now render the same idiomatic **dumb template** — one event, one method call:

```html
<button (click)='onCancelOrder()' [disabled]='cancelOrder.isPending()'>Cancel</button>
```

The page-shell emits a component method that reads the record id **inside** the method (a `?.id` access + early-return guard), so there's no in-markup side effect and the `<op>Id` capture signal goes away — it was only ever a workaround for method-scope `this`-prefixing:

```ts
async onCancelOrder(): Promise<void> {
  const id = this.orderById.data()?.id;
  if (!id) return;
  await this.cancelOrder.mutate(id, {});
  this.router.navigateByUrl("/");   // the optional then: effect
}
```

This **unifies** the two previous forks (no-then → inline `mutate`; then → id-capture signal + method) into one shape, and adds the pending-disabled binding. `this.`-prefixing stays string-literal-safe, so a route like `"/orders/:id"` is left intact.

## Why not the reviewer's headline (TanStack Angular Query)?

The hint's primary suggestion was to adopt TanStack `injectQuery`/`injectMutation`. That **reverses** this project's deliberate, documented, test-enforced decision that the Angular data layer is DI-native signals — so I deliberately did **not** apply it. Only the within-architecture refinements (dumb template, read-id-in-method, drop the capture signal, `?.id` guard, `[disabled]=isPending()`) are taken here.

## Verification

- **Real `ng build` green** on a project carrying both a no-`then` `Action` and a `then: navigate(...)` `Action` on a `byId` QueryView record.
- `walked-pages.test.ts` updated: both Action cases now assert the dumb-template method shape + `not.toContain("cancelOrderId")`.
- Full `npm test` (5564) + biome clean. Only the Angular renderer + page-shell change — no shared-walker edit, so the other frontends are byte-identical.

author: topi-banana
body:
## Summary

google-java-format keeps a block / Javadoc comment that is written *inside* a
construct — with code on the same line right before and after it — exactly where
it was written, e.g. the marker comment in:

```java
java.lang./* @MarkerAnnotation */ String s = null;
```

jals attached such a comment as a **trailing** comment of the preceding token and
emitted it as a line suffix, which flushes it to the end of the line:

```java
java.lang.String s = null; /* @MarkerAnnotation */
```

That relocation is the only divergence on the gjf golden file
`testdata/N.output`. As with every other gjf divergence in this repo, this adds a
new opt-in config key rather than changing jals's default comment placement.

Related issue: N/A.

## What changed

A new `inline-block-comments` option (bool, default `false`). When on, a block /
doc comment written immediately before a significant token **on the same line**
hugs that token (reusing the existing `leading_inline` machinery) instead of
trailing the previous token to end of line. Layout-only — only comment trivia
moves; the significant-token sequence is preserved exactly. Line comments run to
end of line, so they are never followed by a same-line token and are unaffected.

`jals-fmt/src/config/mod.rs`, `config/tests.rs`:

- New `inline_block_comments` field on `Config` (default `false`) with a
  doc-comment, a kebab-case parse test, and a default assertion.

`jals-fmt/src/comments.rs`:

- In `build()`, a block / doc comment is flagged `inline` (→ `leading_inline`,
  hugging the following token) when a new `followed_by_same_line_sig` lookahead
  finds a significant token on the same line after it. The condition keys purely
  on the *following* token, not the preceding one: the hug glues the comment to
  its token with one space and no break, so the property survives reformatting and
  the hug is idempotent (keying on the preceding token's line would flip once the
  following token wraps onto its own line).

`jals-fmt/src/lower/mod.rs`:

- Thread `cfg.inline_block_comments` into `comments::build`.

`jals-tests/src/golden.rs`:

- Enable `inline_block_comments` in the Google Java Style preset
  (`google_config()`) + a defaults assertion. This is what makes `N.output` match.

`jals-fmt/README.md`:

- Document the new key in the comment-placement prose, the option table, and the
  "what's wired" matrix.

## Invariants

Formatter-only change, consistent with CLAUDE.md:

- **Significant-token sequence** is preserved exactly — this option moves only
  comment trivia (a comment's attachment / emission position), never a significant
  token. It is **not** one of the seven options that relax the exact-sequence
  guarantee.
- **Comments are never dropped** — every comment is still anchored exactly once;
  the option only changes whether a same-line comment trails the previous token or
  hugs the following one.
- **Idempotency** holds — the hug keeps the comment glued to its following token,
  so re-parsing reclassifies it identically. Caught a non-idempotent earlier draft
  (which keyed on the preceding token's line) via the new proptest and corrected
  it.
- **wasm32** unaffected — uses only `rowan` token traversal (`next_token`), no new
  deps or host-only IO.

## Testing

- `jals-fmt/tests/formatter.rs`: snapshot tests — an embedded marker stays in
  place, consecutive embedded comments both hug, a comment followed by a newline is
  *not* hugged (stays relocated), the option-off default still relocates, and an
  idempotency check.
- `jals-fmt/tests/invariants.rs`: an `inline_block_config()` plus property tests
  for idempotency, significant-token-sequence preservation, and comment-multiset
  preservation.
- `jals-tests/src/golden.rs`: `google_config()` defaults assertion updated.
- End-to-end: `jals fmt --config ./jals-fmt.toml --check …/testdata/N.output` now
  exits 0 (previously failed on the relocated marker comment).
- Full CI suite passes locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`,
  `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `taplo fmt --check`, `cargo machete`,
  the `wasm32` build (`jals-syntax` + `jals-fmt`), and `xtask codegen --check`.

Note: the local `jals-fmt.toml` Google-style preset is intentionally left
untracked (the canonical preset is `google_config()` in `golden.rs`).

author: man7a-afk
body:
Closes #49


Summary
Implements full keyboard interaction across the three main list views — recent events, watchlist, and notification rules. Uses the roving tabindex pattern so only one row is in the natural tab order at a time, with arrow keys moving focus between rows. All lists are now properly labelled for screen readers.

Changes
use-keyboard-list.ts
 (new) Shared hook that encapsulates the roving tabindex pattern. Exposes listRef and getRowProps(index) to spread onto each row. Keyboard contract:

ArrowDown / ArrowUp — move focus to next / previous row
Home / End — jump to first / last row
Enter / Space — bubbles naturally to child buttons and links
Each row receives role="option", aria-posinset, and aria-setsize so assistive technologies announce the row's position within the list.

src/app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx Recent events <ul> gains role="listbox" and aria-label="Recent events". Each <li> receives keyboard row props and a descriptive aria-label composed from event name, contract, chain, and delivery status.

src/app/(app)/watchlist/page.tsx Watched contracts list updated with role="listbox" and aria-label="Watched contracts". Each row aria-label describes the contract name, chain, and active/paused state.

src/app/(app)/rules/page.tsx Rules grid converted from <div>/<div> to semantic <ul>/<li>. Gets role="listbox" and aria-label="Notification rules". Each row aria-label announces the rule name, status, and 24h trigger count.

Acceptance Criteria
Criterion	Status
Rows are focusable	✅ Roving tabindex — first row is in tab order, rest reachable via arrow keys
Arrow keys navigate records	✅ ArrowDown/Up move focus, Home/End jump to ends
Screen reader compatibility is preserved	✅ role="listbox/option", aria-setsize, aria-posinset, and aria-label on every row
Testing
Open /dashboard, /watchlist, or /rules
Tab into the list — focus should land on the first row with a visible ring
Press ArrowDown — focus moves to the next row
Press ArrowUp — focus moves back
Press End — focus jumps to the last row; Home returns to the first
Press Tab inside a focused row — focus moves to the next interactive element inside the row (button, link), not the next row
Use a screen reader (VoiceOver / NVDA) — each row should be announced with its position, e.g. "Transfer on USDC, Ethereum, status delivered, 1 of 10"

body:
## Summary
Resolves all 36 pre-existing TypeScript strict-mode errors across 10 Convex files. These were silently accumulating since the project started and became visible once the import-path bugs (#6, #7, #8) were fixed and production builds could finally reach the `tsc` typecheck step.

### Changes per file
| File | Error class | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `schema.ts` | Missing type literals in `agentThoughts.type` union | Added `action/complete/error/warning/thinking/finding` — matching the mutation validator that already accepted them |
| `benchmark.ts` | `callAIWithFallback` return type has no `usage` field | Remove `usage` destructuring; replace token fields with `undefined` |
| `buildLoop.ts` | Implicit `any` on array callbacks (stale generated types) | Annotate `f: any` on callback params |
| `crossProject.ts` | Same | Annotate `m/i/t/a/b/p: any` on callback params |
| `engine.ts` | `api` imported three times (TS2300 Duplicate identifier) | Remove the two redundant re-imports |
| `errorIngestion.ts` | `ctx.db.get()` called inside an `action` (real runtime bug — actions lack `ctx.db`) | Add `internalQuery getIncidentById`; use `ctx.runQuery` in the action |
| `gitops.ts` | Handler infers `ciStatus: string` but validator requires the literal union | Add `as const` to each `ciStatus` return value |
| `http.ts` | Broken `Parameters<typeof internal.swarm.logEventsBatch>` conditional type | Simplify to `as any[]` |
| `reflection.ts` | Implicit `any` callbacks | Annotate `m/r/s: any` on callback params |
| `suggestions.ts` | `callAI(prompt, 4000, ...)` passed `number` where `model: string` expected; implicit-any filter callbacks | Fix arg order to `callAI(prompt, undefined, 4000, byok)` + annotate callbacks |

## Notable
`errorIngestion.ts` was a real runtime bug (not just a type error): the `autoFix` action called `ctx.db.get()` which doesn't exist on action contexts. This would have thrown at runtime if `autoFix` was ever triggered. Now fixed to use an internal query via `ctx.runQuery`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p convex/tsconfig.json` — 0 errors (down from 36)
- [ ] Production deploy succeeds with `--typecheck enable` (can re-enable in `vercel.json` after this merges)

body:
Continues the **Lifecycle-pillar deep program** (Spec 338), building on the substrate hardening (339a, PR #215) and the transition events + engine wiring (344 / 339a-cont, PR #228, merged).

## Spec 340 — enforced A2A transition table (the state machine)

Hardens the substrate `Lifecycle.move` (the sole state writer, Spec 339) with an enforced transition table, so the A2A machine stops being decorative — any state can no longer jump to any state.

- **`agency/_lifecycle_data/transitions.json`** — the base table as **data** (`# AGENCY-DRIFT: lifecycle-transitions`), validated against `LifecycleState` at load (a typo is a startup error, not a silent gap).
- **`agency/_lifecycle_transitions.py`** — pure, engine-free module: typed `IllegalTransition{from_state, to_state, allowed}`, `assert_transition`, `extend_table` (monotone union + terminal-floor: a graph override can never remove a base edge nor reopen a terminal state), `terminal_states`.
- `Lifecycle.move` asserts the transition **before** writing, reading a graph override (`Artefact{kind:"transition-table"}`, the `shell.define` pattern, Spec 075) per-move with seed fallback. The three routed writers (delegate / gate / `lifecycle_gate`) inherit enforcement for free.
- 6 acceptance scenarios: legal succeeds · terminal→illegal with `allowed=[]` · skip raises · seed table internally consistent · override read + floor-safe · override can't reopen a terminal.

> **Grounded table refinement** (not a magic-number edit — CLAUDE.md #8): the spec sketch's `submitted: [working, canceled]` rejected `submitted→input-required`, which broke 15 real consumer gate tests (music/prompt) — a **pre-flight readiness gate fires before work starts** and pauses a freshly-opened (`submitted`) lifecycle. So `submitted` also reaches `input-required`/`auth-required`. The invariant the spec defends — *no `completed` without passing `working`* — stays intact (`submitted` still can't skip to `completed`/`failed`).

> **Deferred to 339b:** the B3 static drift-guard (fails CI on a raw state-write outside `lifecycle.py`) waits until `subagent`/`music` writers are routed through `move`. Parameterization variant data lands in 342.

## Merge `main`

Merges `origin/main` (Specs 348 frugal-capability-port, 349 pillar-event-bus, 350 relevance-filter). The only conflict was `TODO.md` (resolved: keep main's new 348/349/350 rows + my 340 update to the lifecycle row). `engine.py` auto-merged cleanly (349's `_pre_tool_use_handler` + my Spec 344 monitor-before-lifecycle init). The two event systems are complementary — 349's `agency/_events.py` is a **hook** event bus (frugal first-use-once); 344 is the **lifecycle-transition** event bus on `move`.

## Verification

- 6 new acceptance scenarios; full pre-merge suite **1283 passed**.
- Post-merge: reinstall (`frugal` cap from main) + smoke (lifecycle move/close + `_events` bus coexist) + lifecycle/gate/delegate (51) green + `scripts/check-drift` clean. Full post-merge suite running.
- CORE.md / lifecycle reference doc + TODO.md + spec Followup updated (rule 4); `scripts/check-no-truncate` + `scripts/check-doc-drift` clean.

## Next (not in this PR)

339b: migrate the remaining unguarded writers (`subagent`, `music`) through `move` (unblocks the deferred B3 drift-guard); `SessionLifecycle`→`session` parameterization (Q4); then 341's `watch` consumer of the 344 trail + 342's parameterization variant data.

author: vlakir
body:
Implements T043.

## Проблема

`domain/keys.py` строил составные ключи (`make_source_key` /
`make_dedup_key` / `make_idempotency_key`) простым colon-concat — **не
инъективно**, если компонент содержит разделитель `:`. Реально для Matrix:

- `make_source_key('matrix','acc','!room:server')` ≡
  `make_source_key('matrix','acc','!room', thread_id='server')` →
  `matrix:acc:!room:server` для обоих кортежей;
- тот же класс в `dedup_key` (Matrix event-id `$id:server` как `external_id`)
  и `idempotency_key` (Matrix-комната как `target.address`).

Следствие — схлопывание состояния реестра/курсоров/дедупа/outbox разных
источников. Долг из ревью CodeRabbit на PR #41 (T041), пред-существующий
(функция идентична до и после T041).

## Решение

Общий `_escape` (`\` → `\\`, затем `:` → `\:`) для каждого нетерминального
компонента ключа. Единственные неэкранированные `:` становятся структурными
разделителями → разбор однозначен, отображение «кортеж → ключ» инъективно.
Терминальные компоненты (`slot` в EDITED, `n` в idempotency) не экранируются —
после них ничего нет, инъективность держится и так. `->` в idempotency-ключе —
зарезервированный структурный маркер.

**Scope расширен** с исходного «только make_source_key» (формулировка BOARD)
до всего класса ключей — согласовано с Разработчиком, зафиксировано в ADR.

## Миграция — чистый разрыв формата (без Alembic data-миграции)

- Схема БД **не меняется** (типы/PK те же) — меняются только значения вновь
  записываемых ключей.
- Для компонентов без `:`/`\` (числовые Telegram chat-id, имена транспортов/
  аккаунтов) `_escape` — **no-op**: Telegram-персистентность байт-в-байт
  прежняя. Меняются только Matrix-ключи (ровно багованные).
- Старый формат **в принципе неоднозначен** (это и есть баг) → точная
  миграция значений невозможна. Проект pre-alpha, релиза с Matrix не было,
  затронуто лишь локальное catch-up-состояние (регенерируемо одним проходом;
  at-least-once на outbound прикрывает). Прецедент big-bang без алиасов — T041.

ADR 2026-06-20 в `DECISIONS.md`.

## Acceptance

- [x] Разные кортежи `(transport, account_id, address, thread_id)` дают разные
      ключи при `:` в любом компоненте (тесты на коллизию Matrix-room-id /
      event-id / target-address зелёные).
- [x] Telegram golden-ключи байт-в-байт сохранены (no-op для colon-free).
- [x] Существующие данные: разрыв обоснован (см. ADR), схема не тронута.
- [x] `mypy --strict` чист, coverage 96.51% (≥ 90), 1123 теста зелёные,
      ruff/format чисты.

## Update

CHANGELOG (`### Changed`, breaking), DECISIONS (ADR), BOARD (Doing→Done),
BACKLOG (T043 убран). Пример не требуется — `keys.py` внутренняя
инфраструктура, пользователь не вызывает её напрямую (§17.9).

body:
**[e2e-coder]** — #1912 **b** (control-IR op gate — the common-path half). #1912a (#1920) merged. This closes the **larger** half: the DEFAULT (json-mode) skill phase dispatches ops via `ControlIRExecutor.execute` — the common path a narrowed agent's skill takes.

## What
Gates the control-IR op dispatch through the **SAME shared check** as the chat / phase RouterLoop (`effective.tool_contextually_denied`) → contextual narrowing is enforced on **every** tool path, bypass-impossible by construction.

- **`contextual_gate.py`**: `op_kind_tool_names` (op kind ∪ chat-tool qualified aliases) + `op_contextually_denied`. The op kind is **always** a name candidate → an un-aliased kind still gates on its own name (no silent bypass). `_OP_KIND_ALIASES` is **exhaustive over `ALL_OP_KINDS`** (pinned — steer 1).
- **`control_ir_executor.execute`**: a pre-handler gate denies a contextually-denied op (`status="denied"` / `tool_excluded`, decision-enabling) before the handler runs.
- **Threading**: `OSRuntime → ControlIRExecutor → OpContext`, completing the `Session→SkillRuntime→OSRuntime` chain from #1912a.

## Mapping (steer 1 — every deny-set entry accounted for)
`sandboxed_exec` / `mcp_install` (dangerous, **have** op kinds) → gated via **both** qualified (`exec__sandboxed_exec`, `mcp__install_*`) + unwrapped forms. `delegate` / memory-writes have **no** op kind → router-only (the chat gate covers them).

## Test plan (real ControlIRExecutor + real execute(), no mocks)
- [x] **Mapping completeness** over `ALL_OP_KINDS` (steer 1) + op-kind self-named.
- [x] Dangerous deny entries reach their ops (qualified + unwrapped).
- [x] The **REAL `execute()`** denies a denied op; un-narrowed does **not** (CLEAN RED contrast). **Falsification-verified**: removing the gate reds the deny test (reverted).
- [x] **Threading-flows** (steer 3): a narrowed **OSRuntime** threads contextual to its `ControlIRExecutor` so the op is blocked — proving the contextual **flows through skill execution**, not just the gate in isolation.
- [x] Byte-identical: control-IR/kernel/skill suites **245 passed**; tier-audit + ruff clean.

## Result
With #1912a + #1912b, `effective.py` is the **truly single tool gate** across chat + phase + control-IR — the phase-path bypass is closed (the over-claim corrected).

Forward: per-MCP-verb deny for the generic `mcp` op; #1199 `require_tool` static-authority live-wiring. Refs #1912. **Closes #1912.** S4b (#1827 context-auto) resumes next.

author: d-morrison
body:
## What

Vendors pinned copies of the lab manual's authored fragments and `@`-imports them into `CLAUDE.md`:

- `shared/vendored/prompt-formats.md`, `shared/vendored/copilot-review-before-human.md` — byte-identical copies of the upstream files.
- `shared/vendored/MANIFEST.json` — source repo, per-file pinned commit, and content `sha256`.
- `scripts/check-vendored-drift.py` — recomputes each copy's hash and asserts it matches the manifest; wired into `validate.yml`.
- `check-links.py` now also scans `shared/**/*.md`.
- `CLAUDE.md` gains two `@`-import sections; `README.md` documents `shared/vendored/`.

## Why

This is the **manual → ai-config** direction of the two-way sync (UCD-SERG/lab-manual#331 authored the fragments). ai-config can't add the manual as a submodule — the manual already submodules this repo, and a mutual submodule would recurse — so it keeps a vendored copy instead.

## Design notes

- **Network-free drift check.** The manifest carries a content `sha256` per file, so `check-vendored-drift.py` catches hand-edits to the vendored copies without any network call in core CI (no flakiness). Verifying freshness against upstream is the sync workflow's job, not every-PR CI's.
- **Byte-identical copies.** The vendored files carry no "do not edit" header, so their hash matches upstream exactly; the "don't edit here" guidance lives in the README and manifest.

## Verification

```
$ python3 scripts/check-vendored-drift.py   # ✓ 2 vendored file(s) match their manifest hashes
$ python3 scripts/validate-skills.py        # PASS
$ python3 scripts/check-links.py            # ✓ no broken relative links (114 files)
```

## Follow-up

author: elementalcollision
body:
## Problem

`tests/test_critic_gate.py`'s module docstring contract is **"no live providers"**, but `check_commit_critic` builds a *real* cross-model escalator (`_default_escalator` → `_build_reviewer`) when `escalator is None`. With a populated `.env` in the environment, `escalator=None` therefore becomes "a real opus escalator" rather than "none available" — so `test_failclosed_unparseable_then_no_escalation_blocks` flaked: the fail-closed "needs human review" path never fired because a real escalator ran and rejected, yielding the generic "NOT faithful" reason instead.

Reproduced on clean `main` (changes stashed): **passes in keyless CI, fails locally with keys.** Surfaced during the ADR 0185 graduation suite run.

## Fix

An autouse fixture pins `_default_escalator → None`, so the no-escalator paths are deterministic regardless of ambient API keys (matches the keyless CI environment). Tests that exercise escalation already inject their own escalator explicitly, so the rescue/escalation paths are unaffected.

## Verification

`tests/test_critic_gate.py` — **24/24 green both with and without a populated `.env`.**

author: thomas-adam-leigh
body:
Closes [ARC-18](https://linear.app/leigh-dev/issue/ARC-18/auth-and-user-bootstrap-provisioning-first-thread-on-signup) — **Auth & user bootstrap** milestone of the AG-UI Interaction Substrate.

## What

Extends the existing `auth.users → public.users` provisioning trigger (`handle_new_user`) to also open the user's **first `threads` row** in the same transaction. An authenticated session now lands on an empty conversation ready for first contact — the unit every AG-UI client subscribes to and every run lives on.

- **Migration** `20260620120000_bootstrap_first_thread.sql`: `create or replace function public.handle_new_user()` adding `insert into public.threads (user_id) values (new.id)`. `SECURITY DEFINER` + empty `search_path` preserved; objects schema-qualified. No table/column change → generated types unchanged → drift gate stays green.
- **`listThreads(db, userId)`** query helper for the substrate's per-user thread reads (consumed next by the run endpoint, ARC-19).
- **Integration smoke test** `auth-bootstrap.test.ts` proving the acceptance criteria:
  - signup round-trip: an `auth.users` insert provisions a `public.users` row **and exactly one** bootstrap thread;
  - threads RLS: `auth.uid()` resolves from the JWT `sub` claim and each `authenticated` user reads back **only their own** thread (cross-user isolation).

## Decision

Implemented the **trigger-bootstrap** path (vs. just-in-time on first run) — it gives the cleanest "empty conversation ready on first contact" the milestone describes.

## Verification

- `pnpm db:gen` → `database.types.ts` unchanged (drift gate green); `squawk` migration lint clean.
- Biome `ci`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm -r build`, full `pnpm test` all green.
- The integration test is gated on `TEST_DATABASE_URL` so the default no-DB CI vitest run **skips** it; I ran it locally against an ephemeral Postgres with the auth stub + all migrations applied (the same shape `gen-types.sh` builds) — **2/2 passing**, including teardown.
- Migration applies cleanly on top of `archer_core` + `archer_interaction`; it will apply to Supabase on merge via the release rail.

author: rejifald
body:
## What

`packages/react-native/src/polyfills.ts` (`assertStreamingPolyfills` / `hasStreamingPolyfills`) had **no** test coverage. It's the guard that turns a cryptic "ReadableStream is not defined" deep in the stream decoder into one actionable install message on bare Hermes.

## How

New `packages/react-native/test/polyfills.spec.ts`. Both functions take an injectable `scope`, so the tests use fake scopes (plus the default `globalThis` path) — no monkeypatching:

- **`hasStreamingPolyfills`**: `true` when `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`/`ReadableStream` are all present, `false` when one is absent, and a global explicitly set to `undefined` counts as missing.
- **`assertStreamingPolyfills`**: does not throw when present; otherwise throws naming the missing globals (in `REQUIRED` order) and the `react-native-polyfill-globals/auto` install hint.
- The **default scope** is `globalThis`, which Node provides — so the no-arg calls report present / do not throw.

`adapter.ts`, `lifecycle.ts`, and `store.ts` already have dedicated specs; `index.ts` is re-exports and `native-modules.d.ts` is a declaration, so this closes the package's last gap.

body:
## Add Requesty as an OpenAI-compatible LLM provider

Adds `requesty` as a selectable `LLM_PROVIDER`, mirroring the existing OpenRouter wiring. Requesty (`https://router.requesty.ai/v1`) is an OpenRouter-shaped aggregator: it speaks the OpenAI wire protocol, uses the same `provider/model` slug naming (e.g. `openai/gpt-4o-mini`), and accepts the same optional `HTTP-Referer` / `X-Title` attribution headers. Because of that, this reuses the single `AsyncOpenAI` code path — no new client, no new behavior surface.

author: jmhodges
body:
## Summary
Refactored the Accept header parsing logic in redirect handling to use proper MIME type parsing and respect quality values (q-parameters) per RFC 7231. This prevents false positives from substring matching and correctly handles cases where JSON is explicitly marked as unacceptable.

## Key Changes
- Extracted Accept header parsing into a new `acceptsJSON()` helper function that uses the standard library's `mime.ParseMediaType()` for robust MIME type parsing
- Now properly respects quality values (q-parameters) in Accept headers, treating `q=0` as explicitly unacceptable
- Simplified the redirect handler by delegating MIME type validation to the helper function
- Updated test expectations to reflect that `Vary: Accept` should always be set when the response varies based on Accept headers, regardless of whether the header was present in the request
- Added test cases for:
  - JSON with `q=0` quality value (should fall through to HTML)
  - Non-ASCII characters in query parameters (should be percent-encoded in Location header)
- Added validation in tests to ensure Location header values contain only ASCII bytes

## Implementation Details
- Uses `mime.ParseMediaType()` to properly parse MIME types and parameters, avoiding false positives from substring matching (e.g., distinguishing `application/json` from `application/json-patch+json`)
- Correctly handles multiple Accept headers by iterating through all header values
- Respects RFC 7231 quality values, skipping MIME types with `q=0`
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing redirect behavior for HTML responses

author: shkhdev
body:
## What

Three targeted correctness/security fixes surfaced by a provider audit, plus the test
and CI infrastructure to keep them from regressing. **No HTTP API or published Terraform
schema changes** — every change here is internal behavior, lint, CI, or tests.

## Fixes

### 1. `client`: stop leaking raw response bodies into diagnostics (security)
`parseResponse` put the full raw HTTP body into `APIError.Message` whenever the body was
not the standard `{success,errors[]}` envelope. That message is rendered in every
Terraform diagnostic and CI log, so a malformed/5xx body on a credential-bearing endpoint
(kube_config, VM password) could print secrets verbatim — defeating the schema's
`Sensitive` markings. The fallback now emits a body-free `HTTP <status>` message; the full
body is kept in `RawBody` (never rendered) for programmatic inspection. The same redaction
is applied to the unparsed-success path, and a success envelope that omits `data` is now
handled gracefully instead of failing with `unexpected end of JSON input`.

### 2. `volume_attachment`: read the attachment by its real id space
`attached_volume_id` is a **VmDisk** id (and `Delete` correctly uses it as one), but `Read`
looked it up with `GetVolume`, which keys on **volume/UserDisk** ids — a different id
space. So `Read` queried the wrong object, 404'd, and silently dropped the attachment from
state, which the next apply would re-create (risking a double-attach). `Read` now resolves
the attachment through the VM's disk list (`GetVmVolumes`) and matches the VmDisk id, and
only removes the resource from state on a genuine not-found (transient errors surface as
an error instead of a silent state drop).

### 3. `kubernetes_cluster`: don't replace a cluster on a transient refresh blip
`fetchPool` returned `nil` both when the default node pool was confirmed gone and when a
transient API error left it undetermined. `Read` treated either as "pool deleted" and
nulled the block, which `ModifyPlan` turns into a **full cluster replacement** — so a
momentary error during `plan`/`refresh` could propose destroying a live cluster.
`fetchPool` now reports whether the absence is confirmed; `Read` only nulls the pool (and
plans a replace) on a confirmed absence, and otherwise keeps the last-known values with a
warning.

## Lint + CI

- Fixed the existing lint/format debt so the configured linters pass cleanly: gofmt drift,
  one unchecked type assertion in production code, `predeclared` `min` shadows, a
  `staticcheck S1016`, an `unparam`, and a `godot` nit.
- Added `.github/workflows/test.yml` (build, vet, gofmt, `golangci-lint`, unit tests) on
  pull requests and the default branch. There was previously no CI other than release, so
  the configured linters and tests were never gated.

## Tests

- Unit regression tests for fixes 1 and 3 (`parse_response_test.go`,
  `kubernetes_fetch_pool_test.go`); fix 2 is covered by the new acceptance test.
- Acceptance tests + sweepers for the seven resources that had none:
  `local_network`, `public_ip`, `volume`, `volume_attachment`, `public_ip_attachment`,
  `kubernetes_cluster`, `kubernetes_node_pool`. Each carries the `tfacc-` disposable name
  prefix and is gated by the existing production-mutation guard; the Kubernetes tests carry
  an extra opt-in because they provision a full cluster. Also fixed invalid `timeouts {…}`
  block syntax (must be `timeouts = {…}`) in the pre-existing VM acceptance config.

### Verification

- `go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...`, `gofmt -l`, and `golangci-lint run` are all clean.
- Unit regression tests for fixes 1 and 3 pass.
- Acceptance tests run live against a real ProData stand (own account, disposable
  `tfacc-` resources, all cleaned up — no leftovers). **5/7 pass:**
  `local_network`, `public_ip`, `volume`, **`volume_attachment` (the fix-2 regression
  witness)**, and `public_ip_attachment`. The two Kubernetes tests are written and gated
  but could not be validated live: cluster creation returns a backend `HTTP 500` on the
  stand (server-side, unrelated to this change). Fix 3 is covered by the unit test.

### Notes for maintainers (separate findings, not addressed here)

Surfaced while validating; left as follow-ups so this PR stays scoped:

1. **`GET /volumes/{id}` returns soft-deleted volumes.** After deletion the by-id endpoint
   still returns the volume (`success:true`) while the list endpoint drops it. The
   `volume` resource's `Read` uses the by-id endpoint, so an out-of-band volume deletion
   may not be detected as drift. (`local_network`/`public_ip` by-id correctly report
   not-found, so this is volume-specific.) The acceptance `CheckDestroy` here uses the
   authoritative list endpoint.
2. **`prodata_vm` RAM read-back can transiently differ from the configured value**, showing
   up as a one-off `ram = N-1 -> N` plan right after create (the backend was otherwise
   stable at the configured value across a 90s poll). The VM-backed acceptance tests
   therefore assert plan stability on the attachment resource specifically rather than the
   whole config.
3. **Kubernetes cluster creation returns a generic `HTTP 500`** on the validated stand.

body:
## Résumé

Ajoute `scripts/setup-worktree.sh` pour créer en une commande un environnement de session/agent isolé, afin d'éliminer les collisions quand plusieurs agents travaillent en parallèle sur le même poste.

```bash
./scripts/setup-worktree.sh avatar feature/epic-30-story-27-avatar-upload
```

## Ce que le script automatise

1. **git worktree** `../archilan-<name>` → working tree isolé (plus de checkout/stash partagés).
2. **Résolution de branche** : locale existante → checkout ; `origin/<branch>` → branche de suivi ; sinon nouvelle branche depuis `--base` (défaut `develop`).
3. **Base de test isolée** via le hook existant `dbname_suffix: '_test%env(default::TEST_TOKEN)%'` (api/config/packages/doctrine.yaml) → écrit `api/.env.test.local` avec `TEST_TOKEN=_<name>` → `archilan_test_<name>`.
4. **Dépendances** : `composer install` + `pnpm install` (per-worktree).
5. **Création de la base** de test.

## Options & garde-fous

- `--base <branch>` (hotfix depuis `main`), `--no-frontend`, `--help`.
- Refuse si le dossier existe, base introuvable, ou hors dépôt git ; ne touche pas un `.env.test.local` existant.

## Note

Aucune infra dupliquée : Postgres, Docker, MinIO et serveurs dev restent partagés ; seule la base de test est isolée. Script développé et commité… via un worktree jetable, sans perturber les sessions en cours.

body:
## What & why

Contact-form enquiries were email-only — a push notification, not a record you can work. Each submission is now **also** appended to a Notion database that doubles as a lightweight CRM (Status pipeline: `New → Contacted → Quoted → Booked / Lost`), so leads become something you manage and convert.

The Notion write is **additive and best-effort** — it changes nothing about the existing behaviour:
- Runs in `pages/api/contact.ts` **only after the notification email succeeds**, inside a `try/catch`.
- A missing or failing Notion config is logged but **never fails the request** (`{ success: true }` still returned).
- Email notification, enquirer acknowledgement, honeypot, validation, and the Meta Pixel `Lead` event are untouched.

## Changes

- **`lib/notion.ts`** (new) — `recordEnquiryInNotion()` maps form fields → Notion page properties. No-ops with a warning when env vars are absent (local dev without Notion still works); chunks long text into ≤2000-char `rich_text` segments (Notion's per-chunk cap). Submission time comes from the database's auto `Created Date` property — no timestamp is written.
- **`pages/api/contact.ts`** — best-effort call to the helper after the notification email send.
- **`package.json` / `yarn.lock`** — add `@notionhq/client@2.3.0` (3.x requires Node 22; project is on Node 20).
- **`docs/notion-integration.md`** (new) — integration/database/sharing setup, property schema, and env vars.

## Database property mapping

| Notion property | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Title | `name` |
| Email | Email | `email` |
| Phone | Phone | `countryCode` + `phone` |
| Type | Select | `type` (optional) |
| Subject | Text | `subject` (optional) |
| Source | Select | `source` (optional) |
| Message | Text | `message` |
| Status | Select | always `New` on insert |
| Created Date | created_time | auto (Notion) |

## Env vars (already set locally; **must be added to Vercel** Production + Preview)

```
NOTION_ACCESS_TOKEN=<integration secret>
NOTION_DATABASE_ID=<32-char database id>
```

The Notion integration must also be connected to the database (`••• → Connections`).

## Verification

Ran the full path against the live database via a throwaway script (since removed): a row was created with every field populated, `Status = New`, `Created Date` auto-set, and a 2159-char message stored intact (chunking verified). Failure isolation is covered by the `try/catch` wrapper. `tsc --noEmit` passes. The test row was archived afterwards.

author: tosinfamzy
body:
Phase 2 of Issue 1 — [plan](docs/plans/issue-1-phase2-weekly-plan.md). Makes `generateWeeklyPlan` constraint-aware so the engine never **schedules** an unsafe exercise into the actual program (the MVP only stopped it *suggesting* unsafe substitutes).

## How
**Service resolves, engine applies** (keeps the engine pure/library-free):
- **Engine** (`planning.ts`): `ExercisePerformance` carries a pre-resolved `constraintDecision` (`allow`/`substitute`/`omit`). Per-exercise precedence **omit > constraint-substitute > rotation-swap**; deload scaling still applies to whatever survives. `PlannedExerciseUpdate` gains `omitted`/`omissionReason`/`substitutionSource`.
- **Service** (`week-generation.ts`): loads the athlete's constraints + permanent subs, batch-fetches exercise metadata + a candidate pool, runs `isExerciseAllowed` per exercise, and resolves via `getTopSubstitutes` — which already does permanent-sub-first + the constraint safety-valve. Omitted exercises are **dropped from the scheduled workout** (not silently shortened — surfaced in `changes[]` + structured logs). **Fast path:** unconstrained users skip all library work → byte-identical to before.
- **Shared lib** `apps/server/src/lib/athlete-profile.ts` — extracted the loaders + `mapToExercise` from `exercises.ts` (DRY; userId + clerkId variants), refactored the route to use it (~100 lines deduped).
- **Bonus fix:** populating constraint-filtered `availableSubstitutes` revives rotation, which had been dead (always `[]`).

## Scope decisions
- **No new `DecisionType`** — constraint enforcement is a safety guarantee, not a coaching judgment; surfaced via `changes[]` + logs, avoiding the DecisionType/UI ripple.
- **Deferred:** weight-carry read-through (`weightCarries` still unused), grip (`no_wrist_extension` still needs the grip attribute).

## Tests / verification (independently re-run)
Engine **158**; Server **163** including a **live** `week-generation` integration test (seeds real data, calls `generateNextWeek`, asserts the generated workout's `plannedExercises` — substitute appears / omit drops one / unconstrained identical — does NOT self-skip). Typecheck + lint + db clean.

## Friendly times in the backup list
The list showed a raw timestamp (`6/20/2026 2:32:05 PM`); it now shows **"just now" / "5 min ago" / "yesterday" / "3 days ago"**, with an absolute date for older backups. Sorting by date is **unchanged** because the list sorts by the `FileInfo` stored in each row's `Tag`, not the displayed text, so `FriendlyTime` is purely cosmetic.

## Backup-location heads-up
When you pick a backup folder that's **in a cloud-synced folder** (OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive) or **on the same drive as your saves**, Savedrake now shows a one-time, **non-blocking** note about the trade-off (cloud sync can conflict during a backup; same-drive means one disk failure loses both). It never blocks, and inside-the-save-folder was already prevented at Browse time.

## Tests
`FriendlyTime` and `BackupLocationWarning` are pure static helpers, **13 new `RestoreHarness` assertions** (relative-time buckets incl. singular/plural and the absolute fallback; cloud / same-drive / inside-save / clean cases). Harness **183 -> 196**, Release green, app smoke-launched OK.

## Remaining QoL
Name/note backups and the autobackup-active indicator are left for the UI rebuild (they want proper UI surfaces); accessibility is best done during that rebuild too.

author: deibisgm
body:
## 📌 Summary

Optimizes rotating task scheduling and foreign key validation in `TaskService.cs`. This branch replaces the current pattern of performing one `HasActivePendingForDateAsync` query per date and one `PersistRotationSelectionAsync` call per assignment with a single in-memory load of all pending dates and a single persistence operation for the latest `RotationPlacement` per scheduling run.

Additionally, `ValidateForeignKeysAsync` is parallelized using `Task.WhenAll` to reduce task creation latency when categories or zones are provided.

## 🧩 Changes Made

- Replaced the per-date `HasActivePendingForDateAsync` lookup with a single `LoadPendingAssignmentDatesAsync` call that returns a `HashSet<DateOnly>`, loaded once at the beginning of each scheduling run. This affects all three scheduling methods: daily, weekly, and custom frequency.

- For tasks with `Rotating = true`, the code no longer calls `PersistRotationSelectionAsync` after every placement. It now tracks the `lastPlacement` and persists it **only once** at the end of the method.

- Fixed the rotating-task exit logic in the weekly and custom-frequency methods. The corresponding loop now uses `break`, and `occurrences.Count > 0` is checked so that skipping a date correctly respects the rotating behavior.

- Added a private helper, `LoadPendingAssignmentDatesAsync(taskId, start, end, ct)`, which queries `TaskAssignments` with a status of `pending` or `in_progress`, where `DueAt.HasValue` is true and the due date falls within the specified range, then projects the results into a `HashSet<DateOnly>`.

- Rewrote `ValidateForeignKeysAsync` to run the `AppUsers`, `Spaces`, `TaskCategories`, and `Zones` checks in parallel using `Task.WhenAll`. It also reuses the previously loaded `space` instead of querying it again to validate whether the `AssignedUserId` belongs to the space.

- Removed the duplicate `Spaces` query. Previously, the space was queried once to validate its existence and again to verify the assigned user's membership.

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria Covered

- Rotating tasks no longer generate N `TaskAssignments` writes per scheduling run. The process is reduced to a single write for the latest placement.

- Duplicate-date detection now uses an in-memory set instead of performing a database round trip for every date.

- Foreign key validation in `CreateTask` is no longer sequential. User, space, category, and zone checks now run in parallel.

- `AssignedUserId` is still correctly validated against the members of the space without performing a duplicate `Spaces` query.

- Observable behavior—such as which dates are created, which members are selected, and how many assignments are generated—remains unchanged. Only the execution cost is reduced.

## 📁 Files Changed

- `Services/TaskService.cs`

## 🧪 Testing

- Pending verification: Create a daily rotating task with N dates and confirm that only **one** `TaskAssignment` is persisted with the corresponding `RotationRound`, rather than N assignments.

- Pending verification: Run the scheduling process again for the same task and confirm that dates already containing `pending` or `in_progress` assignments are skipped without creating duplicates.

- Pending verification: In `ValidateForeignKeysAsync`, provide a `CreateTaskRequest` with valid `CategoryId` and `ZoneId` values and verify that all four checks complete successfully using EF Core logs or traces.

- Pending verification: Provide an `AssignedUserId` that is **not** a member of the specified `SpaceId` and confirm that an `InvalidOperationException` is thrown with the existing error message.

- Pending verification: Provide a nonexistent `CategoryId` and a nonexistent `ZoneId`, and confirm that the correct `KeyNotFoundException` exceptions are thrown. Parallel validation must not break the existing error contract.

## 📝 Notes

- **Low risk:** The changes are internal to `TaskService` and do not modify public method signatures, controllers, DTOs, or the database schema. External behavior—including generated dates, the member selected by the rotation logic, and thrown exceptions—remains unchanged.

- **Expected benefit:** For tasks with a large scheduling window, such as 365 daily rotating occurrences, the process is reduced from 365 queries and 365 writes to one query and one write per scheduling run. In `CreateTask`, when all foreign keys are present, validation latency is reduced to `max(user, space, category, zone)` instead of the sum of all four checks.

- **Dependencies:** None. No new packages or database migrations were introduced.

- **Suggested follow-up:** Consider moving `LoadPendingAssignmentDatesAsync` into a repository such as `ITaskAssignmentRepository` to keep `TaskService` focused on scheduling logic.

author: furukama
body:
## What

Adds **Hetzner Agent** (`src/hetzner-agent/`) — a connector agent that operates Hetzner Cloud servers, DNS zones, and Storage Boxes from chat, bundling the `hetzner-cloud`, `hetzner-dns`, and `hetzner-storage-box` skills. Built to `dist/hetzner-agent.claw` via `build.sh`, so it's installable as `official:hetzner-agent`.

This is the reference connector agent behind the "agent directory → land in a specialized, pre-skilled agent" flow.

## Highlights

- **`manifest.json`** — full `presentation` block (`role`, `cardDescription`, `skillTags`, `registerContext`, `statusLabel`) for the directory card; `skills.bundled` lists the three Hetzner skills, vendored under `workspace/skills/`.
- **`BOOTSTRAP.md`** — first-run greeting with example prompts drawn from the skill docs, plus the one-time `HETZNER_API_TOKEN` setup, then asks for default project + autonomy. This is what actually fires on a fresh agent's first session.
- **`OPENING.md`** — returning-session greeting with example prompts.
- Standard workspace (`IDENTITY`/`SOUL`/`AGENTS`/`BOOT`/`MEMORY`/`TOOLS`/`USER`/`HEARTBEAT`, `.hybridclaw/policy.yaml`) + the Hetzner logo.

Reads by default and confirms every change with its cost; tokens are gateway-injected and never handled in plaintext.

## Why both BOOTSTRAP and OPENING

On a brand-new agent the runtime injects `BOOTSTRAP.md` and `resolveStartupBootstrapFile()` returns it on the first session — so `BOOTSTRAP.md` carries the first greeting, and `OPENING.md` handles returning sessions. Both contain the example-prompt greeting + token guidance.

## Validation

CLI isn't built locally, so validated structurally (15/15): `formatVersion`, safe relative `imageAsset` (+ present), `skills.bundled` matches the archive `skills/` dirs, every `SKILL.md` present, OPENING differs from template, tutorials bundled, no symlink/`..`/absolute entries. To confirm end-to-end:

```bash
./build.sh
hybridclaw agent inspect dist/hetzner-agent.claw
hybridclaw agent install dist/hetzner-agent.claw --id hetzner-agent --activate
```

## Reviewer notes

- **Skills are vendored** from the hybridclaw repo's `skills/` (kept in sync manually for now). Open to importing via `clawhub/…` instead if these get published there, matching the other agents.
- **Not added to `production-claws.json` `homepage_personas`** — it's a tool/connector agent rather than a homepage persona. Happy to surface it differently if the directory wants it.

author: itsfederico
body:
## Summary

In `async_catchup_multi_thread`, the spawned reader task drained stellar-core's stdout pipe into an unbounded channel at full speed. Stellar-core would finish writing all ledger metas and exit before ingestion processed them. Downstream retroshade state queries (HTTP to stellar-core) then hit a dead process and failed silently.

## Change

Switch the catchup channel from `unbounded_channel()` to `channel(16)`:
- `core_runner.rs`: stagger > 1 and no-stagger branches use `channel(16)` directly, passing the bounded sender as the 6th arg to `BufferedLedgerMetaReader::new`. Return type is now `Receiver<Box<MetaResult>>`. Stagger <= 1 branch wraps `start_and_transmitter_async`'s unbounded receiver via a forwarding task (that function is shared with the live `run_async` path and must stay untouched).
- `buffered_ledger_meta_reader.rs`: `async_multi_thread_read_ledger_meta_from_pipe` gains a bounded send path using `try_send` + 1ms spin-sleep (avoids a Send-constraint violation from `.await` inside the non-Send XDR iterator loop). When the channel is full the reader spins, the OS pipe fills, and stellar-core's `write()` blocks, keeping it alive.
- `captive_core.rs`: `async_prepare_ledgers` return type updated to match.

Effect: bounds stellar-core's lead over ingestion to ~16 ledgers (~80s), well within Reflector's 5-minute update cadence. Live ingestion path (`run_async`, `start_online_no_range`, `start_and_transmitter_async`) is unchanged.

## Dependencies

Pairs with mercury PR #59 (MER-061). Merge both together.

author: francomarb
body:
## Summary

Ships [`docs/order_lifecycle_state_machine.md`](docs/order_lifecycle_state_machine.md) §10.4 — the last structural duplication carried over from the order-lifecycle foundation (PR #60 / PR #61). `option_trailing_stops` no longer mixes legitimate strategy state with a duplicate mirror of broker-order state; the trailing row now points at the substrate row that owns broker identity / status via a new `lifecycle_order_id` FK.

Closes the deferred lifecycle-state split that PR #69 left as the durable fix.

## Migration shape

- New column: `option_trailing_stops.lifecycle_order_id INTEGER REFERENCES position_lifecycle_orders(id)`.
- **FK targets the autoincrement PK, not `order_id`.** `position_lifecycle_orders.order_id` has a *partial* unique index (`UNIQUE WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL`). SQLite refuses to treat a partial-unique column as an FK parent key, so the autoincrement `id` is the only valid target — surfaced in the discovery doc as review-6 finding #2.
- Fresh installations get the FK enforced inline; pre-existing tables get a plain `ALTER ADD COLUMN INTEGER` (SQLite cannot add a column with a FOREIGN KEY clause via `ALTER`). Application code maintains integrity on legacy tables; a future rebuild promotes the constraint.

## What stays as a denormalized mirror

`alpaca_stop_order_id` / `stop_order_status` columns on `option_trailing_stops` are retained during migration so legacy rows (whose FK is still NULL) keep working and so the safety net survives if the substrate insert fails. The follow-up cleanup PR removes them once every reader migrates to the FK join.

## Substrate wiring that landed inline

`§10.4` as written assumed the foundation already owned option stop rows on `position_lifecycle_orders`. It didn't — the existing P-4 / P-5 substrate writes only covered equity stops. So this PR also wires:

- `submit_option_gtc_stop` → inserts a `role='protective_stop'` row.
- `replace_option_stop` → inserts a `role='replacement_stop'` row with `replaces_order_id` carrying the superseded order id, mirroring the equity P-5 lineage pattern.

Both follow the foundation's POST-submit discipline: substrate failure logs CRITICAL and is absorbed so the broker order is never orphaned. Callers without `position_uid` (broker smoke paths, legacy tests) skip the substrate write.

## Commit-by-commit

1. Schema migration (`option_trailing.py`, `reporting/logger.py`).
2. Substrate wiring for `submit_option_gtc_stop` / `replace_option_stop` + engine call sites pass `position_uid` through.
3. `OptionTrailingStopStore.upsert` + `OptionTrailingStopRow` extended with `lifecycle_order_id`.
4. Every `option_trailing_store.upsert` site in `_sync_option_trailing_stops` populates the FK from the just-written substrate row.
5. Read-path migration: `_recent_option_stop_submit_pending` reads substrate-authoritative status via `_option_trailing_authoritative_identity`, falling back to the mirror columns when FK is NULL. New `JoinedOptionTrailingRow` + `get_by_occ_joined` API.
6. `_cleanup_option_trailing_state` docstring shifts to "drop strategy trailing state" only — substrate row terminal status is owned by `apply_order_event`.
7. Tests + tracker + PLAN: ~20 new tests across store / broker / engine layers; PR #46 trailing tests and PR #69 cleanup tests stay green.

## Out of scope (explicit follow-ups)

- Strict removal of `alpaca_stop_order_id` / `stop_order_status` columns.
- Phase 2 consumer migration (dashboard, health monitor) — per `docs/operator_controls_proposal.md` §17.2.
- The 2026-06-16 underlying-vs-OCC symbol-key collision was a `_detect_external_closes` issue, not directly a trailing-mirror issue. This split makes PR #69's cleanup helper vestigial-but-still-correct; it does not on its own eliminate that collision class.

## Risk

- Stop replacement sequence: substrate insert succeeds → trailing FK updates to the new id → old substrate row terminates async through `apply_order_event`. If the substrate insert fails, the trailing row keeps the old FK and the mirror columns remain authoritative for that cycle (cycle reconciliation catches up next pass).
- PR #64 SPY option stop replacement audit (`OPTION_STOP_REPLACE_AUDIT_ENABLED=true`) reads its own DB (`data/diagnostics/option_stop_replace_audit.db`) and does not touch `option_trailing_stops`. Audit hooks unaffected.
- `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is set on every connection ([reporting/logger.py:430](reporting/logger.py:430)).

## Test plan

- [x] `/Users/franco/trading-bot/venv/bin/pytest tests/test_option_trailing.py tests/test_broker.py tests/test_engine.py tests/test_lifecycle_review_fixes.py tests/test_lifecycle_orders_schema.py tests/test_apply_order_event.py` → 449 passed.
- [x] Full suite: `/Users/franco/trading-bot/venv/bin/pytest` → 2756 passed.
- [ ] Paper bake on `feat/option-trailing-state-split` for ≥1 SPY option ratchet cycle: confirm new substrate rows are written under `role='protective_stop'` / `role='replacement_stop'` for `spy_options_reversion` and the trailing row's `lifecycle_order_id` matches.
- [ ] PR #64 audit DB continues to capture every ratchet on the recycled paper bot.

author: jeremi
body:
## Summary

Addresses findings from the post-validation security review (v0.3.0). All are Low/Info severity against an already-STRONG posture; these changes close them out as defense-in-depth and make implicit invariants explicit.

> **RN-01 was dropped from this PR.** The OpenFn source-adapter execution engine is being retired separately (branch `claude/sleepy-noether-qk2y0z`). RN-01 documented network-layer egress controls for the unguarded **Node.js OpenFn engine path** — once OpenFn is removed, that path no longer exists and only the Rust `http_json`/`http_flow`/`fhir` paths remain (which already enforce in-process SSRF defenses). The egress-hardening doc and its cross-links were therefore removed here rather than shipping guidance for a code path that is going away.

| Finding | Severity | Status | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~~RN-01 — OpenFn engine egress~~ | ~~Low~~ | ⛔ dropped | Obsoleted by OpenFn removal (separate PR) |
| RN-02 — Notary tokens without `jti` get no replay protection | Info | ✅ landed | Fail closed for single-use token typs |
| RN-03 — OID4VCI URL building trusts `X-Forwarded-*` | Info | ✅ landed | Gate forwarded headers behind trusted-proxy allow-list |
| RN-04 — admin `reference` into `FileLocalApprovalStore` | Info | ✅ landed | Boundary validation rejecting path-traversal references |
| RN-05 — sidecar `/metrics` unauthenticated | Info | ✅ landed | Opt-in bearer auth (`metrics_require_auth`, default off) |

## RN-02 — fail-closed replay protection (server)
- `consume_notary_token_jti` now fails closed (`MissingCredential`) when a single-use **transaction-typ** token is missing its `jti`, instead of silently returning `Ok(())`. Non-single-use typs legitimately have no `jti` and are still accepted.
- New unit test covering both the fail-closed and accepted paths.

## RN-03 — trusted-proxy gate for forwarded host/proto (server)
- The OID4VCI type-metadata endpoints honor `X-Forwarded-Host` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` only when the socket peer is in the configured `trusted_proxy_ips`, mirroring the existing `token_client_address` gate. Untrusted peers fall back to the `Host` header / request URI / configured issuer.
- New `forwarded_host_trusted` helper; explicit `trust_forwarded` flag threaded through. Unit tests for trusted/untrusted peers; integration tests serve via `into_make_service_with_connect_info` so the loopback peer is visible to the gate.

## RN-04 — approval-reference boundary validation (server)
- New `is_valid_approval_reference` rejects empty/whitespace, any `..` path-traversal marker, and anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` before the value reaches the platform `FileLocalApprovalStore`. Applied in `stored_break_glass_approval` and `load_local_approval`.

## RN-05 — `/metrics` auth (sidecar)
- New `ServerConfig.metrics_require_auth: bool` (`#[serde(default)]` → `false`, backward-compatible). When enabled, `/metrics` requires the same bearer token as other protected endpoints, reusing the existing `authorize` path.
- Unit tests + example config documentation.

## Coordination with the OpenFn-removal PR (`claude/sleepy-noether-qk2y0z`)
If this PR merges first, the removal branch will need to absorb two cleanups when it rebases:
1. **RN-05 carry-forward** — the removal rewrites the `metrics` handler (`State`-only signature) and `ServerConfig`. The `metrics_require_auth` gate must be re-applied on top of the rewritten handler so `/metrics` auth survives the removal.
2. **RN-05 example** — the `metrics_require_auth` example comment currently lives in `examples/openfn-sidecar.yaml`, which the removal deletes. It should be re-added to the replacement examples (`civil-http-json-sidecar.yaml` / `dhis2-health-sidecar.yaml`).

## Notes
- The workspace's sibling path-dependencies (`../registry-platform`, `../crosswalk`) are not present in the authoring environment, so changes were verified by inspection rather than `cargo build`/`test`. CI's `rust` job is the compile/test gate.

body:
## Summary

This updates PR #17 from a scoped fallback cutover to a Rust-default CLI cutover with the legacy Python CLI retained only as an explicit compatibility escape hatch.

- `ai-hist` auto mode now routes the user-facing command surface to Rust: `sync`, `search`, `recent`, `show`, `session --full`, `context`, `stats`, `pack`, `resume --json`, `watch`, `export`, `import`, `tag`, `untag`, `tags`, and `sync-opencode`.
- `AI_HIST_CLI=python` and `ai-hist-python` remain available for legacy compatibility, but normal commands no longer route to Python fallback in auto mode.
- `install.sh` provides the primary one-command install path and installs deterministic `ai-hist`, `ai-hist-rust`, and `ai-hist-python` launchers so users do not manually run Cargo commands.

author: ksaddamfse-ai
body:
Implements PageIndex RAG — a vectorless alternative to Vector RAG.

**How it works:**
- LLM ingests PDFs by building a hierarchical tree with pre-computed summaries
- On query, LLM navigates the tree using summaries (no brute-force text scan)
- Only fetches raw text from relevant leaf nodes for answer generation
- Stores trees + node texts in SQLite (no vector DB required)

**Endpoints:**
- \POST /api/pageindex/documents\ — upload PDF, LLM builds tree
- \POST /api/pageindex/query\ — ask questions, LLM navigates tree

**Tested** end-to-end with a resume PDF. Tree correctly identified 4 sections + 3 child nodes under Experience. Queries returned accurate citations.

author: weiliangchenoist
body:
## What

Adds a geometric **`sphere CX CY CZ INNER OUTER SIZE`** directive to `--size-field-file`, alongside the existing `patch` and `component` settings.

It defines a spherical **refinement shell**: cells/facets whose location falls between `INNER` and `OUTER` radius of `(CX,CY,CZ)` are sized down to `SIZE` (the minimum of the local and per-label global field wins). `INNER = 0` gives a solid ball.

## Why

`patch` and `component` both key off component identity, so refining the thin cytosol gap between two close compartments meant refining a whole boundary patch/component **globally** — a large element-count increase for a local need. A sphere is purely geometric: many small shells placed along a contact resolve the gap (so close compartments stay nested instead of collapsing into contact) **without refining whole bodies**.

This is what the [STEPSMeshPipeline](https://github.com/CNS-OIST/STEPSMeshPipeline) adaptive size field emits. On a packed bouton+mitochondria scene it took the mesh from a whole-body-refinement approach (~1.65M tets) down to ~200k tets while keeping all inner compartments nested with a gap.

## How

- `struct Refine_sphere` + `Spatial_sizing_field` functor (models `MeshDomainField_3`) overlays the spheres on the existing constant per-label `Sizing_field`s.
- Facet distance inside a shell is scaled to ¼ of `SIZE` so refined facets hug the surface tightly enough to keep the gap open.
- Parsing added to the `--size-field-file` reader; unknown-line error message and README/`example/sizefields.txt` updated to document it.

## Test

Builds cleanly (CGAL). Verified end-to-end via STEPSMeshPipeline: the mesher parses the `sphere` lines ("Local refinement shell at …") and the resulting mesh passes the STEPS size-window, shape, containment (31/31 nested), and operator-splitting ζ criteria.

author: samarthanalytics-sj
body:
## Desktop "Tag suggestions" panel — review & one-click create

A new left-nav panel in the desktop app that closes the loop on the "measurement plan from a URL" feature: **scan a site → review the GA4 tags worth creating → approve → create as GTM drafts.**

```
type a URL → main-process crawl (hidden Electron BrowserWindow) → ranked suggestions
           → review / select / edit → Approve & create → create_gtm_tracking_tag (draft)
```

### Why this approach (you said "suggest me")
Electron **is** Chromium, so the desktop crawls with a hidden `BrowserWindow` — **no Playwright dependency, no second server to run**, fully self-contained. It reuses the *exact same* pure, tested suggestion engine from `apps/web-audit-mcp` (`buildSuggestInput`/`buildSuggestions`/`classifyPageElements`/`analyzeForms`), imported cross-package. Those modules are **leaf-pure** (their Playwright page type is a `type`-only import, erased), so nothing browser/Playwright lands in the desktop bundle. A **"paste a `gtm_tag_suggestions` report"** path is also included.

### The panel
- One row per suggestion: confidence badge, `GA4 event` chip, page · event · trigger, evidence.
- **EM-overlap warning** — suggestions GA4 Enhanced Measurement already auto-tracks (downloads/outbound) are flagged and **unticked by default**.
- Per-row edit (tag name / event name / measurement ID), bulk select (all / none / new-only).
- Target = the active `gtmContext` (account/container/workspace); create disabled until a draft workspace is chosen, with a `{{GA4 Measurement ID}}` caveat.
- Sequential create with per-row ✓/✗ status, success banner, and retry (failures stay selected).

### Guardrails (verified)
- **Read-only** scan + paste; **create** goes through the single existing `create_gtm_tracking_tag` path — **draft-only, never publishes**. Write tools still only exist when a confirm fn is supplied; the renderer performs an **explicit batch approval** before the create IPC runs.
- **SSRF**: the start URL is admitted, and every in-browser request (incl. redirects/subresources) is blocked when the host **or its resolved IP** is private/loopback/metadata.
- Hidden window hardened: `sandbox`, `contextIsolation`, `nodeIntegration:false`, no preload, `webSecurity`, popups denied, ephemeral session destroyed after each scan.

### Review
4-lens adversarial review (Electron/SSRF security, guardrails, correctness, renderer/contract) → adversarial verify. Core checks all PASS. Confirmed findings fixed: **DNS-rebind SSRF** (resolve + block private IPs in `onBeforeRequest`), `executeJavaScript` timeout, `editRow` `flexWrap`, and a confirm-dialog `{{GA4 Measurement ID}}` reminder.

### Tests
- `suggestion-service.test.ts` — **29** pure checks (crawl BFS via a fake driver, classification, EM flags, notScanned labeling, the 4 paste shapes, the create loop).
- smoke `+3` create-path checks (incl. "without a confirm fn the write is refused" and "35 read tools intact").
- `desktop:check` (node + web) clean; `desktop:test` + smoke **12/12**.

Independent of [Phase 3 #43](https://github.com/samarthanalytics-sj/samarth-analytics-mcp/pull/43) — reuses the engine already on `main`. `apps/desktop`-only; `chore(desktop)` (no version bump).

> Note: the live Electron crawl is integration-tested manually (needs a real browser host); the pure orchestration + create loop are unit-tested via an injected driver.

author: abkrim
body:
## What

`Invoice::userTaxProfile()` and `Invoice::companyFiscalConfig()` are `belongsTo`
relations to models that use `SoftDeletes`. Without `withTrashed()`, soft-deleting
a referenced fiscal snapshot made the relation resolve to `null`, so an
already-issued (immutable) invoice "lost" its historical fiscal identity. The
visible symptom was `InvoiceVerifactuService::validateForVerifactu()` failing with
"Invoice must have a tax profile" on a perfectly valid invoice.

## Why

A fiscal `SoftDeletes` is history closure, not erasure: an immutable invoice's
snapshot must never disappear from its context. (It is also the proof that fiscal
soft-delete and GDPR erasure must never be conflated — see AID-221.)

## Change

`->withTrashed()` on both `belongsTo` relations. AID-222 named only
`userTaxProfile()`; auditing the sibling snapshot relation showed
`companyFiscalConfig()` carries the same latent bug, so both are fixed together.

## Tests (TDD)

- `InvoiceRelationshipsTest`: each snapshot relation stays accessible after the
  referenced row is soft-deleted (and reports `trashed()`).
- `InvoiceVerifactuServiceTest`: a fit invoice still validates after its tax
  profile is soft-deleted.

Full suite: **975 passed**, 1 skipped (2817 assertions). Pint + PHPStan clean.

Closes AID-222.

body:
## Summary

- Fix dashboard layout on mobile (page blank/unscrollable on iOS Safari)
- Fix SQL cartesian product in `get_budget_compliance`
- Fix budget calculations to convert expenses to the budget's currency before summing

## Changes

### Mobile layout (`h-dvh`)
`h-screen` (`100vh`) freezes the layout height at load time on iOS Safari — when the address bar appears/disappears the content area doesn't resize. Changed to `h-dvh` (`100dvh`) so the viewport adjusts dynamically.

### Modal height on mobile
Added `max-h-[90dvh] overflow-y-auto` to the dialog so tall forms (BudgetForm, MonthlyIncomeModal) scroll inside the modal instead of overflowing off-screen.

### SQL: cartesian product fix (migration 013)
`get_budget_compliance` joined budgets × expenses without a category filter, producing N×M rows. With 3 budgets and 5 expenses, each expense was counted 3 times. Rewrote using CTEs that aggregate separately, then join the aggregated totals.

### SQL: currency conversion (migration 014)
Both `get_budget_summary` and `get_budget_compliance` were summing raw expense amounts regardless of currency. Added a `convert_currency()` helper (direct rate → inverse rate → fallback 1.0, same pattern as migration 005) and call it when aggregating expenses so all amounts are compared in the budget's currency.

## Post-merge steps
Apply migrations 013 and 014 on the live Supabase instance:
- `supabase/migrations/013_fix_compliance_cartesian.sql`
- `supabase/migrations/014_fix_budget_currency_conversion.sql`

author: gaboracnicolai
body:
**T8 BUILD-NOW #1.** `dependency.Create` / `BulkCreateRelations` accepted `A blocks B` **and** `B blocks A` — and any longer chain — creating a circular dependency (deadlock). Adds **transitive** cycle detection.

## Fix
Before inserting a blocks-family edge (`blocker → blocked`), a recursive walk of the blocks graph asks whether `blocked` can **already reach** `blocker`. If so, the edge is refused with a typed `ErrCycle` → handler maps to **409 Conflict**.

- `WITH RECURSIVE` reachability (deduped → terminates even on pre-existing cycles), scoped to `type='blocks'` + `workspace_id`.
- `blocked_by` (the inverse) normalises to the same `blocker → blocked` edge, so it's caught too.
- Non-dependency relations (`relates_to`, `duplicates`, `clones`) never trigger detection.
- `BulkCreateRelations` checks each target.

## RED→GREEN (real PG)
```
GREEN: 2-node rejected · 3-node transitive (A→B→C→A) rejected · 5-node chain rejected
       · blocked_by rejected · diamond (A→B,A→C,B→D,C→D) ALLOWED · relates_to allowed
       · handler → 409
RED (detection disabled): 2-node & 3-node ACCEPTED (got nil), handler → 201,
       while the diamond STAYS GREEN — proving the diamond passes because there's no
       cycle, not because the check over-rejects.
```
The 3-node case is the one to scrutinize: the closing edge `C→A` shares no endpoint with `A→B`/`B→C`, so only a real reachability walk catches it — a direct-reverse-only check would miss it.

## Green
`tenancy-lock` unaffected (`issue_relations` keys on `source_id`/`target_id`, not a workspace-scoped ref — the guard `assertIssuesShareWorkspace` is unchanged); gosec/golang clean; no `nosemgrep`.

author: jordanlarch
body:
## Summary

Implements **#15 — reaction system (Opportunity Attacks + Ready)**, the deterministic-engine primitives for reactions on top of the M3 combat core. The full interrupt-driven window/prompt system (Counterspell, Shield, Sentinel, &c.) is a later product-track concern; this slice delivers the budget, opportunity attacks, and the Ready action.

### Reaction budget
- `EntityState.reactionAvailable` — a round-spanning budget, distinct from the per-turn `actionEconomy` (which is only present on the active turn). Granted to all combatants at encounter start, refreshed at the start of the owner's turn, and spent by reactions. One per round, enforced.

### Opportunity attacks
- New pure helper `combat/reactions.ts → provokesOpportunityAttack(threatener, from, to, reach = 5)`: leaving a threatener's reach provokes; moving within reach or toward the threatener does not.
- `move_entity` in combat emits `ReactionWindowOpened { trigger: "leave_reach", mover, eligible }`, listing combatants who threatened the mover and still have a reaction.
- `opportunity_attack { reactor, target, attackBonus, damage }` resolves an attack (reusing the existing attack pipeline) against the mover of an open window and spends the reactor's reaction.

> Note: there is no faction model yet, so eligibility is reach + reaction-availability only; the GM/LLM decides which threateners actually take the OA.

### Ready action
- `ready_action { entity, trigger, action }` spends the entity's action (on its turn) and stores the trigger + queued attack.
- `trigger_readied { entity }` resolves the queued attack for a reaction and clears the readied action.
- Readied actions lapse at the start of the owner's next turn.

### Plumbing
- New commands, events (`ReactionWindowOpened`, `ReactionTaken`, `ActionReadied`, `ReadiedActionTriggered`), and validation codes (`NO_REACTION`, `NOT_PROVOKED`, `NO_READIED_ACTION`).
- tRPC engine router accepts the three new commands.

## Test plan
- [x] `combat/reactions.test.ts` — provoke-detection units (leave / within / toward / larger reach).
- [x] `engine.reactions.test.ts` — budget grant, window open/no-open, OA resolution + reaction spend, one-per-round enforcement, next-turn refresh, Ready spend/resolve/lapse, rejections, replay determinism.
- [x] `npm run test` — 234 passing.
- [x] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` — clean.

body:
Autonomous **context-strategy** loop (cron `c66c8b81`, 20m, session-scoped, loop-creator v2). Fires 1-5 already merged to main (5-fire ff-merge). This PR carries fire 6+ on the branch.

## fire 6 — thread per-turn query relevance into the cross-block edge-placement
Fire 1's `edgePlaceByPriority` accepted a per-block `relevance?` but `commands-ask` never supplied one → the reorder was relevance-blind in production (always fixed tier). Now a pure `optionalGroundingRelevance(tierKey, perTurnScore?)` blends normalized tier with the per-turn episode recall score on one 0–1 scale, and the fallback also normalizes — so a high-recall episode block climbs toward the head/tail attention zone (bounded: never above top actionable surfaces).

- **Grounding:** arXiv:2410.05983 (reorder by retriever score at boundaries), arXiv:2504.07104 (blend, not pure-sort).
- **Floor-safe:** pure permutation, set-equality + fabrication=0; score-less turns byte-identical to fire-1; no gate/banner change.
- **Verified:** recall 340 + cli 2763 + `pnpm check` + `pnpm lint` green; mutation-first RED→GREEN; two independent Opus adaptive judges (1st caught a scale-mix — fixed — final PASS).

Prior fires (on main): cross-block edge-placement (1), stale-observation masking (2), default tool-exposure ceiling (3), query-anchored cap (4), inflection-aware tool match (5).

🤖 **Draft** — human merges. The loop ff-merges this branch to main every 5th fire; never force-pushes.
