author: tutkli
body:
## Summary

- Closes [#938](https://github.com/tutkli/forty-cdk/issues/938). Promotes virtualization to a dedicated `forty-cdk/virtualization` secondary entry point so `@tanstack/virtual-core` is isolated to its own bundle chunk — apps, and lazy routes that don't virtualize even when a sibling route does, no longer pull it into the shared `forty-cdk` chunk (~4–5 kB gzip/route).
- **Breaking**: the windowing core (`injectVirtualizer`), the declarative `[forVirtualViewport]` + `*forVirtualFor` layer, `injectInfiniteScroll`, and the `[forTableVirtualized]` companion (plus their related types / context) now ship from `forty-cdk/virtualization` instead of `forty-cdk`. Migration: change those imports' module specifier to `forty-cdk/virtualization`; no API shapes changed. Documented in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).
- The entry point mirrors the `internationalized-date` precedent: its own [ng-package.json](projects/forty-cdk/virtualization/ng-package.json) + [public-api.ts](projects/forty-cdk/virtualization/src/public-api.ts), with the moved source under [virtualization/src/](projects/forty-cdk/virtualization/src). Removed the barrel export from [public-api.ts](projects/forty-cdk/src/public-api.ts) and the `ForTableVirtualized` re-export from the [table barrel](projects/forty-cdk/src/lib/table/index.ts).
- Decoupled the two main-entry → core bridges so the main FESM no longer statically references the core. `[forTableVirtualized]` moved into the entry point; `[forTableRowReorder]` now reaches the virtualized companion through a new read-only `virtualRowNavigation` accessor on `FOR_TABLE_CONTEXT` ([table-context.ts](projects/forty-cdk/src/lib/table/table-context.ts), [table.ts](projects/forty-cdk/src/lib/table/table.ts), [table-row-reorder.ts](projects/forty-cdk/src/lib/table/table-row-reorder.ts)) instead of `inject(ForTableVirtualized)`.
- The `_internal` `afterNextRenderCancellable` helper can't be relative-imported across the entry-point boundary (ng-packagr "file belongs to two entry points"). Rather than duplicate it or widen the public surface, its small cancel-on-destroy logic is **inlined directly into `injectVirtualizer`** ([virtualizer.ts](projects/forty-cdk/virtualization/src/virtualizer.ts)), leaving that file with no cross-entry-point import at all and the public API surface unchanged.
- The `unit-test` builder roots spec discovery at the project `src`, so the relocated specs are picked up via an `include` glob in [angular.json](angular.json); the `TableVirtualizedNavigator` unit tests were extracted from `table.spec.ts` into a co-located [spec](projects/forty-cdk/virtualization/src/table-virtualized-navigator.spec.ts). Updated the SSR fixtures' imports, the harness + playground import paths, and the tsconfig path aliases (root / spec / harness / playground).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes.
- [x] `pnpm test` — 3782 passing across 140 files; the 4 relocated virtualization specs (38 cases) verified discovered and green.
- [x] `pnpm build` — library compiles via ng-packagr; verified the main FESM has **no** `@tanstack/virtual-core` import, the `forty-cdk/virtualization` FESM is its only importer, and the subpath is present in the generated `package.json` `exports`.
- [x] `pnpm exec playwright test --project=chromium` — virtualization / table-virtualized / combobox-/listbox-/select-/tree-virtualized fixtures green (45/45). One `select-virtualized` failure was a `count()`-race flake (no auto-wait); 5/5 on isolated re-run.

author: henrycgbaker
body:
## Summary

Fifth PR of the behavioral-audit cleanup campaign. Revives the dead VRAM dry-run estimate and fixes four CLI robustness gaps.

- **D4 - VRAM dry-run was dead** (`cli/_vram.py`, `pyproject.toml`): `estimate_vram` depended on `huggingface_hub`, which was imported under a blanket `except` but never declared as a dependency, so it always returned None ("unavailable"). Declares `huggingface-hub`; reuses the `domain.model_info.extract_model_arch` helper (from #725) for the architecture fields instead of re-parsing config field variants inline; makes the KV-cache term GQA/MQA-aware (`num_key_value_heads`) and batch-aware (per-engine batch field) instead of hardcoding batch=1 + full MHA; and memoizes the study dry-run loop by `(model, dtype)` so a sweep of N experiments over one model makes one HF Hub round-trip, not N.
- **C2 - report-gaps false all-clear** (`api/report_gaps.py`): a missing / typo'd `--study-dir` silently yielded "No gaps found" with exit 0. Now raises and exits nonzero with a clear message.
- **C3 - report-gaps verbosity** (`cli/report_gaps.py`): adds `--verbose/-v`, making the previously-unreachable dir-skipped log path observable.
- **C4 - silently-ignored study flags** (`cli/run.py`): single-experiment runs now warn when study-only flags (`--cycles`, `--order`, `--resume`, ...) are set.
- **C5 - doctor column overflow** (`cli/doctor_cmd.py`): widen the Engine column so "transformers" no longer breaks alignment.

## Test plan

- New / updated tests across `tests/unit/cli/{test_vram,test_cli_display,test_cli_run,test_doctor_cmd,test_report_gaps}.py` and `tests/unit/api/test_report_gaps.py`: VRAM returns a GQA-aware estimate (not None) with the right KV scaling + batch size; the study loop fetches once per unique model (memoization); report-gaps exits nonzero on a missing dir; `-v` surfaces the skip message; single-exp study-flag warning fires; doctor table aligns.
- Verified at the real surface: `llem report-gaps --study-dir /nonexistent --out ...` exits 2 with "Study directory does not exist"; `estimate_vram` on a mocked Llama-3-8B (GQA) returns weights ~16 GB + a modest GQA KV term.
- `make lint` (import-linter 4 contracts kept) + `make typecheck` (mypy clean) pass.
- Full suite: 2442 passed, 0 failed (skips dropped 52 -> 43 because huggingface_hub now lets optional-dep tests run).

## Doc audit

No doc regeneration needed. `huggingface-hub` added to runtime dependencies in pyproject.toml.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide an accessible, non‑destructive dark mode that respects the user’s system preference and persists their choice, instead of a naive color inversion. 
- Make the theme toggle available on desktop and mobile while keeping changes isolated and compatible with the existing layout and auth flow.

### Description
- Add a `ThemeProvider` and `useTheme` hook in `src/context/ThemeContext.jsx` that chooses an initial theme from `localStorage` or the system `prefers-color-scheme`, toggles the `dark` class on `document.documentElement`, and sets `color-scheme` for the browser.
- Wrap the app with `ThemeProvider` in `src/main.jsx` so the theme is available everywhere without changing existing auth/router structure.
- Add an accessible `ThemeToggle` UI to the header (desktop + compact mobile) and wire it to `useTheme` in `src/components/Header.jsx`, and update navigation classes to include dark-mode friendly color tokens.
- Enable Tailwind class dark mode by setting `darkMode: 'class'` in `tailwind.config.js` and add curated dark palette overrides in `src/styles/index.css` (base & utilities) to ensure readable contrast for backgrounds, text, borders, forms, prose, and shadows.
- Fix a Tailwind `@apply` issue by avoiding an unsupported `placeholder:` apply and using explicit placeholder color rules in the dark styles.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build`, which initially failed on a postcss `@apply` circular dependency, then succeeded after the placeholder fix and produced a production build (`dist/*`) without errors. 
- Ran `npm run lint`, which reported many existing unrelated `no-unused-vars`/JSX and config warnings across the codebase and therefore did not pass; these lint failures are pre‑existing and not introduced by the dark mode changes.

## What this PR does

This PR validates ACP `_qwen/file/read` window parameters before calling the file system, and validates `_qwen/file/read_bytes` offset and maxBytes parameters before byte reads. It adds transport coverage for valid params, omitted defaults, and invalid window values.

## Why it's needed

ACP file reads should reject malformed window values at the transport boundary instead of letting partial parses or invalid numeric values reach file-system logic. That keeps the method contract predictable for IDE and HTTP callers.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused ACP HTTP transport file-method tests. Confirm valid and omitted window params still work, while invalid `startLine`, `limit`, `offset`, or `maxBytes` values return validation errors before a file read is attempted.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: malformed ACP file-read window params could pass through to the file-system call path.

After: invalid window params are rejected at dispatch/transport validation; valid and omitted defaults continue to work.

author: matuyuhi
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced `.entry(file.to_string()).or_insert(0)` with a `.get_mut(file)` check.
🎯 **Why:** The previous implementation unconditionally created a `String` inside the loop for every single match, just to check/update the HashMap. By using `get_mut()`, we can query the map with a `&str` and only allocate when a new key needs to be inserted.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** Measured with a simple microbenchmark creating 100,000 matches. The optimization halved the processing time from 1.05s to 0.49s (approx. 2.1x speedup).

  - `vN` タグ push 時のみビルド（PR/main push の重いビルドを廃止）

配布物は未署名のため、ダウンロード版は Gatekeeper の quarantine 警告が出る（別件、恒久対応は Developer ID 署名＋notarize）。

Message: Plain text docs: add [FirstName LastName] to Group 7 team members table Commit 2 – docs/design_notes.md Scroll to the very bottom. Add after the last line: Markdown ### 10. Why the Swarm Class Exists Instead of a Plain List  A naive implementation of the tracker could store peers as a plain dictionary mapping file hashes to lists of peers. Instead, a dedicated `Swarm` class was created. This matters for two reasons. First, `Swarm` uses a Python `set` internally, which prevents duplicate peer registrations without any extra guard code — if the same peer registers twice, the set silently ignores the second insertion. Second, `Swarm` implements `__len__`, `__contains__`, and `__iter__`, making it behave like a built-in container: you can write `if peer in swarm:` or `for p in swarm:` naturally. author: rstar327
body:
## Description

Adds `keras.ops.image.euclidean_dist_transform` — for each non-background pixel of a binary image, computes the Euclidean distance to the nearest background (zero-valued) pixel. Each channel is processed independently. Closes #22038.

This is commonly needed for distance-based loss functions on segmentation masks (boundary loss, signed distance regression, weighted CE) and for distance-aware visualization.

**Signature**

```python
keras.ops.image.euclidean_dist_transform(
    images,           # 3D (H, W, C) or 4D (N, H, W, C) integer tensor
    dtype="float32",  # output float dtype
    data_format=None, # "channels_last" | "channels_first" | None -> config
)
```

**Behavior**

- Returns a tensor of the same shape as `images` with the requested float dtype.
- Per-channel: distance from each non-zero pixel to the nearest zero pixel; zero pixels have distance 0.
- Implementation reuses `scipy.ndimage.distance_transform_edt` (already a Keras dependency) through each backend's appropriate callback mechanism:
  - tensorflow: `tf.numpy_function`
  - jax: `jax.pure_callback`
  - torch / numpy: direct numpy call on device-host buffer
  - openvino: raises `NotImplementedError` (matches the `sobel_edges` precedent)

**API additions**

- `keras.ops.image.euclidean_dist_transform`

**Tests**

`EuclideanDistTransformTest` in `keras/src/ops/image_test.py` covers:

- 3D and 4D inputs, `channels_first` and `channels_last`
- Numeric agreement with the scipy reference on a randomized input
- Closed-form check on a single-background-pixel image (distance equals geometric distance to that pixel)
- Dtype handling (`float32` default, `float16` explicit)
- Input validation (rejects float input, rejects rank-2 input)
- Symbolic call shape/dtype propagation

All 9 tests pass on tensorflow, jax, torch, numpy backends locally. openvino is covered in CI (raises with a clear message and the test class skips).

author: punk6529
body:
## Issue

The responsiveness runner currently treats any `nextjs-portal` as a blocking Next.js error overlay. Modern Next dev also renders the normal Dev Tools route/bundler panel in a `nextjs-portal`, so the runner can stop before app content readiness and report an app-wide blank-screen failure even when the artifact only contains Dev Tools chrome.

This showed up while reviewing 6529seize-frontend PR #2793: the artifact text was ordinary Next Dev Tools text (`Route`, `Bundler`, `Turbopack`, `Route Info`, `Preferences`) rather than a real module/runtime error. The existing frontend reviewbot lanes are preserved; this is an additive signal-quality fix for the responsiveness lane.

## Fix

- Tightens generated responsiveness metrics so generic Next Dev Tools portal text is not automatically classified as `nextErrorOverlay`.
- Still treats true Next error text such as build/runtime errors, module-not-found, failed compile, uncaught, hydration, and `Error:` diagnostics as blocking overlays.
- Adds normalization for the exact Dev Tools strings seen in the artifact, including extracted text quirks like `Clo e`.
- Adds namespaced `REVIEWBOT_RESPONSIVENESS_*` endpoint env vars to the production and manual responsiveness workflows.
- Makes the generated Playwright web server prefer those namespaced endpoint env vars with remote-safe defaults, instead of ambient target-repo `API_ENDPOINT` / `WS_ENDPOINT` values.
- Documents the namespaced local override contract.

## Validation

- `npm run check`
- `npm test`
- `npm run check:review-workflows`
- `npm run check:worker-adapter-contract`

## Safety

- Does not remove or weaken any existing review kinds or bot entrypoints.
- Does not add provider secrets to the benchmark job.
- Keeps real Next build/runtime overlays as failures while reducing false positives from normal dev chrome.

author: jpcamara
body:
**Found by intensive browser testing of realtime_talk against a real AnyCable stack.** Document edits synced, but **presence and remote cursors didn't propagate** — because `ActionCableProvider` sent awareness over AnyCable's `whisper`, and anycable-go **silently drops whispers unless the server enables them** (`stream_from key, whisper: true`; `--streams_whisper` defaults off). Whisper-by-default = silently-lost presence on any server that hasn't opted in.

## Fix
Awareness now defaults to a normal `send` (which `YrbLite::ActionCable::Sync` relays — works on plain ActionCable *and* AnyCable). Whisper is **opt-in** via a new option:
```js
new ActionCableProvider(doc, consumer, "DocumentChannel", { id }, { awarenessWhisper: true })
```
Only turn it on once you've enabled whispering server-side. `SyncEngine` still flags awareness frames; the provider decides the route.

## Verified
- 25 `node:test` cases (default = send even when whisper is available; `awarenessWhisper:true` whispers docs-sent; fallback to send when no whisper method).
- **realtime_talk e2e over the real AnyCable stack is now fully green** — presence over AnyCable, remote caret renders, selection highlight, convergence both ways, durability.

Bumps to **0.1.3**.

author: zandor435
body:
## Problem
`pages.yml` (`on: push`) hasn't deployed since **June 12** — the last *human* push. The every-3h "Update standings" cron commits fresh data daily, but those pushes use the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and **GITHUB_TOKEN pushes don't trigger other workflows** (GitHub anti-recursion). So github.io is frozen on June-12 standings while the repo data has advanced to June 19. This is user-facing: the daily email links every CTA/image at `zandor435.github.io/wc-challenge`.

## Fix
Add a `deploy-pages` job to **update-data.yml**, gated on the existing `update` job, so the deploy runs *inside* the same workflow — no token-trigger issue.

- Checks out `ref: main` (the commit `update` just pushed), not the event SHA, so it publishes the refreshed `site/data/*.json`.
- Job-scoped `pages: write` / `id-token: write` permissions (overrides the workflow's `contents: write`).
- Same `pages` concurrency group as `pages.yml` so a manual-push deploy and a cron deploy can't race on the single `github-pages` environment.
- Rest days stay free: `needs: update`, which the gate skips on no-match days, so this job is skipped too.

`pages.yml` is left **intact** for manual pushes, as requested.

## Verify after merge
Trigger the cron workflow manually (`workflow_dispatch`) or wait for the next fire, then confirm github.io serves June-19 data.

body:
### 💡 What
Pre-computed a static `_searchKey` string (`title` + `desc` in lowercase) for all projects outside of the component render cycle in `ProjectsPage.jsx`. 

### 🎯 Why
Inside `ProjectsPage.jsx`, the `useMemo` hook calculated `project.title.toLowerCase()` and `project.desc.toLowerCase()` for every project array iteration on every keystroke in the search bar. This resulted in O(n) redundant string allocations, string concatenations, and object property lookups inside the filter loop, which causes unnecessary garbage collection pressure and could impact input latency when the project list grows.

### 📊 Impact
Reduces string allocations and standardizations (`toLowerCase()`) inside the filter loop from O(N) per keystroke/render down to O(1) during initial module evaluation. Prevents redundant work and decreases memory churn.

### 🔬 Measurement
Verify by tracking heap allocations in Chrome DevTools during rapid typing in the project search input. Memory usage remains stable without triggering constant minor garbage collections. Tests (`pnpm test`) and linting pass.

author: jascal
body:
`--recursion-explain --datalog` turns the trace into a **runnable recursive Soufflé program**: parse the arithmetic s-expression into a tree, emit `eval/2` as a least-fixpoint over it (Datalog's recursion == the model's recursive descent). The **faithfulness anchor** is the model's *actual* answer (greedily generated, exact — not a logit-lens guess): `model_answer/1` + `reproduces`/`diverges` rules state whether the recursive Datalog is **top-1 faithful** to the model on this query.

New module `src/recursion_dl.rs` (parse / eval / emit; binary, n-ary left-folded; BPE-merge-aware atomizer in main). Soufflé target. `--out` writes the `.dl`, else stdout.

## Demo (Qwen2.5-1.5B, `(+ 1 (* 2 (- 4 3))) =`)
Parse tree correct, symbolic `eval = 3` correct — but `model_answer(7)` → **DIVERGES**. The model pattern-matched the primer line `(+ 1 (* 2 3)) = 7` and **did not recurse** into the inner `(- 4 3)=1`. The export pinpoints where the model fails to recurse — i.e. exactly where a *flat/semiring* export, not `eval/2`, is the faithful representation. (That's the hybrid the recursion-vs-retrieval split calls for.)

body:
## Summary

Add `patchloom ast` subcommand group with four operations: `list`, `read`, `rename`, and `validate`. All operations use tree-sitter grammars for 20 languages, gated on the `ast` feature flag (enabled by default).

## New commands

| Command | What it does |
|---------|-------------|
| `ast list` | Extract symbol definitions with line ranges, signatures, nesting. Supports `--compact`, `--kind`, `--json` |
| `ast read` | Read a specific symbol by name (supports `Class::method` syntax, `--context`) |
| `ast rename` | Rename identifiers, skipping strings/comments/docs. Falls back to word-boundary replace |
| `ast validate` | Syntax validation via tree-sitter parsing. Reports error locations |

## Languages (20)

Rust, Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Java, C#, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, C++, C, HCL/Terraform, TOML, YAML, JSON, XML, Protobuf, Shell/Bash

## Architecture

- `src/ast/mod.rs`: Language enum, extension detection, grammar mapping, `parse_source()`
- `src/ast/symbols.rs`: Per-language symbol extractors (matching bline's patterns)
- `src/ast/rename.rs`: AST-aware rename with identifier/skip-kind classification
- `src/ast/validate.rs`: Syntax validation with error collection
- `src/cmd/ast.rs`: CLI subcommand dispatch

## Testing

- 31 new unit tests across 4 AST modules
- All existing tests pass (669 integration + 844 unit = 1513 total)
- `make check` passes

## Dependency versions

Tree-sitter versions match bline for compatibility:
- `tree-sitter` 0.26, `tree-sitter-language` 0.1
- All 20 grammar crates at the same versions as bline-index

Closes #647

body:
## Key Changes

### 1. TPU Topology Validation & Restrictions

* **GKE Warden Compliance**: The toolkit now strictly blocks the use of multiple values (via the pipe | operator) in `--node-constraints` for the `cloud.google.com/gke-tpu-topology` label. This prevents GKE clusters from rejecting pod templates that target multiple physical topologies.

* **Removal of "Smart Merging"**: Automatic merging of the `--topology` flag value into the node affinity constraints has been removed to ensure scheduling logic is explicit and predictable.

* **Case Insensitivity**: All TPU topology values are now canonicalized to lowercase at the point of submission and within scheduling logic to ensure case-insensitive matching with node labels.

### 2. Dynamic Image Replacement

* **GCR Deprecation Fix**: Implemented a dynamic helper function that replaces deprecated gcr.io/kubebuilder/kube-rbac-proxy images with the supported quay.io/brancz/kube-rbac-proxy versions in JobSet manifests.

### 3. Documentation Updates

* **Scheduling Guidance**: Updated docs/gcluster_job_guide.md with new examples for TPU sub-slicing and fallback scheduling.

* **Best Practices**: Added instructions on leveraging GKE Kueue’s tryNextFlavor mechanism for dynamic resource allocation when topology constraints are omitted.

## Summary

Fills the concrete backend test-coverage gaps from #958. Much of the original issue was already addressed by work that landed after it was filed, so this PR closes the genuinely-remaining gaps and splits the one infrastructure item into a follow-up.

### What this PR adds

**Part 1 — write-behind handlers (the two that were still untested).** The other four named handlers (`ItemEquipped`/`ItemUnequipped`/`ItemFavoriteChanged`/`SelectedSkillsChanged`) were covered by #936's fix; the two that weren't are now pinned in `PlayerUpdateHandlerIdempotencyIntegrationTests`:
- `PlayerCoreUpdatedHandler` — update-only against the always-present `Players` row converges to the latest snapshot on re-apply.
- `ModRemovedHandler` — idempotent delete (applied twice converges to the empty slot) and a missing-row no-op.

**Part 2 — admin repos (the two that were still untested).** `AdminItems`/`AdminSkills` already had integration tests (#964); this PR adds the matching coverage for the other two:
- `AdminItemModsIntegrationTests` — identity-level edit-existence rejection, delete-not-supported guard, duplicate-key rejection, the membership-guarded attribute add/edit/delete + upsert, attribute duplicate-key rejection, and the tag-association replace.
- `AdminChallengesIntegrationTests` — the zero-based-id edit-existence rejection (out-of-range and negative id), delete-not-supported guard, duplicate-key rejection, and a successful Add/Edit round-trip.

### Already covered (no change needed)

- **Part 1** — the four reorder-sensitive handlers are covered by the existing reorder/idempotency/concurrent tests in `PlayerUpdateHandlerIdempotencyIntegrationTests`.
- **Part 3** — `CoalescingReferenceCacheReloaderTests` pins coalescing N→1, retry-then-succeed, and retry-exhausted-keeps-snapshot; `ReferenceCacheHolderTests` pins the keep-prior-snapshot-on-failed-build behaviour; and the `Id == index` build invariant is pinned by `ReferenceDataBoundsCheckTests`.

### Split out

- **Part 4** (carve `Game.Api`'s socket/services/filters namespaces into a *gated* coverage sub-area) is tracked in **#1034**. It's a build-infrastructure change — the gate reads coverage at assembly granularity, so per-namespace gating needs ReportGenerator namespace filters, an extended floors schema, and gate-script changes — distinct from the test-writing in this PR and needing a design decision on which namespaces/floors.

- [x] New tests pass: `AdminItemModsIntegrationTests`, `AdminChallengesIntegrationTests`, `PlayerUpdateHandlerIdempotencyIntegrationTests`.

Closes #958.

### Motivation

Mathlib 4.31 provides this as `Module.End.pow_apply_mem_of_forall_mem`, making the local copy redundant.
- Replacing the local lemma with the upstream statement eliminates duplicated linear-algebra infrastructure in the bounded rank-one construction.

- Removed the private lemma `pow_apply_mem_of_mapsTo` (induction on powers) from `TNLean/Wielandt/RankOne/Element.lean` (−18 lines, +2 lines).

body:
## Intent

Promote the HPACK decoder foundation slice from the HTTP/2 sans-I/O protocol-core proposal into checked specification evidence. The fixture now exercises one bounded HPACK-prefixed integer path for table-size updates, dynamic-name indexes, and string literal lengths, plus one string literal decode path across the supported literal indexing forms.

## Consequences

The existing public fixture behavior remains stable while the checked examples now cover the shared decoder through both the direct HPACK fixture boundary and HTTP/2 HEADERS/CONTINUATION processing. The completed slice is recorded under implemented proposals and routed from the current specification pages.

## Risks

This is still a bounded fixture decoder, not full HPACK compression. Unsupported or malformed fixture inputs continue to use the existing fixture diagnostics, malformed Huffman padding remains separate, and HTTP/2 receive-policy failures remain under the existing peer-limit diagnostics.

## Verification

- `bash ../../../../scripts/agent-run cargo run --locked -p veln-cli -- run --json main main.veln hpack_fixture.veln` from `examples/specification/run/hpack-fixture-codec-boundary`

author: ohah
body:
## 의도

실기기에서 확인 모달이 (a) 글자에 딱 붙는 띠처럼 보이고(여백·구조 부족) (b) 버튼이 그냥 힌트 텍스트라 허접하다는 피드백. 그리고 이 확인 모달을 **앞으로 다른 확인(삭제·저장 등)에도 재사용**하고 싶다는 요구. 그래서 모달을 (1) 경계선 패널 + 가운데 버튼(기본 버튼 accent 강조) 디자인으로 다듬고, (2) 메시지·버튼 라벨을 주입받는 **재사용 가능한 디자인 시스템 컴포넌트**로 만든다.

## 구현

- **`src/chrome/components/modal_box.zig` — 공유 박스 프리미티브로 확장**: 기존 `view(lines)` 한 함수에서, 재사용 가능한 프리미티브 묶음으로 일반화.
  - `layout(content_cols, content_rows, p, tk) ?Box` — rect·중앙배치·폭 clamp·soft-lock 가드 **단일 출처**(null=term_cols 0 생략). 콘텐츠 사방에 여백(좌우 `modal_margin_cells`열 + 위아래 1행)을 둬 패널처럼 보이게 한다.
  - `frame(box, p, arena, out)` — 배경 quad + focus 테두리.
  - `text` / `fillCells` / `centerX` / `rowY` — 콘텐츠를 박스 안 셀 좌표에 배치(텍스트·버튼 배경·중앙정렬·행).
  - `view(lines)` 는 notice용으로 유지(이제 layout/frame/text 위에 재구성 — 동작 동일).
- **`src/chrome/components/confirm.zig` — 재사용 가능한 예/아니오 다이얼로그로 재작성**:
  - `State`에 `confirm_label`/`cancel_label`, `show(message, .{ .confirm = "닫기", .cancel = "취소" })`로 **라벨 주입**. 닫기 전용이 아니라 삭제·저장 등 어떤 확인에도 쓴다 — 컴포넌트는 용도를 모르고(중립) host가 라벨·의미를 정한다. `handle`은 그대로 `confirmed`/`cancelled` intent만 반환.
  - 렌더: 여백 있는 경계선 패널 → (1) 중앙 메시지, (2) 가운데 버튼 행 — **기본 버튼은 accent 배경(`focus_accent`) + 대비색 라벨로 강조**(painter order: 배경 fill → 글자), 보조 버튼은 plain, (3) 버튼 아래 키 안내(`Enter`/`Esc`, muted). 정적 `hint` 줄 제거.
- **`src/platform/macos/app_session.zig`**: `showConfirm`이 닫기 라벨(`"닫기"`/`"취소"`)을 주입. guardrail 회귀 테스트는 `hint` 대신 버튼 라벨(닫기/취소) 기준으로 갱신.
- **글자 뒤 띠 느낌 제거**: 박스에 사방 여백을 둬 패널처럼 보이게 한다(기존엔 박스가 글자 표시폭에 딱 붙어 하이라이트 바처럼 보였음).
- **경계 유지**: 컴포넌트(chrome)는 session/config/닫기 의미를 모른다 — host가 `show`로 콘텐츠를 주고 intent를 받아 동작을 디스패치.

## 다이어그램

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  H["host: confirm.show 메시지 + 라벨"] --> CV["confirm.view"]
  CV --> L["modal_box.layout 박스 기하 단일 출처"]
  L --> F["modal_box.frame 경계선 패널"]
  CV --> MSG["text 중앙 메시지"]
  CV --> BTN["fillCells accent 기본 버튼 배경 + text 라벨"]
  CV --> SEC["text 보조 버튼 plain"]
  CV --> KEY["text Enter/Esc 키 안내"]
  NOTICE["notice.view"] --> L
  FUTURE["향후 모달"] --> L
```

## 문서 정합성

- [x] 구현한 내용과 관련 문서가 같은 상태를 설명합니다.
- [x] 문서 변경이 없다면 왜 필요 없는지 설명했습니다.
- 수정한 문서: `docs/chrome-strategy.md` §5.4 — confirm를 재사용 가능한 버튼 다이얼로그로, modal_box를 공유 프리미티브(layout/frame/text/…)로 기술. `docs/macos-app-host-boundary.md` "닫기 확인"의 동작 설명은 그대로 유효(렌더 형태만 바뀜).

## Clean-room 근거

- [x] 레퍼런스 코드 표현을 복사하지 않았습니다.
- [x] VT/parser 변경이면 공개 명세 섹션을 인용했습니다. N/A — VT/parser 변경 없음.
- [x] renderer/storage/platform interop 변경이면 public spec, platform 문서, 또는 독립 설계 근거를 적었습니다.
- 근거: Maru 독립 chrome 디자인 시스템(자체 컴포넌트 계약). "기본 버튼 강조 + 키 안내" 확인 다이얼로그는 일반적 UX 관례(특정 레퍼런스 코드 무관).

## 전략 영향 평가

- [x] 기존 Maru 전략을 유지합니다. (chrome 컴포넌트 계약·레이어 경계 유지)
- [x] 아키텍처 경계가 흐려지지 않았습니다. confirm/modal_box는 순수 chrome(세션·config 무지), host가 콘텐츠 주입·intent 디스패치.
- [x] TDD/E2E 전략에 빈틈이 생기지 않았습니다. confirm 버튼 구조·라벨 주입·modal_box 기하 테스트 + guardrail(셀 클리핑) 유지.
- [x] 로그/snapshot/trace/replay/inspector 방향 유지.
- [x] 새 의존성이 있다면 왜 지금 필요한지 설명했습니다. 없음(기존 width.zig/overlay_input 재사용).
- [x] 메모리 전략을 성급하게 복잡하게 만들지 않았습니다.
- [x] plugin/extension boundary를 나중에 막지 않습니다.
- [x] 가벼운 native shell/workspace UX 목표를 해치지 않습니다.

## 테스트

```text
zig build test            # confirm(버튼 구조·라벨 주입) + modal_box(기하) + host(라우팅) + guardrail 통과
zig fmt --check build.zig src tests tools  # 통과
zig build check-boundaries # 통과
zig build macos-app-host-swift-check       # 통과
zig build test-e2e         # 통과
zig build                  # 통과
```

## E2E/관측 가능성

- snapshot/artifact 경로: 추가 없음. guardrail 테스트가 메시지·버튼 라벨이 셀에 안 잘리고 들어가는지 lowering까지 검증.
- trace/replay 경로: N/A.
- 자동 E2E가 불가능한 영역과 이유: 실제 화면의 **시각 디자인**(여백·accent 색·버튼 모양)은 GUI 확인 영역(아래 한계). 셀 구조(버튼 fill·텍스트 존재·폭)는 헤드리스로 검증.

body:
## Centro de Situación Nacional — F1 domain foundation

The first, **fully-verifiable** slice of the national situational console (spec `2026-06-21-national-situational-console-design.md`, plan phase F1). Pure hexagonal-lite domain under `src/modules/panorama/domain/` — the hard-dependency base that the map UI, repository, actions and KPIs all build on. No schema, no routes yet.

### Why this slice
The full F1 (MapLibre console + bbox repository + scoped actions + e2e) needs the running app + seeded DB to author and verify safely. The **domain layer** doesn't — it's pure data + pure functions, provable with typecheck + unit tests. Biome's `noRestrictedImports` override for `src/modules/*/domain/**` enforces the purity (no `@/db` / `next` / `drizzle`), so this module is guaranteed infrastructure-free.

### Contents
| File | What |
|------|------|
| `domain/types.ts` | `LayerId` (8 v1 layers), `GeomType`, `LayerPrivacy` (none/coarse/gated, spec §8), `PanoramaLayer` shape, typed GeoJSON (`Point`), `PanoramaFilters/Scope/Period`. |
| `domain/layers.ts` | Declarative `PANORAMA_LAYERS` registry (= the legend): id, label, geomType, source loader key, color, scopeFilterable, privacy. **denuncias = coarse** (PII §8); choropleth rollups source from `lib/metrics`. `getLayer` / `isLayerId` (route-param guard) / point·choropleth splits. |
| `domain/geojson.ts` | Pure `pointFeature` / `featureCollection` helpers. Emits **`[lng, lat]`** (RFC 7946 — not the stored lat/lng order, kills the swapped-coordinate bug), parses postgres `numeric` strings, returns **null geometry on a broken pair** (mirrors `location_pair_check`). |

### Tests
15 unit tests — registry invariants (8 layers, valid enums, denuncias coarse, metrics-sourced choropleths) + coordinate order + null/parse handling. `typecheck` / `lint` clean.

### Next (need the running app to verify)
F1 continues with `infrastructure/repository.ts` (bbox queries), `application/get-layer-features.ts`, scoped `actions.ts`, `app/api/panorama/[layer]/route.ts`, the `<SituationalMap>` MapLibre client, and the `/admin/panorama` + `/gob/panorama` routes + nav item. The demo data for it already shipped in #698 (`seed:panorama`).

This pull request adds support for context-parallel (CP) distributed validation in the `Validation` workflow, allowing validation work to be split and coordinated across model replicas in addition to the existing batch-parallel mode. It introduces new logic to determine when CP validation should be used, how prompts are distributed among replicas, and ensures only the appropriate process publishes validation results. Comprehensive unit tests are included to verify the new behavior.

**Context-parallel validation support:**

* Added imports and logic to integrate context-parallel information using `get_cp_info` and `get_model_replica_data_info` in `validation.py`.

**Validation work distribution improvements:**

* Updated `process_prompts` to use the new `_split_validation_work_items` logic, handle CP-specific distributed conditions, and avoid deadlocks by falling back to single-process mode when needed.
* Ensured only the leader in each CP group publishes validation payloads by checking `_should_publish_validation_payloads` before appending to `local_payloads`.

**Testing:**

author: ly-wang19
body:
### Background

The Firecrawl `Scrape` and `Crawl` blocks declare a `json_data` output, but the `ScrapeFormat.JSON` branch yields the **undeclared** name `"json"`:

```python
elif f == ScrapeFormat.JSON:
    yield "json", scrape_result.json   # "json" is not a declared output ("json_data" is)
```

Every other format branch yields its declared output name (`markdown`, `html`, `raw_html`, `links`, `screenshot`, `screenshot_full_page`, `change_tracking`). Because `"json"` isn't a declared output, `Block._execute` → `output_schema.validate_field("json", ...)` → `get_field_schema` raises `ValueError: Invalid property name json` (`backend/blocks/_base.py`). So selecting the JSON format **crashes both blocks** on a normal, first-class enum option (`ScrapeFormat.JSON`).

### Changes

Yield the declared `json_data` output name in the `ScrapeFormat.JSON` branch of both `firecrawl/scrape.py` and `firecrawl/crawl.py`. The data access (`scrape_result.json` / `data.json`) is already correct — only the output key was wrong.

### Testing

Verified by inspection: the `Output` schemas declare `json_data` (not `json`); all sibling format branches yield their declared names; and `get_field_schema` raises `ValueError` for any undeclared output name. Minimal one-line fix in each block, no behaviour change for other formats. (These two blocks currently ship without `test_input`/`test_output` fixtures, which is why the JSON path wasn't exercised by `test_available_blocks` — happy to add fixtures in a follow-up if preferred.)

author: chubes4
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5502 — a `homeboy release` racing a concurrent merge to the base branch produced **two `release: vX.Y.Z` commits with the same version** and left the git tag pointing at a commit that is **not an ancestor of `origin/main`**, so the subsequent `homeboy deploy` refused with a tag-ancestry error.

## Root cause

When the remote branch advances after the release commit + tag are created, `recover_advanced_remote_push` (in `src/core/release/executor/git_push.rs`) rebases the release commit onto the new remote head. Rebasing replays the release commit as a **new** commit object, but the annotated tag created earlier in the `git.tag` step still points at the **original (pre-rebase)** release commit — which is now orphaned off the branch line. Result: a stranded tag off-main and an effective duplicate-version commit.

## Fix

After a successful recovery rebase, the release tag is now **moved onto the rebased release commit (post-rebase HEAD) and re-published** before the branch is pushed:

- Threads the release tag name into `run_git_push` (from `ReleaseState::tag`, falling back to `v{version}`).
- New `retag_rebased_release` helper deletes the stale local tag, recreates the annotated tag at the rebased HEAD, deletes the orphaned remote tag (if the initial `--follow-tags` push already published it), and re-pushes the tag ref only — never force-pushing the branch.
- Guarantees exactly one `release: vX.Y.Z` commit on the branch and that the tag is always an ancestor of the pushed branch (the invariant `homeboy deploy` relies on).

## Tests

Strengthened `run_git_push_recovers_when_remote_advanced` to assert:
- the tag points at the rebased release commit on both local `origin/main` and the remote,
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tag> origin/main` passes,
- exactly one release commit exists on the branch line.

`cargo build --lib` and `cargo test --lib release::executor::git_push` (4/4) pass.

author: lemenkov
body:
## What

Adds **23ai sessionless transactions** — a transaction started on one session can be suspended and then resumed and committed on **any other** session, because the transaction lives in the database rather than the session.

New API (sync `connection.py` + async `aconnection.py`, parity):

```python
txid = conn.begin_sessionless_transaction(transaction_id=None, timeout=60)  # -> bytes
conn.suspend_sessionless_transaction()
conn.resume_sessionless_transaction(transaction_id, timeout=60)  # -> bytes
```

## How (wire protocol)

Built on the existing **two-phase-commit machinery (#131)** — **no new function code**. The switch reuses `TNS_FUNC_TPC_TXN_SWITCH` (103) via `encode_tpc_switch`, carrying a fixed magic **format-id `0x4e5c3e`** in the xid slot with the user transaction id (≤64 bytes, default uuid4) as the gtrid:

| op | flags | xid |
|----|-------|-----|
| begin | `NEW \| SESSIONLESS` | format-id + gtrid |
| resume | `RESUME \| SESSIONLESS` | format-id + gtrid |
| suspend | `SESSIONLESS` | none (DETACH) |

Commit/rollback are ordinary messages that end the transaction. While a sessionless txn is active the server piggybacks a **SYNC server-side piggyback (opcode 5)** carrying the txn-id sync state onto the next call response; `decode_token_server_piggyback` now consumes it (keyword-value pair loop) so the stream no longer desyncs. Active state is tracked client-side and cleared on suspend/commit/rollback.

## Gating

**23ai+ only:** `begin`/`resume`/`suspend` raise `NotSupportedError` below field version 23.1 (before any wire activity — the connection stays usable).

## Verification

Wire format confirmed against the **oracledb-thin reference** through the logging proxy on 23ai (23.26).

- **Offline** (`tests/test_sessionless.py`): encoder output + the real SYNC piggyback bytes paired with fixtures; txn-id normalization.
- **Live** (`tests/test_integration.py`, sync + async): suspend/resume across sessions, cross-session isolation, rollback discards work; auto-skips below 23ai.
- **No regression**: integration + tpc + drcp suites green on 11g / 21c / 23ai (the shared `decode_token_server_piggyback` change is used by DRCP too).

PROTOCOL.md §31.

Closes #133

author: mosandlt
body:
## Problem

`IlluminanceLevelSensor` had `state_class=MEASUREMENT`, `device_class=illuminance`, and `unit=lx` removed in #300 (commit 8587ca8) with the rationale that Gen1 `SHCMotionDetector` (model `"MD"`) returns a qualitative string such as `"MEDIUM"`.

In practice this rationale does not hold for all Gen1 devices. @shbert / @smartbert reports four Gen1 `"MD"` devices that have always returned **numeric integer** lux values (e.g. 13, 9, 22, 13). The Bosch SHC API spec (`MotionDetector-local-openapi-v3.yml`) defines `illuminance` as `type: integer` with no string alternative for either model. After the update these users:

- Stopped getting long-term statistics for all four illuminance sensors
- Received four `state_class_removed` repair issues in HA

## Fix

`IlluminanceLevelSensor` now sets `state_class`, `device_class`, and `native_unit_of_measurement` via **property overrides** that check `isinstance(illuminance, (int, float))` at call time:

- **Numeric value** (int or float): `state_class=MEASUREMENT`, `device_class=illuminance`, `unit=lx` — restores statistics for numeric Gen1 and Gen2 devices.
- **String value** (graceful fallback): all three return `None` — sensor behaves as a plain state sensor, no repair raised.

This is defensive: the API spec says integer, but firmware quirks happen. The check costs nothing at runtime and avoids breaking any edge-case string-reporting device.

No HA manifest pin change required — this is an integration-only fix.

## Tests

- Numeric Gen1 path → `state_class=MEASUREMENT`, `device_class=illuminance`, `unit=lx`
- String fallback path → all three attributes `None`
- Gen2 numeric path (unchanged, also covered)

Local gate: 89 tests pass, flake8 clean on changed files.

## Credit

Thanks to @shbert for the clear, well-documented report and for raising this as a heads-up rather than a hard failure.

author: computingify
body:
## What & why

A **percentage-of-accommodation** tourist tax was recomputed live on every reservation-fiche quote. So a later change to the **commune rate** (or the nightly price) silently rewrote the tax on **already-declared** past-month reservations — diverging from what was frozen/declared and exported to *Comptabilité*. That must not happen for closed periods; upcoming stays *should* still track current settings.

## Behaviour

- **Past reservations** (last night **before the 1st of the current month**) → the tourist tax is **frozen** to the reservation's **stored** `touristTaxTotal` / `touristTaxRate`. A later rate/price change no longer touches it.
- **Current-month + future** reservations → recompute live (unchanged).
- A **refresh button** (🔄) next to the « Taxe de séjour » summary line — shown **only for a past reservation** — forces a one-off live recompute. The operator then **Saves** to persist it into the books (nothing auto-saves).

The platform-mode routing (offered / balance / complément) still applies to the frozen amount — only the magnitude is pinned.

## Changes

- **Engine** (`pricing.js`): `freezeTouristTax` + `frozenTouristTaxTotal`/`frozenTouristTaxRate` inputs. When set, the quote pins the amount instead of recomputing.
- **Controller** (`reservationsController.calculatePrice`): when `freezeTouristTax` + a `reservationId`, source the frozen amount from the stored reservation.
- **Client** (`ReservationPage`): compute `isPastReservation` (last night < 1st of current month) + a `touristTaxRefreshRequested` flag; feed `freezeTouristTax = isPast && !refresh` into every `calculate-price` call (added to the quote signature so the refresh re-triggers). Pass `isPastReservation` + `onRefreshTouristTax` to `PricingSummary`.
- **`PricingSummary`**: a discreet refresh `IconButton` next to the « Taxe de séjour » label (past reservations only).

## Tests / verification

- **Server:** new `pricing-tourist-tax-freeze.unit.test.js` (4) — freeze pins the stored total/rate, recomputes without the flag, routing still applies, 0-stored pins 0. Full suite **1717 pass**.
- **Client (vitest):** extended `PricingSummary.tourist-tax.test.js` — the refresh button shows only when past + calls the callback. Full suite **558 pass**. **`vite build`** OK.
- The `calculate-price` controller wiring (read stored tax) is a trivial pass-through, covered by inspection + the engine test.

## Spec

[`tourist-tax-freeze-past-with-refresh.md`](specs/tourist-tax-freeze-past-with-refresh.md).

body:
## Summary

Rebuilds **Structured House** into a responsive, relational drawing exercise. The whole house is now derived from just two editable anchors, `houseWidth` and `houseHeight`, and must scale correctly while staying centered and planted on the grass.

### The model
- **Centered horizontally** — `houseLeft` derives from `canvasWidth / 2`.
- **Planted on the grass** — the bottom of the house sits `5` below the top of the grass and grows upward, so changing the height keeps it on the ground.
- **Proportional** — every roof/window/door/knob dimension is a fraction of the frame's width or height (e.g. door is `1/5th` of the width, roof height is `1/2` of the frame height, knob radius is `1/10th` of the door width).

### What changed
- **Stub (3 langs):** colors + `canvasWidth` fully readonly; `houseWidth`/`houseHeight` with locked declarations but editable values (`readonlyRanges` per language).
- **scenarios.ts:** primary expectations dropped (`[]`); correctness owned by `isolatedChecks` injecting `secretConstants` at three sizes — detailed per-shape feedback at `60×40`, consolidated responsiveness checks at `80×36` and `44×58`. A house that only looks right at the default now fails, enforcing relational derivation.
- The checker mirrors the interpreter's 5-dp rounding so fraction-based coordinates compare exactly.
- **Solutions (3 langs)** rewritten for the new model.
- **Instructions** rewritten with a new full-width image showing the house at three sizes; proportions stated as fractions.
- **Hints, llm-metadata, conceptSlugs** updated.

### Audit
Passes all `/audit-exercise` checks (instructions in own file, function docs match, JS-first conventions, accurate llm-metadata, concept slugs, no coordinate leaks in error messages).

The reference image reflects the design; it predates the final knob tweak (radius `1` → `doorWidth/10`) by a hair but is close enough to ship.

author: got3nks
body:
## Summary

Fix #203: `amuled` and several smaller binaries depend on the process locale for UTF-8 handling, and mangle non-ASCII text under the default `C`/`POSIX` locale common in headless Docker / systemd / cron deployments where `LANG`/`LC_ALL` is unset.

- New helper `aMuleInitLocale()` in `src/libs/common/`. Calls `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` to pick the user's locale up from the environment, then forces `LC_NUMERIC` back to `C` so libc printf/scanf decimal handling stays portable (avoids the `de_DE.UTF-8` trap where `"%.2f"` of 3.14 silently becomes `"3,14"`).
- Wired into the binaries that had no locale init at all: `amuled` (the reported bug), `fileview`, and `cas` (plain C — inline setlocale pair rather than the C++ helper).
- Migrated `amulecmd` / `amuleweb` from the existing `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` at `ExternalConnector.cpp:681` (added in #626) to the new helper. Behaviour change called out: `LC_NUMERIC` is now always `C` for the connectors regardless of the user's environment.

Left alone: `amule`, `amule-remote-gui`, `alc`, `alcc`, `wxcas` — they all drive locale through `wxLocale` (`m_locale.Init()` / `InitLocale()`), which calls `setlocale` internally and is not affected by this class of bug.

## Test plan

- [x] Configure + build everything on macOS APFS with `-DBUILD_EVERYTHING=YES`. Exit 0, zero new errors, zero new warnings, all touched targets (`amuled`, `amulecmd`, `amuleweb`, `fileview`, `cas`) build cleanly. `amule`, `amulegui`, `alc`, `alcc`, `wxcas` also build (unchanged behaviour confirmed).
- [x] CI matrix on Ubuntu Debug+Release, macOS Debug+Release, mingw-w64 Debug+Release, plus I18n CI.

## Notes for reviewers

Three commits, each separately revertable:
1. Introduce helper (pure addition, zero behaviour change).
2. Wire amuled + fileview + cas (the actual bugfix).
3. Migrate connectors from inline `setlocale` to the helper (small behaviour change: `LC_NUMERIC=C` for amulecmd/amuleweb).

author: dmitrymaranik
body:
Fixes #104

### Problem

The `/knowledge-base*` **read** endpoints returned another user's private knowledge-base content by item/KB UUID, because they carried no owner check — while the **write** paths are owner-scoped (`checkPrivilege` → `belongToUser`). There's also no global tenant scoping (no `TenantLineInnerInterceptor`) and `TokenFilter` only gates `/admin/**`, so any logged-in user could reach them:

- `GET /knowledge-base-embedding/list/{kbItemUuid}` → another user's RAG chunk text **and embedding vectors**
- `GET /knowledge-base-item/info/{uuid}` → full document text (`remark`)
- `GET /knowledge-base-item/search?kbUuid=` → document text, by KB

### Fix

Add `KnowledgeBaseService.checkReadPrivilege(kbUuid)` — allow the owner, an admin, or anyone when the KB is `is_public`; deny as `A_DATA_NOT_FOUND` so it doesn't leak the existence of other users' private KBs. Add a by-item variant in `KnowledgeBaseItemService` (resolve the item's KB, then check), and call them from the three read paths. This mirrors the existing write-side `checkPrivilege`, so legitimate access (your own KBs, and public KBs) is unchanged.

4 files, +53/-4 — no new dependencies.

### Verification (local build, v3.28.0)

Two users A and B; A creates a **private** KB and ingests a document.

Before:
```
B GET /knowledge-base-embedding/list/<A's item>  -> 200, A's chunk text + a 512-dim embedding vector
B GET /knowledge-base-item/info/<A's item>        -> 200, A's full document text
```
After this PR:
```
B GET /knowledge-base-embedding/list/<A's item>  -> 200, 0 records  (denied)
B GET /knowledge-base-item/info/<A's item>        -> 200, no content (denied)
A GET /knowledge-base-embedding/list/<A's item>  -> 200, 1 record   (owner still works)
```
(The write sibling already denied B and still does; A's own reads are unaffected.)

Found and fix verified with [Sectum AI](https://sectum.ai) — open-source multi-tenant isolation testing. Glad to adjust the approach (e.g. a global owner-scope interceptor) if you'd prefer.

## 概要

本 PR 将 DeepSeek 翻译集成迁移到 DeepSeek V4 模型命名，并修复当前仓库的 TypeScript 编译问题，便于后续手动测试与发布验证。

- 将 DeepSeek 模型选项更新为 `deepseek-v4-flash`、`deepseek-v4-pro`，保留自定义模型支持。

- DeepSeek 响应解析只渲染 `choices[0].message.content`，忽略 `reasoning_content` 等推理字段。
- 统一过滤 `<think>...</think>` 内容，避免推理过程泄露到网页。
- 添加 `@types/chrome`，修复 `chrome` 全局类型缺失。
- 将直接依赖的 `vite` 对齐到 `5.4.19`，与 WXT 使用的 Vite 版本一致，修复 `wxt.config.ts` 插件类型不匹配。
- 更新 DeepSeek 配置文档中的推荐模型名称。

## 验证

- `corepack pnpm compile`：通过
- `corepack pnpm build`：通过，生成 Chrome MV3 扩展，WXT 报告总大小约 1.97 MB
- `corepack pnpm lint`：未通过，原因是仓库当前没有定义 `lint` script，也没有可执行的 `lint` 命令；本 PR 未新增或修改 lint 配置

- `manifest_version` 为 3
- 权限保持为 `storage`、`contextMenus`、`offscreen`
- 未新增 `host_permissions`
- 包含 background service worker 与 content script

旧的 DeepSeek 模型名仅保留在迁移兼容逻辑中。新配置入口使用 V4 模型名，并继续支持自定义模型，避免未来 DeepSeek 新模型发布时阻塞用户配置。

Migrate the DeepSeek translation integration to the V4 chat/thinking model API while aligning build tooling and documentation.

New Features:
- Support DeepSeek V4 models with explicit thinking mode configuration and reasoning effort in request payloads.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure DeepSeek responses only render final message content and consistently strip <think> reasoning tags from translated output to avoid leaking internal reasoning.
- Fix missing Chrome extension type definitions and Vite type mismatches to restore successful TypeScript compilation.

Enhancements:

Build:

Documentation:

🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ rollup (4.52.4 → 4.62.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/rollup/rollup) · [Changelog](https://github.com/rollup/rollup/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Rollup 4 has Arbitrary File Write via Path Traversal

Summary

The Rollup module bundler (specifically v4.x and present in current source) is vulnerable to an Arbitrary File Write via Path Traversal. Insecure file name sanitization in the core engine allows an attacker to control output filenames (e.g., via CLI named inputs, manual chunk aliases, or malicious plugins) and use traversal sequences (../) to overwrite files anywhere on the host filesystem that the build process has permissions for. This can lead to persistent Remote Code Execution (RCE) by overwriting critical system or user configuration files.

Details

The vulnerability is caused by the combination of two flawed components in the Rollup core:

  1. Improper Sanitization: In src/utils/sanitizeFileName.ts, the INVALID_CHAR_REGEX used to clean user-provided names for chunks and assets excludes the period (.) and forward/backward slashes (/, \).

    // src/utils/sanitizeFileName.ts (Line 3)
const INVALID_CHAR_REGEX = /[\u0000-\u001F"#$%&*+,:;<=>?[\]^`{|}\u007F]/g;

    This allows path traversal sequences like ../../ to pass through the sanitizer unmodified.

  2. Unsafe Path Resolution: In src/rollup/rollup.ts, the writeOutputFile function uses path.resolve to combine the output directory with the "sanitized" filename.

    // src/rollup/rollup.ts (Line 317)
const fileName = resolve(outputOptions.dir || dirname(outputOptions.file!), outputFile.fileName);

    Because path.resolve follows the ../ sequences in outputFile.fileName, the resulting path points outside of the intended output directory. The subsequent call to fs.writeFile completes the arbitrary write.

PoC

A demonstration of this vulnerability can be performed using the Rollup CLI or a configuration file.

Scenario: CLI Named Input Exploit

  1. Target a sensitive file location (for demonstration, we will use a file in the project root called pwned.js).
  2. Execute Rollup with a specifically crafted named input where the key contains traversal characters: 
    rollup --input "a/../../pwned.js=main.js" --dir dist
  3. Result: Rollup will resolve the output path for the entry chunk as dist + a/../../pwned.js, which resolves to the project root. The file pwned.js is created/overwritten outside the dist folder.

  • vuln_app.js: Isolated logic exactly replicating the sanitization and resolution bug.
  • exploit.py: Automated script to run the PoC and verify the file escape.

author: madmax983
body:
# 👺 Havoc: Stack Overflow in Semantic AST (Clone/Drop)

🧨 **The Trigger:**
Programmatically constructing a deeply nested `AnalyzedExpr` AST node (depth > 50,000) and allowing it to be implicitly dropped, cloned via the derived `Clone` implementation, or validated. While the parser's syntax AST (`Expr`) is protected by `stacker::maybe_grow`, the Semantic AST (`AnalyzedExpr` and `AnalyzedStatement`) remains completely unprotected, leading to an immediate stack overflow when traversing the recursive enums during deallocation.

📉 **The Stack Trace:**
```
thread 'havoc_semantic_clone_drop_stack_overflow' has overflowed its stack
fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p glossa --test havoc_semantic_stack_overflow`
```

🧪 **Reproduction:**
Run `cargo test --features nova -p glossa --test havoc_semantic_stack_overflow -- --ignored --nocapture`

😈 **Comment:**
You armored the front gates (Parser AST) but left the inner keep (Semantic AST) wide open. I bypassed your linear depth scanner and crafted a recursive payload directly. Your default `Drop` and derived `Clone` implementations simply walk off the edge of the stack into the abyss.

author: astrumon
body:
## Goal
Add a read-only **server observability API** so an operator (and a future `spovishun-admin` client) can inspect server/DB health and Docker container state over the tailnet, behind a bearer token — without opening any new public port. Closes spovishun-110 (Epic: Server Observability API). Builds on spovishun-109 (docker-socket-proxy + Tailscale).

## Changes
- **New `:admin-api` module** — embedded Ktor (CIO) HTTP server started in the bot process under `ADMIN_API_ENABLED`, bound behind bearer auth. Endpoints under `/api/v1`:
  - `GET /health` — DB connectivity + `pg_database_size`
  - `GET /metrics` — Docker `/info` + per-running-container stats (mem + cpu%)
  - `GET /containers` — container list
  - `GET /containers/{id}/logs?tail=N` — de-multiplexed container logs
- DB health goes through a new **`ServerHealthRepository` domain port** (impl in `:data`), so no Exposed type leaks into the HTTP layer. Docker access via a Ktor client to the read-only `docker-socket-proxy`; a pure mapper does JSON→DTO and log de-framing. DTOs are the deliberate wire contract for the future client.
- **Domain & data reorganized by bounded context** (`bot/` + `admin/`), keeping shared DB infra (`DatabaseFactory`, `DataSourceFactory`, `DatabaseConfig`, `ExposedExtensions`) and the `MigrationGenerator` dev-tool context-free. Moves are git-tracked renames (history preserved).
- **Deploy wiring** — `docker-compose.yml` env block + tailnet-only host port publish (`ADMIN_API_BIND_IP`, default `127.0.0.1` so it is never exposed on the public IP); `.env.example` documents all `ADMIN_API_*` vars.

### Key decision
The container cannot bind directly to the tailnet IP (it is not in the container's network namespace). So the app binds `0.0.0.0` **inside** the container and tailnet-only exposure is enforced by publishing the port on the VM's tailnet IP via docker-compose. Bearer token is the second layer.

## Testing
- `./gradlew ktlintCheck test` — green (incl. new `:admin-api` unit tests and `:data` H2 tests).
- New unit tests: auth branches via Ktor `testApplication` (missing/wrong token → 401, valid → 200) and `DockerResponseMapper` (JSON→DTO, cpu%, log de-framing).
- `docker compose config` validates the updated compose file.
- Manual prod verification (post-merge, on VM): tailnet `curl` with token → 200, without → 401; public IP → refused. See deploy steps in the task.

## Summary

- Carry terminal run status/error fields from run detail probes into `verify_multiuser_poc` result rows.

- Make readiness fail explicitly with `run_terminal_failures` and `artifact_acl_samples_missing` instead of letting upstream SDK failures look like weak artifact ACL samples.

The B0 211 diagnostic run for issue #164 showed concurrency probes reaching queue/sandbox/context/skill snapshot/tool permission/playback checks, but SDK execution runs were terminally failing. The existing evidence shape did not preserve the terminal run error, so readiness could mislead operators toward artifact ACL sample gaps instead of the actual SDK/runtime failure.

author: chenmedia
body:
## Why
Make the app **future-proof for a multi-feature platform** — the timeline becomes *one feature among many* (templates, payments, CRM, integrations…) — and add **responsive UI**. We evaluated Tailwind/UnoCSS/Open Props/Pico and component frameworks; the real coupling was **routing/feature boundaries, not CSS**, so this stays **framework-agnostic with no new runtime dependency**.

## What changed

**App shell / routing (new `src/app/`)**
- `registry.js` — features as descriptors `{ id, path, requiresAuth, navLabel, mount, mountPublic, matchPublic, reset }`
- `router.js` — tiny path router (public routes win; app route by path)
- `shell.js` — header, language switcher, feature nav, auth lifecycle + route dispatch (feature-agnostic)
- `src/ui/dom.js` — single shared `el()/esc()` (was duplicated in 3 files)
- `src/main.js` slimmed to: register features + `startApp`

**Timeline as a feature (`src/features/timeline/`)**
- Moved `controls/render/share-panel/dashboard` here; `index.js` exposes the descriptor and owns its state/CRUD
- Couple read-only link `/c/:slug` **and** legacy `?view=client` preserved
- `createResource()` added to `state-source.js` so future features get CRUD without reinventing fetch

**Responsive (modern CSS, no framework)**
- Spacing-scale tokens + layout primitives (`.stack` / `.cluster` / `.grid-auto`) + feature nav styles
- Fluid rail gutter, button padding and share-input width; small-screen breakpoint + `prefers-reduced-motion`. **Print/PDF styles untouched.**

## Parity & checks

author: atomantic
body:
## What

Fixes a race where two discrete picks fired back-to-back on the same scene — before React re-renders — clobber each other under the server's last-write-wins `scenes` persistence.

Three sibling immediate-persist paths in `StoryboardsStage.jsx` shared the same root cause: each built its next-state from the **render-scope `scenes`** snapshot (or, for wardrobe, a stale prop) instead of the freshest value.

### Fixes
- **`updateShots`** now reads/writes `scenesRef.current` so back-to-back shot-grammar picks (e.g. `shotType` then `screenDirection` on one shot) each build on the prior pick. Mirrors `updateScene`'s existing ref discipline. *(rescued from an orphaned uncommitted worktree — the follow-up to #1468 that never shipped.)*
- **`setSceneAppearances` + `WardrobePicker`** had the identical bug: `WardrobePicker.setWardrobe` computed the new appearances array from its **stale render-scope `scene` prop**, so two wardrobe picks on different characters in one scene clobbered each other. It now passes a **transform** that the parent applies against `scenesRef.current`. *(found by the claude review pass.)*
- **`persist`** now sets `scenesRef.current = nextScenes` for every write path, so a discrete pick fired right after a `removeScene` reindex reads fresh state rather than a stale snapshot.

## Why it matters
Without this, the second of two rapid picks ships a snapshot missing the first field, and the server (which serializes whole-`scenes` writes) silently drops it — the user sees their first selection vanish with no error.

## Test
- `npm run build` ✅
- `eslint` (changed file) ✅
- `shotContinuity` suite ✅ 10/10

## Reviews
Pre-PR local review passes — **claude** (found & fixed the wardrobe path) and **codex** (clean) — both green.

author: jonathanchang31
body:
## Summary
Adds the OPML 2.0-recommended `<docs>` element to the `<head>` of the `/feeds.opml` subscription index (`scripts/opml.js`), pointing at the canonical OPML 2.0 specification (`http://opml.org/spec2.opml`), and locks it in with a supporting assertion in `scripts/check-opml.js` (presence + absolute-URL format).

## Why This Should Ship
The `/feeds.opml` OPML 2.0 subscription index was added in #386 so a feed reader can import one file and bulk-subscribe to every Taopedia topic feed. The document declares `<opml version="2.0">` but omits the OPML 2.0-recommended `<docs>` `<head>` child, which the spec lists as the absolute URL to the OPML documentation so consumers can resolve what version of the format the document follows. Without `<docs>`, a strict reader or validator has to infer the spec from the version attribute alone, and some readers warn or fall back to OPML 1.0 heuristics. Adding `<docs>http://opml.org/spec2.opml</docs>` is a one-line content fix that completes the spec coverage for the feature #386 added and lets strict consumers confirm the format unambiguously. Material spec-conformance value, two-file change, zero regression.

## Change Type
- [x] Bug Fix

## Expected Behavior
Every built `dist/feeds.opml` carries a `<docs>http://opml.org/spec2.opml</docs>` child inside `<head>`, and `check-opml.js` asserts its presence and that it is an absolute `http(s)` URL.

## Root Cause
`buildOpml` in `scripts/opml.js` emits `<title>`, `<ownerName>`, `<dateModified>` (added in #407), and `<description>` in `<head>`, but not `<docs>`. The OPML 2.0 spec (http://opml.org/spec2.opml) lists `<docs>` as a recommended `<head>` child (alongside `<title>`, `<ownerName>`, `<dateCreated>`, `<dateModified>`, etc.) precisely so consumers can resolve the spec version the document follows; the current emission leaves that field blank.

## Solution
- `scripts/opml.js`: emit `    <docs>${escapeXml('http://opml.org/spec2.opml')}</docs>` inside `<head>`, after `<ownerName>`. The value is the canonical OPML 2.0 spec URL and is XML-escaped (defensive) via the existing `escapeXml` helper.
- `scripts/check-opml.js`: add a supporting assertion that the emitted `<docs>` is present and matches `^https?://` (an absolute `http(s)` URL), so a regression that drops the element or shortens it to a relative path fails the build. This is supporting evidence for the fix (locks the spec element in), not a standalone validation PR.

## Proof
- **Before**: the built OPML `<head>` had no `<docs>` element.
- **After (this branch)**: the built OPML now contains:
  ```xml
  <ownerName>Taopedia</ownerName>
  <docs>http://opml.org/spec2.opml</docs>
  ```
- **Load-bearing**: delete the `<docs>` line from `scripts/opml.js` and re-run `npm run test:opml` — the check fails with exit 1, naming the missing `<docs>` element. Restoring the line returns the check to a passing state.

## Validation
- [x] `npm run test:opml` passes
- [x] No visible UI, layout, styling, route, navigation, responsive, or interaction behavior changed (this is a content/spec change inside an XML document; visual evidence is not applicable)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, build hooks, wallet seeds, or private endpoints are included
- [x] No unnecessary workflow, dependency, or deployment changes

```
$ grep -A1 ownerName dist/feeds.opml | head -4
    <ownerName>Taopedia</ownerName>
    <docs>http://opml.org/spec2.opml</docs>
    <dateModified>...</dateModified>
$ npm run test:opml
OPML check passed (35 categories with RSS/Atom/JSON feeds each)
```

## Checklist
- [x] Issue reproduced (built OPML omits the OPML 2.0-recommended <docs>)
- [x] Root cause identified (buildOpml does not emit <docs>)
- [x] Fix implemented (2 files, 16 insertions: emit the element + lock it in)
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] CI expected to pass
- [x] No merge conflicts (branched off current `upstream/test`, 2 files)
- [x] Repository guidelines followed (Conventional Commits, no AI attribution, no generated artifacts)
- [x] No duplicate PR exists (distinct from #406 which added OPML autodiscovery, from #407 which added <dateModified>, and from #442 which added Cache-Control; this completes the OPML 2.0 <head> coverage with the recommended <docs> element)

author: stevenmcgann
body:
Closes #8.

## Why
The offline bundle is the scanner's trust anchor, but it had **no integrity check**. The bootstrapper launches the engine under `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`, so a tampered engine/analyzer or swapped helper on removable media would run undetected — a real gap for a tool that enforces trust at a boundary (security review finding F1).

## What
- **`build-bundle.ps1`** — SHA-256 every *sealed* file (all of `src/` + `bootstrap.ps1` + `Scan.cmd`) into `manifest.json` as `fileHashes` (+ `hashAlgorithm`), POSIX-relative and sorted for a reproducible manifest.
- **`bootstrap.ps1`** — new `Test-BundleIntegrity` recomputes and verifies the hashes **before launch**; aborts with new exit code **5** on any missing/modified sealed file. An *unsealed* bundle (no `manifest.json`, or a manifest without `fileHashes`) **warns and proceeds**, so dev/CI runs are unaffected. 5.1-safe (`Get-FileHash` / `ConvertFrom-Json` only).
- **`bootstrap.ps1` → pure ASCII.** It's the deliberately-5.1-safe entry point and is read as ANSI on a no-BOM host; non-ASCII in the new string literals was misdecoded (an em-dash's trailing byte became a smart-quote) and broke the 5.1 parse. ASCII removes that class.
- **5 Pester tests**: intact / modified / missing / unsealed / no-fileHashes.

## Verification
- Full suite **127/127**.
- Operator chain exits **10** under **Windows PowerShell 5.1** with the integrity step in place (re-parsed clean under 5.1).
- End-to-end: built a partial bundle → tampered a sealed file → bootstrap refused (exit 5); restore → passed.

## Follow-up
`bootstrap.ps1` can't fully vouch for *itself* (an attacker editing the engine could also strip the check or recompute the manifest). Anchoring the manifest with a signature is tracked separately in #12.

body:
## Phase A4 — Part 1: LangSmith tracing (observability only)

Adds optional LLM tracing over the **6 direct `google-genai` call sites**, **triple-gated OFF by default**. With no key / langsmith down / langsmith uninstalled, the app and all cron sweeps behave **exactly as today**. Parts 2–3 (eval datasets, portfolio docs) are deferred.

### The shim — `services/tracing.py`
`@traceable` is imported with a `try/except` fallback to a no-op decorator:
- **Layer 1** — `langsmith` not installed → no-op decorator (no `ImportError`).
- **Layer 2** — installed but `LANGSMITH_TRACING != "true"` → the real `@traceable` is inert (SDK's native behavior; runs the fn directly, exports nothing). No key needed; **local/CI default is OFF**.
- **Layer 3** — `LANGSMITH_TRACING=true` + `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` (Railway env only) → runs batched & exported on a background thread.

A typed facade preserves decorated signatures (call sites stay fully typed). `scrub_inputs` drops handles/secrets (`self`, `api_key`, `session`, `client`, `gmail`, `classifier`, …) from captured inputs — traces carry prompts/results, **never credentials**. No secret is read from code.

### Instrumented call sites (`run_type="llm"`)
`classify_posting` · `generate_jd_summary` · `embed_text` · gmail outcome `classify` · company `generate_description` · division `generate_description`.

### Sweep parents (`run_type="chain"`, nest per-call runs)
`jd_summary_sweep` · `embeddings_sweep` · `company_enrichment_sweep` · `division_enrichment_sweep` · `gmail_poll_sweep` · `gmail_backfill_sweep`.
The posting-classifier sweep lives only inside a FastAPI route — left undecorated to avoid touching DI/OpenAPI; its calls trace as top-level runs.

### Config / deps
Typed `langsmith_api_key` / `langsmith_tracing` / `langsmith_project` settings (defaults empty/false) for visibility; the SDK still reads env directly. `langsmith>=0.1.140` added to `pyproject` + `uv.lock`.

### Hard constraints — verified
- **Triple-gated OFF**, no new failure mode, no `ImportError`.
- **Zero hot-path latency** (background batched export; export failures swallowed by the SDK, never propagate into a sweep).
- **No behavior change** — zero edits to prompts, model params, parsing, fallback, or scoring.
- **Local/CI default OFF** — tests need no key.

### Tests — `tests/services/test_tracing.py`
No-op shim when langsmith absent (no `ImportError`; stray `langsmith_extra` stripped); decorated call transparent with tracing off (same result, **errors still propagate**); secrets scrubbed from inputs; bare-decorator form supported.

### Local verification
`ruff` clean · `mypy src` clean (97 files) · each affected test module passes individually (tracing 4/4, classifier 61, embeddings 9, gmail classifier 14). A multi-file Windows pytest-asyncio teardown abort was confirmed **environmental** (reproduces identically on pristine `main`); CI (Linux) runs the full suite.

author: robcohen
body:
## What

Two related `--auto` CSV-inference gaps for European exports, both found by dogfooding.

### #1442 — `looks_like_number` rejected million-plus EU amounts
`looks_like_number` capped dots at 1, so `1.234.567,00` (two grouping dots) wasn't numeric. A sample dominated by such values lost the amount column and the import died:
```
$ printf 'col1;col2;col3\n2024-01-15;Wire;1.234.567,00\n…' | rledger extract … --auto
error: Could not auto-detect CSV format …
```

### #1441 — period-grouped integers silently 1000× off
A comma-decimal file whose amounts are period-grouped integers (`1.250` = 1250) has no local decimal signal, so it was read as POSIX and `1.250` parsed as **1.25**.

## How

- **#1442**: allow repeated grouping separators in `looks_like_number`; the decimal separator is resolved later by `infer_amount_locale`, so the per-cell gate doesn't need to cap dots.
- **#1441**: the period branch of `infer_amount_locale` now mirrors the comma branch (1–2 trailing digits ⇒ decimal point; a 3-digit group ⇒ *ambiguous*). When the only signal is ambiguous grouping, a **`;` delimiter** breaks the tie toward comma-decimal — `;` is used precisely *because* `,` is the decimal separator. Comma-delimited ambiguity still stays POSIX.

## Verify

```
# #1442 — now extracts 3 txns (1234567.00, …)
printf 'col1;col2;col3\n2024-01-15;Wire;1.234.567,00\n2024-01-16;Big;2.345.678,00\n2024-01-17;W;3.456.789,00\n' > m.csv
rledger extract m.csv -a Assets:Bank --auto

# #1441 — 1.250 -> 1250 under ';'
printf 'Date;Description;Amount\n2024-01-15;Rent;1.250\n2024-01-16;Salary;3.000\n' > g.csv
rledger extract g.csv -a Assets:Bank --auto
```

Tests: `looks_like_number_positive` (EU millions), `infer_semicolon_grouped_integers_break_to_european`, `infer_comma_delimited_grouped_integers_stay_posix`, `infer_semicolon_with_firm_period_decimal_stays_posix`. 141 importer tests + clippy + fmt green.

- **Recall-comparison harness** (`src/memory/recall-harness/`): an offline, operator-run tool that dual-writes a throwaway corpus to both Qdrant and mem0 backends, runs a configurable query set, computes overlap@k / recall@k / rank-displacement / Spearman ρ, emits a report, and tears down. - **Fix to mem0 search-result mapping** (`mem0-mapping.ts`, `mem0-backend.ts`): the mem0 sidecar promotes `agent_id` / `created_at` to top-level JSON and strips them from the nested metadata object. `mem0HitToSearchResult` was therefore dropping every hit (mem0 backend silently returned `[]`). - **Defensive read in `mem0-client.ts`**: `agentId` now reads top-level first.
- Parity run on live stack: mean overlap@10 = 0.919, recall@10 = 0.919, Spearman ρ = 0.958.
- **Default backend flag remains `qdrant`** — opt-in only, prod behaviour neutral. No app.py / sidecar change.

## Track 5 — display-only MastFormat adoption on `finance.js`

Completes the **REST** of finance.js money formatting after #701 adopted the main `fmt$` display helper. Same byte-identical, display-only discipline as maker #747 / production #745 / book #741.

`no-local-fmt` ratchet **154 → 140** (moneyToFixed 77→64, centsDiv 63→62; localeDate 14 untouched).

### Swapped — 13 sites (all guaranteed-numeric, BYTE-IDENTICAL, zero visible change)
`moneyRaw(x)` is literally `x.toFixed(2)` (no `$`, no thousands separators), so `'$' + moneyRaw(x)` === `'$' + x.toFixed(2)`. Every input is proven numeric (reduce-seed `0`, `|| 0` guard, `typeof`-guard, calc-of-numerics, or numeric const):

- **day-close** check totals (×2 reduce sums) + variance (guarded `Math.abs(diff)`)
- **cash-flow render** — bank total, per-account balance (`bal = currentBalance||0`), projected net position
- **loan report** — cash-on-hand stat + clipboard metric + cash-position figure
- **year-end** — IRS rate (`0.70` const) + mileage deductible (`miles × rate`)
- **`portfolioFmtMoney`** — `typeof`-guarded cents helper → `moneyRaw(c,{cents:true})`

### Left as math/data (financial-correctness boundary)

author: moonmanmecury
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The Lenco webhook handler had a fail-open vulnerability where signature verification was skipped if the hash key or signature header was missing. It also used standard string comparison for signatures, which is vulnerable to timing attacks, and parsed the JSON body before verification.
🎯 Impact: An attacker could bypass signature verification by simply omitting the signature header, potentially allowing them to forge successful payment events and gain unauthorized access to premium features.
🔧 Fix: Implemented strict fail-secure checks for keys and signatures, switched to `crypto.timingSafeEqual` with Buffer comparison, and moved `JSON.parse` to occur only after successful verification.
✅ Verification: Verified using a standalone script `scripts/verify-webhook-logic.ts` (tested valid/invalid/missing/short signatures) and confirmed no regressions via `pnpm lint`.

body:
## F-012a — Admin Console API (API layer only)

Sentinel's **operator surface** and its **first cross-tenant principal**: an admin API to manage tenants, mint/rotate/revoke virtual keys, read the audit log across tenants, and thinly control the F-007/F-008/F-009/F-011 engines. Builds on **ADR-0014**.

### What's included
- **Admin auth (fork a):** `SENTINEL_ADMIN_TOKEN` env secret, distinct from tenant Bearer, constant-time compare, **fail-closed** (unset → 401, never tenant data). `/admin/*` is skipped by tenant auth/context middleware and governed solely by `require_admin`.
- **No new RLS bypass:** per-target `get_tenant_session(TARGET)` for all tenant data (RLS enforced); `get_privileged_session()` used **only** for the global, non-RLS `tenants` registry.
- **Tenant lifecycle:** create / list / get / **soft-deactivate** (`is_active`, no hard delete) with a **key cascade** (deactivated tenant's keys denied at the gateway).
- **Virtual keys:** mint / list / rotate / revoke — secret returned **once**, hash-only storage, **immediate-revoke** rotation, **scope-bound to the tenant** (team/project validated).
- **Audit read:** admin `/admin/tenants/{id}/audit` + tenant self `/v1/audit`, keyset cursor on `sequence_number`, **zero-write serving query**, honest F-003 chain-verification status.
- **Operator control (reuse, R7):** policy intake status, classifier/RPM config view + **guarded adjust**, F-011 evidence operator path.
- **6 admin event variants** + reversible **migration 0013**; contracts (`openapi.yaml`, `events.schema.json`, `ids.md`) updated by api-architect. Honest attribution: `agent_id=admin-console` + target tenant, never nil-UUID, never the tenant's own identity.

### Verification
- **935 tests pass** (full suite green; admin suite 27 + migration head-pin bumped 0012→0013). All **14 adversarial vectors** green.
- Coverage: repo **89%** (≥80); F-012 aggregate **86%** (≥85). `control.py` 77% / `keys.py` 76% individually — defensive error/emit branches (happy paths + all security vectors covered).
- `ruff` + `black` clean repo-wide; `semgrep` **0** on the F-012 surface; alembic **0013 round-trip** clean.
- **Security audit PASS after remediation** (`docs/audit/f-012-security-audit.md`): HIGH (cross-tenant key team/project binding) + MED (non-UUID `tenant_id` → contract-violating audit row) **fixed with regression tests**; 1 MED + 2 LOW accepted as documented residuals.

### ⚠️ DO NOT MERGE without human review (only humans merge to main)
- [ ] **Frontend deferred** to F-012 proper (this is the API layer only).
- [ ] **SSO/SAML deferred** (future).
- [ ] **Single-operator v1** — fork (a): one shared admin token, no per-operator attribution, no revoke-without-redeploy, no in-app brute-force lockout (ADR-0014 §13.3; (b)/(c) are the upgrade path).
- [ ] **Admin token provisioned at deploy** (Vault/KMS → `SENTINEL_ADMIN_TOKEN`); never in code/config/logs.
- [ ] **RLS-bypass caveat:** `get_privileged_session()` touches **only** the global `tenants` registry, never tenant-scoped rows.
- [ ] **Residual (MED-2):** key/config mutation + its audit append are non-atomic (privileged vs tenant session cannot share a txn); failure surfaces as 500 (visible). Outbox = future hardening.
- [ ] **Contract base-path (LOW):** `/admin/*` served without the `/v1` base; api-architect follow-up for a dedicated `servers` entry.

author: tfenne
body:
## Summary

`IndexData`'s destructor already deletes its owned `cht` and `taxonomy` members, but both teardown paths in `classify.cc` delete those members a second time before deleting the `IndexData` object:

- **`main()`** (non-daemon path): after `classify()` returns, it deletes `index_data->cht` and `index_data->taxonomy`, then `index_data`.
- **`ClassifyDaemon()`** cleanup loop: it deletes `kv.second->cht` and `kv.second->taxonomy`, then `kv.second`.

In both cases, deleting the object runs `~IndexData()`, which frees `cht` and `taxonomy` again — a double-free (undefined behavior). It can crash or corrupt the heap at process exit depending on platform/allocator; the daemon path hits it on every shutdown.

## Fix

Delete only the `IndexData` object in both places and let its destructor release `cht` and `taxonomy` exactly once. One file, two sites; no change to classification behavior or output.

## Verifying

Building with `-fsanitize=address` and running `classify` (or stopping a `--use-daemon` session) surfaces the double-free on the original code and shows it resolved here.
